News.title: Moment council meeting erupts into chaos after Reform councillor ‘farts into mic’ during rival’s speech
News.content:
Next

THIS IS the moment a council meeting descends into chaos after a Reform councillor “farted” at a rival.

The Blackburn and Darwen Council Forum meeting on Thursday (October 1) was supposed to update the councillors and members of the local authority on the past month.



But whilst Councillor Terri Mahmood, Independent/4 BwD member for Blackburn Central, was speaking when a loud “fart” sound can be heard ripping from a microphone from across the room.

Several other nearby councillors can be seen in hysterics after hearing the loud flatulence, which has since been dubbed “fartgate”.



Fingers were later pointed at Reform UK Blackburn South East councillor Andy Mahon, who came to the meeting dressed in a distinctive leopard print fedora and matching tie paired with a safari jacket.

Moments after the incident, the meeting – which was set to last four hours – paused for a break.

The gathering threatened to descend into chaos as independent councillor Tasleem Fazal felt the need to challenge Cllr Mahon’s behaviour.

He said: “Whilst I have got the opportunity to speak, I would like to address something from earlier.



“Whilst I understand we are all elected members in here and we do get passionate members of public, I don’t mind that because they are most likely not going to be back here next month or the month after.

“What I do take issue with is the decorum in here of late and especially this evening.

“I think as elected members we all respect one another’s positions we are all here on merit, but I think we have to respect one another.



“I take issue with some of the noise levels and other silly comments being made when other members are speaking.

“But I will tell you what I really take issue with someone lifting their arse cheeks to the microphone in my direction blowing their arse out like we are at school.

“I am really worried about being hit by shrapnel if he gets in wrong and I really really think all the leaders of each party need to have a discussion outside of here and get this in order.



“Because I am not going to come here meeting after meeting putting up with childish behaviour it is not on.”

Cllr Mahon can be seen rasing his arm requesting to speak.

Cllr Fazal goes onto say: “If someone has a problem or a digestive problem there is a bathroom at the end of the corridor, but we have got to be managing this kind of stuff.”

Cllr Mahon and Blackburn and Darwen Council have been approached for comment.

News.title: Brit warning as gangs turn Costa del Sol into ‘ticking time bomb’ with horror shootings… so is it REALLY safe to visit?
News.content:
COSTA DEL HELL Brit warning as gangs turn Costa del Sol into ‘ticking time bomb’ with horror shootings… so is it REALLY safe to visit?







Next

DAYLIGHT gangland killings on the sun-soaked Costa del Sol have turned the tourist hotspot into a “ticking time bomb”.

A botched murder plot at a packed marina restaurant in Malaga left the terrace blood-stained and diners reeling from shock.



More than 14 million Brits flock to Spain’s sun-kissed southern shore every year – but may be forced to question whether their getaway is worth the potential nightmare.

Mafia murders are not unfamiliar on the holiday mecca, with organised crime being a fixture along the Costa del Sol for decades.



But a sudden spike has forced the government to deploy extra police forces to the south.

Cops now face the task of clamping down on escalating turf wars between international drug cartels before the violence spirals out of control.



Chief Superintendent Roberto Rodríguez said: “We have a ticking time bomb right under our feet.”

What’s behind the spate of public executions is not clear, but one expert speculates that younger, more reckless criminals could be responsible.

Professor Michele Riccardi, an organised crime expert and Deputy Director of Transcrime, warned that the old guard may be exploiting this new breed of felon.

He told The Sun: “There is a big debate in Europe at the moment about an increasing exploitation of young people for criminal purposes.



“Certain organisations are exploiting these young people [because] they know they are risk takers.

“These inexperienced people could be more violent simply because they are not able to do a proper cost-benefit analysis as well as senior people.”

He suggested that youngsters have been inspired by violence online.



In the most recent shooting, thugs donning face coverings charged towards the terrace of the Lounge Bar Plaza in Malaga.

They opened fire, shooting their target twice in the face before fleeing on foot.

Ümit Yalçın, 47, was holidaying in Malaga and enjoying a dinner out with a friend and two women.

The Turkish national, known as as “Gypsy Ümit”, is a prominent leader of the notorious football ultra supporter base of club Fenerbahçe SK.

He was rushed to hospital for surgery where he is still fighting for his life.



“It’s a miracle he survived,” a source close to the investigation told local outlet Sur.

Experts warn it could be a sign of escalating turf wars.

Professor Riccardi said: “Either the price [for] which they are fighting for is so high that it justifies the use of such risky violence or the nature of the actors involved have changed.”



Days before the terrace attack, two men were injured in a shooting that investigators believe stemmed from a botched drug rip off.

Police found bullet holes piercing the front door of the house in Alhaurín el Grande, near Marbella.

And two days before that, a construction worker was shot multiple times in the leg and back as he sat on a bench in broad daylight in Barcenillas, an area in Malaga.

Malaga resident Nacho, 20, had no criminal records or gang ties and was mistaken for a rival hitman.

He was able to crawl to a supermarket after being shot, where witnesses heard him shout: “They are killing me, they have shot me twice.”



Customers in the store attempted to help Nacho, but his injuries were critical and he later died in hospital.

The public nature of these shootings will spark fears among tourists hoping to enjoy a relaxing meal out.

These types of shootings have also raised the stakes for police.



Professor Riccardi said: “If shootings themselves raise alerts for law enforcement, shootings in the public against mistakenly identified people are even more problematic.

“These are actually triggers which usually [prompt] law enforcement to do massive raids and prevent the problem.”

He explained that there is a new era of “macro mafias” tied to the Netherlands, Belgium and Sweden, and these groups a “more violent than others”.

The three perpetrators arrested in connection with Nacho’s killing were all Swedish nationals.

They are believed to have lived nearby and stalked the innocent bystander before launching their attack.



In a fourth incident this month, a woman was gunned down in broad daylight on the outskirts of Malaga and left her children fearing for their lives.

She was shot squarely in the chest in what police fear was another gangland attack.

Recent outbreaks of criminal violence in the Costa del Sol expose how a huge network of international organised crime groups operate out of the area’s picturesque towns.

Police have reported a notable influx of illegal weapons in the region, with foreign conflicts sourcing the supply.

In contrast to drug smuggling operations, active war zones have left large arsenals in circulation.



These weapons reach to European black market and can move freely across borders within the Schengen Area.

Holidaymakers may look to safer shores for their next trip away, unless these problems can be solved.

But Professor Riccardi argued that the current spike in violence could lead to a natural downward curve – meaning it’s safe for tourists to visit.

Too much police attention might urge gang leaders to cool off.

He said: “These things have already very much raised the attention of law enforcement. To a certain extent, this may disappear.”



Although tourists might think twice about visiting Costa del Sol in light of the shootings, Professor Riccardi warned that the violence is fairly limited.

He said: “We are talking about a couple of shootings in two months’ time.

“It’s hard to predict, but if you see the likelihood of other severe accidents, it’s higher than being shot by a criminal gang fight.”

News.title: The landlocked waterway arming Putin and Iran’s terror axis beyond Nato’s reach
News.content:
Next

BEYOND Nato’s reach, Iran and Russia are forging a new terrifying axis in a landlocked waterway.

With its southern ports severed by Donald Trump‘s blockade in the Strait of Hormuz, Tehran is turning north to a “war zone” shipping artery rocked by airstrikes and a naval arms race for survival.



The Caspian Sea, a key maritime corridor sitting between Iran and Russia, is both keeping the mullah regime alive and helping Putin launch strikes on Ukraine.

Bordering just five countries, it is the only large-scale transport route linking Moscow and Tehran that bypasses US intervention – due to a ban on foreign military deployments inside it.



International security expert Luke Coffey told the Sun: “The Iranians have been using the Caspian Sea as a way to trade more with Russia and receive assistance… but also to provide energy exports to circumvent international sanctions.

“Munitions, artillery shells, spare parts – these are items that have been sent north to Russia.”



Security analyst Dakota Irvin said the waterway had become a “key lifeline” for the regime.

He told The Sun: “Russia is reportedly sending technology and weapons to Iran, and Iran has also helped Russia with drones and ballistic missiles… it’s really kind of a key lifeline.”



Putin is exploiting the waterway to fuel his war in Ukraine.

To the chokepoint’s northwest lies the Volga-Don canal – a shipping route connecting the Caspian Sea to the Sea of Azov.

Russian vessels carrying military equipment have used the narrow stretch to get arms closer to the Black Sea on Ukraine’s south coast.



The Caspian, which also borders Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan and Azerbaijan, has allowed Iran to trade key imports and exports such as food, essential supplies and oil.

Before the outbreak of war on February 28, the Strait of Hormuz handled 80 per cent of all Iranian trade.

But as of today, the US has achieved a near-total blockade of the regime’s southern ports.



More than 30 per cent of Iran’s imports now transit through the Caspian Sea, according to Tehran.

Coffey said: “They’ve been doing this a lot in recent weeks. What is new is the rate at which they are doing it.”

Increased trade in the Caspian Sea helps both regimes “resupply, rearm, and trade energy” as part of a larger effort to undermine the interests of the West, he added.

Irvin said: “The war isolated Iran from the rest of the world, and Russia is its only remaining key ally.

“The Caspian has emerged as this gateway for them as a back door for illicit trade including weapons and drones.”



Aside from food items like sunflower oil or animal feed, reports say Russia is also sending drone components and explosives to Iran through the sea.

The Kremlin has been helping Iran develop advanced supersonic cruise missiles “in one of the most significant known transfers of strategic military technology from Moscow to Tehran,” the Financial Times reported.

The relationship goes both ways – with Iran reportedly giving Putin drone and missile parts for his war in Ukraine to strike civilians and frontline targets.

Tehran’s imports and exports have not only been suffocated through their southern ports – but also their land and air routes.

Huge queues have been reported near Iran’s borders while cargo flights have been delayed as the US does everything it can to pile pressure on the regime’s neighbours.



Waiting times for trucks to cross the border between the town of Gürbulak in Turkey and Iran have increased fourfold compared to before the war, transport authorities say.

These factors have all pushed Tehran into a corner, with the regime relying on the Caspian Sea, the world’s biggest inland body of water, to keep itself afloat.

Despite a ban on foreign military presences in the Caspian, Ukraine has taken measures into its own hands to slow the flow of Iranian drones destined for the frontline.

In August, Ukraine confirmed it had struck and sunk a ship transporting Moscow-bound Shahed drone components.

Following the blitz – the first direct link between the wars in Iran and Ukraine – Tehran threatened to hit back.



The declarations sparked fears of World War Three as the regime vowed revenge.

Ukraine has also been hit by cruise missiles launched by Russian warships from the Caspian Sea.

Meanwhile, Kyiv has struck Russian off-shore oil fields and dozens of Putin’s warships in the waterway.

Strikes on Tehran’s ships in the maritime flashpoint were also launched by Tel Aviv just weeks after the outbreak of the US-Israeli war with Iran.

“The balance of naval power in the Caspian, it is definitely shifting because of what Ukraine, but also what Israel has done to the Russian and the Iranian fleets respectively,” Coffey added.



“Israel and Ukraine have expanded these two separate wars into one sort of conjoined conflict meeting in the Caspian Sea.”

Irvin said this increasing activity showed the waterway was becoming a “zone of war”.

“The Caspian is now almost a zone of war, which is complicating some of the shipping networks between Russia and Iran,” he said.

To ensure frictionless trade between both regimes amid the threat of strikes, Moscow and Tehran have been repeatedly turning off automatic identification system (AIS) signals according to maritime data, a method known as “dark activity”.

This under-the-radar technique makes it harder for the West to understand the true extent of the deepening bond between the two nations.



The Caspian has now become a symbol of the growing Axis of Evil alliance against the West.

Coffey said: “The Iranian and Russian cooperation, in addition to how China aligns with this and also North Korea, shows that there is an emerging axis against Western interests.”

He highlighted one example of this located just north of the Caspian Sea – the Russian Yelabuga factory that builds drones designed by Iran with parts from China and constructed by workers from North Korea.

But it has also sparked an urgent “naval arms race” between countries bordering the Caspian – due to the increased pressure to keep trade open.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Irvin said: “You’re seeing this increasing militarisation, and that puts a lot of the other countries that are ostensibly neutral in these conflicts, Turkmenistan, Kazakhstan, and Azerbaijan in a really difficult spot.



“We’re actually starting to see the emergence of a naval arms race in the Caspian as the Kazakhs, Azeris, and Turkmen acquire new assets, commission new ships as part of a general militarisation.”

News.title: I defend sex mad female paedo teachers – they all have one thing in common… and this is why they feel untouchable
News.content:
Next

THEY have become faces of depravity – abusing their positions of trust to prey upon pupils and disgrace the teaching profession.

Inspiring disgust and horror among parents across Britain, the likes of Kandice Barber, Rebecca Joynes and Bronwen James have had their sickening crimes splashed across the news, but what is it like to have to defend paedophile teachers like them – and what are their lives like in women’s prisons?



Solicitor Marcus Johnstone – who has represented at least 30 paedo teachers in the last five years – says it can be jarring listening to clients’ explanations who will almost always “try to justify” their actions.

He said he’s heard many “pathetic excuses” as to why a teacher has felt the need to communicate with a child, adding: “It’s quite sad to listen to.”

He told The Sun: “By the time we deal with them, they are quite desperate to avoid any problems – not only are they facing prison but they’ll never teach again.



“There have been many arguments… and sometimes the rationale is disturbing.”

Most of such clients are men, and many have even been found to have committed further offences, including downloading indecent images.

He said, worryingly, their victims maybe even convinced they’re actually in love and refuse to co-operate with the prosecution – sometimes even contacting their abusers after they’ve been caught and even sending them love notes.

The lawyer, MD of PCD Solicitors, said, conversely, the female teachers he’s represented have generally exclusively been accused of targeting teenage boys – telling him “there’s nothing wrong with it” when the victim is 16 or 17.

Mr Johnstone continued: “Of course, in many other scenarios, by law that is the case – but not when they’re in a position of trust.



“Their attitude is very much, ‘I’ve not done anything wrong’. They just often won’t accept it.”

Mr Johnstone, who has worked across almost all prisons in the UK, said, interestingly, paedo female teachers’ crimes are more tolerated in prison where there is no segregation for sex offenders.

He said: “Female sex offenders are very few and far between – it’s uncommon but when it happens, especially involving a teacher, often it makes the press.



“They’re usually quite young, at the earlier part of their teaching career, in their 20s.

“Maybe because they’ve got more of an affinity to older pupils… Not to condone their actions.”

He went on to say: “There seems to be a theme running through this with the females, they do tend to have very specific mental health issues, their cognitive skills are lacking.

“They’re just not recognising the problems that they’re getting into and why it’s illegal.

“For various reasons they seem to be attracted to certain pupils that they’re teaching and they think it’s fine.”



Mr Johnstone said the cases can become more complex when dealing with teenage boys as the victims, including in one circumstance it was found another male pupil found out about an affair with a school pal and tried to blackmail the female teacher.

“Sometimes, I suppose it’s easy to lose sight of things in that sense,” he added.

“There’s lots of scenarios that need to be clarified in such cases.”



Asked if, like many of the men, police also find indecent images on their devices, he said: “That’s not the case with women, strangely – it seems that there’s virtually no cases with females involved with indecent images of children.

“It’s just not a thing usually.”

Mr Johnstone explained one such case saw the prosecution arguing that his female client had known the victim since they were around 10, and had clearly groomed them from a young age.

“She would say ‘no, I’m caring for my pupils and giving them help and support’ – but there’s always going to be a line to be drawn,” the lawyer said.

“If somebody is looking after a child or taking them presents – is that necessarily grooming?



“Some might argue yes.

“Clearly it oversteps the mark if the teacher has other intentions and takes it further.”

Mr Johnstone went on to say, from his experience, the victims are usually “particularly disadvantaged”, perhaps coming from a “poor or disruptive family”, and not used to getting so much positive attention from adults.



What’s more, Mr Johnstone said: “I know the issues in prison and how they’re dealt with.”

He explained that it is “interesting” how male and female jails differ, including in their views of child sex offenders.

In women’s prisons there are no sex offender wings like in the men’s, which helps keep such lags protected from the rest of the general population.

Asked if female prisoners show the same hostility to sex offenders, he said: “You don’t tend to find that with women because there are so few female sex offenders.

“There just wouldn’t be enough to fill one of the wings. So they tend to mix with the normal prison estate.”



He said prison officers will often keep careful eye on women sex offenders, to see if it’s known amongst the rest of the inmates why they’re in prison, to monitor any potential trouble.

“Unless it’s been reported in the press, it wouldn’t be known,” he said.

“And unless they choose to tell their fellow prisoners, it shouldn’t get known.



“Clearly, a female who, for example, harms a baby, a young child, then if that’s made known, they’re going to be open to abuse and need special protections.”

Britain's paedo teachers Gary Day-Davies — Salford, 2026: Teacher jailed for 15 years for rape, sexual assault by penetration and sexual touching of a pupil. The offences occurred between 2006 and 2009; Greater Manchester Police said some abuse occurred at school and some at his home after he invited the pupil there for extra tuition. Edward Waller — Southampton, 2026: Former history teacher at St Anne’s School, jailed for six years. The CPS said he groomed a vulnerable 16–17-year-old pupil between 2004 and 2006, initially giving her extra attention before calls/messages became sexual and he eventually had sex with her. Emily Drury — Lincolnshire, 2026: Former teacher, 26, jailed for four years and six months after pleading guilty to five sexual-activity offences involving a teenage male pupil. She had offered to tutor him for his GCSEs and the sexual behaviour occurred while she was acting as his private tutor. Syed Shahreear Ahmed — Essex/London, 2025: Former maths teacher, 36, sentenced to 15 years’ imprisonment with a five-year extended period after convictions for 21 offences including grooming, rape, sexual activity with a child and indecent-image offences. This one is slightly different from the clean “teacher grooms own pupil” pattern: the CPS says he used social media to target numerous girls and young women while employed as a secondary-school teacher. Craig Smith — South Lanarkshire, 2025: Former drama teacher who admitted sexually abusing three female pupils. He initially contacted one pupil ostensibly because he was concerned about her panic attacks; messages became explicit and he later engaged in sexual contact with her at school. He also abused another pupil on school grounds. Rebecca Joynes — Greater Manchester, 2024: Maths teacher, 30, jailed for six-and-a-half years after being convicted of six counts of sexual activity with children. She groomed two male pupils from the age of 15; remarkably, she began a sexual relationship with the second while on police bail for offences involving the first, and later had a child with him. Russell Tillson — Tonbridge, Kent, 2023: Former senior teacher at Tonbridge School, jailed for five years and eight months for indecent assaults on two pupils. The offending stretched back decades. In one incident he offered a boy an enhanced university reference and suggested it could be achieved through what he called “unconventional methods.” Carole Ann White — Scotland, 2022: Teacher jailed for three years after being convicted of sexual offences against two boys. Police Scotland specifically described her as being in a position of trust when she committed the offences. Steven Bould — Derbyshire/Staffordshire, sentenced 2021: Maths teacher jailed for 33 months after admitting nine offences of intentionally sexually touching underage girls. Seven offences occurred while he worked at Pingle Academy and another two while at Nether Stowe School. Aimee Jones — Darlington, 2021: Teacher jailed for eight months after admitting four sexual offences involving a female pupil aged between 13 and 17 during the relevant period. She was subsequently banned from teaching indefinitely. Kandice Barber — Buckinghamshire, 2021: Married mother-of-three and cover supervisor/form tutor at Princes Risborough School, jailed for six years and two months after being convicted of sexual offences against a 15-year-old male pupil. Barber began communicating with the boy in 2018 and the exchanges became sexual; she sent him topless images and a sexual video before arranging to meet him in a secluded field, where they had sex. The sentencing judge found she had groomed the boy and later used threats and manipulation in an attempt to prevent disclosure. She was also made subject to an indefinite sexual harm prevention order and was prohibited from teaching indefinitely in 2024. Reports revealed that while she was incarcerated at an open women’s prison, Barber met and began a relationship with Jay Delaney, a convicted fraudster

He added: “Women are generally not as violent as men.”

Mr Johnstone said, from what he’s seen of female lock-ups, if a female teacher of say 25 has had a relationship with a 17-year-old pupil: “I don’t think that would cause any major problems even if it was made known inside prison.

“So it does depend on the type of offence that’s being committed.”

For the men, it can be very different, with specially segregated wings for sex offenders – or in several cases in the UK, specific prisons for such inmates.



They will sometimes get asked if they wish to be segregated or housed with mainstream prisoners, Mr Johnstone explained.

“Some clients in the past will say, ‘no, I don’t want to be’.

“If you have, for example, a 25-year-old male who was seeing a 17-year-old girl, and it’s only an offence because he was her football teacher or in another position of trust, then he may feel he’s done nothing wrong… he’ll take his chance in mainstream prison.

“Maybe he wouldn’t have that many problems, even if they knew about it, because of that scenario.”

Mr Johnstone said in some such cases as that, he’s seen it where the offender and victim “actually both want to be in that relationship together”.



In such circumstances, the pupil themself hasn’t actually complained – it might be a parent or a schoolfriend.

“Of course, the young girl believes that she’s truly and madly in love with the teacher,” he said.

“She doesn’t want to complain… I’ve had cases where because the complaint hasn’t come from the girl, it’s been a slight problem for the prosecution because she’s not a willing participant, she’s not a willing complainant.

“Sometimes the police will go to great odds to try to, with the witness liaison and the specially trained police officers, they will often spend quite some time with the child, really just helping her to understand what’s gone on, to process it, and to start to rationalise it, to think that this is more of a grooming thing, rather than she’s in love.

“And it takes on all sorts of legal complexities, because to what extent are the police then trying to create an offence, or to try and create a complainant?”



The victim is sometimes even keen to continue communication with messages and even letters to their abuser.

“There is often a complexity to these cases that maybe doesn’t always come across in the press,” said Mr Johnstone.

“I don’t know if there’s something that can be done at an earlier level, during teacher training to filter out future offenders – but, I suppose, how can it be known?”

News.title: Pilot who ‘attacked captain with AXE in terror attack’ is named & was ‘previously banned from flying over radical views’
News.content:
Next

THE FlyDubai pilot who allegedly stabbed his captain with an axe mid-air in an attempted terrorist attack has been named for the first time.

The co-pilot has been identified as Omani national Hamam al Hammami.



He reportedly attacked the captain with the cockpit’s crash axe and tried to take control of the plane with 182 people aboard, an official said.

Israeli officials claim the co-pilot was trying to crash the plane in a 9/11-style tragedy after steering the flydubai jet into a terrifying 700mph nosedive.



Investigations are ongoing ⁠to determine ​the circumstances of the ​incident, the motives ​and any related ⁠connections.

The co-pilot had previously been banned from flying by Oman over fears he had adopted extremist views, sources told AP.

Al-Hammami, who was born in the UAE to an Omani father and Syrian mother, was then hired by the UAE-based airline FlyDubai, the source said.

It was not immediately clear to what extent he was vetted when he was hired, they added.



A Gulf diplomat said investigations are working to establish whether he acted as a “lone wolf or has any connection with any extremist groups”.

On Thursday, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the suspect was believed to have undergone “Islamist radical indoctrination.”

A LinkedIn profile bearing the name Hamam al-Hammami said he worked at Oman Air for seven years, leaving in February 2025, before joining Royal Air Maroc in June 2025 and departing in January 2026.



The page does not mention of Flydubai, but sources confirmed the profile belongs to the attacker. The profile has since been deleted.

Two posts were made to the profile, both published in quick succession on Wednesday – nine hours after the incident.

It is unclear who published the posts or whether they were scheduled in advance.

One included a video featuring a photo of Ayman al-Zawahiri, who led al Qaeda after the death of Osama Bin Laden.

This was followed with an image of Humam Khalil Abu-Mulal al-Balawi, who killed nine people, including seven American CIA officers, in a 2009 suicide bombing.



The second post featured an AI-generated image depicting Islam’s three holiest sites – in Mecca, Medina and Jerusalem.

Israel is continuing to investigate how a suspected terrorist was able to bring a knife on board a plane and be allowed to fly an Israeli-bound plane.

Tel Aviv and Oman have no diplomatic relations and foreign crew are typically not allowed to fly into Israeli airspace without tight checks beforehand.

Flydubai has grounded all flights to and from Israel as investigations continue.

News.title: A single olive, two pints of ice cream & a lump of dirt – the most unusual final meal request from death row inmates
News.content:
LAST ORDERS A single olive, two pints of ice cream & a lump of dirt – the most unusual final meal request from death row inmates







Next

MURDERER Christa Pike refused to order a last meal before her botched execution on Wednesday.

The killer is thought to have been left with brain damage after two attempts to end her life by lethal injection.



But an empty plate is not the strangest final meal a death row inmate has requested.

In 1963, Victor Feguer, the last man killed under the death penalty in Iowa, requested a single olive as his final luxury.





The murderer kidnapped and killed a doctor after falsely claiming he was with a woman who needed urgent attention.

When he was served the olive – which he specifically requested to be unpitted – he reportedly told guards that he hoped that when he was buried, an olive tree would grow from his grave as a symbol of peace and redemption.

Gerald Lee Mitchell asked for a simple – if strange – last meal: one bag of boiled sweets, specifically assorted Jolly Ranchers.

It wasn’t quite as strange, however, as the final dinner of killer James Edward Smith.



He demanded a lump of dirt, specifically “rhaeakunda dirt” for use in a spiritual ritual.

The request was denied and he was instead given plain yogurt.

Timothy McVeigh, who bombed the Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building, killing 168 people, had a simple ask: he wanted just two pints of mint chocolate chip ice cream.



At the opposite end of the scale, Gary Carl Simmons Jr requested a roughly 30,000-calorie feast for his final dinner.

The butcher was sentenced to death by lethal injection after using butcher’s knives to dismember a body and dumping the remains in an alligator-infested swamp.

When it was time for his death sentence to be carried out in 2012, he asked for an eye-wateringly large amount of food – which he was said to be “still eating” moments before his death.

Simmons requested two Pizza Hut pizzas, with double portions of a huge amount of toppings, 10 8-oz. packs of Parmesan cheese and 10 of packs of ranch dressing and a family size bag of nacho cheese flavour Doritos.

But that wasn’t all. He also demanded 8-oz. of jalapeño nacho cheese, four-oz. of sliced jalapeños and a super-size order of McDonald’s fries with extra ketchup and mayonnaise.



He washed that down with two huge cherry cokes, two large strawberry shakes and two pints of strawberry ice cream.

Prison officials said he had eaten “at least half” of the massive smorgasbord.

Another enormous feast was demanded by Thomas J Grasso in 1995, who was executed for strangling an 85-year-old woman to death with Christmas tree lights.



He asked for 24 steamed clams, the same number of mussels, a Burger King double cheeseburger, six barbecue ribs, two milkshakes and a tin of SpaghettiOs with meatballs.

For dessert, he requested half a pumpkin pie and strawberries and cream.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

News.title: Girl, 5, among 10 injured after ‘car rams into crowd’ at rugby parade in ‘horrible incident’ as driver, 18, arrested
News.content:
Next

A FIVE-YEAR-OLD girl and a man, 67, are in critical condition after a car ploughed into a crowd of ruby fans in Australia.

Eight others were injured in the “horrific” incident and have been rushed to a nearby hospital, according to New South Wales police.



Around 1,000 fans of Newcastle Knights rugby league team had gathered in Newcastle, about 200 miles north of Sydney, as the teams coach set off.

But at around 9.30am a car rammed into the mass of supporters lining the streets, hitting at least 10 people.



A dozen ambulances and three air ambulances rushed to the scene.

Emergency crews treated the injured, including a two-year-old girl, at the site before transporting 10 people to hospital.



The ages of the other people who were hit ranged from 24 to 63.

Police said they arrested an 18-year-old man who had been driving the vehicle and were investigating what happened.

The man, a learner driver, will be subject to mandatory drug and alcohol testing, police added.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese posted on social media: “My thoughts are with everyone injured or involved in the horrible incident this morning in Newcastle.



“I want to acknowledge and thank emergency services and police for responding so quickly, and their ongoing work in treating the injured.”

Police said the crash was not believed to be related to terrorism.

“Police have commenced an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the incident, with initial inquiries indicating it is not believed to be terror related,” police said in an update.



Newcastle Mayor Gavin Morris said in televised remarks that it appeared the driver lost control of the car that hit the crowd.

The young man appeared to have been driving erratically before losing control of the vehicle.

Australian Minister for Police and Counterterrorism Yasmin Catley called the crash “an absolute tragedy” and a “tragedy that was preventable,” pleading with motorists to drive safely.

Police said officers had been escorting the Knights’ team bus, which had not yet left the stadium when the crash occurred.

In a statement, the Newcastle Knights said: “Our thoughts are with everyone impacted by the incident, including those at the scene and their families.”



It comes just weeks after two people were killed a 10 injured when a car ploughed into a crowd in France.

The alleged attack was said to have followed a fight that broke out near the bar, local media reported.

The driver, 26-year-old Russian national Ibrahim I., was arrested and faces charges of murder and intentional violence with a weapon.

He reportedly drove into a group of pedestrians outside a train station in Caen, in the Normandy region on August 26.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A source said: “The ramming is thought to have occurred after a violent argument inside the bar.



“The suspect left, and then returned with his car, attacking the men outside the railway station, as they milled around a tram stop.”

News.title: Breast milk breakthrough could help detect cancer earlier and save lives
News.content:
Breast milk breakthrough could help detect cancer earlier and save lives

Dr Mouliere, who leads the research team analysing samples, said it's a "major step forward"

View 3 Images Breastfeeding is known to lower the risk of breast cancer in the long term, but women have a higher risk during pregnancy and after giving birth (Image: Getty)

Researchers believe testing breast milk could help detect breast cancer sooner. Scientists at the University of Manchester are investigating whether circulating tumour DNA from cancer, which can be present in breast milk, could spot the disease earlier than current methods, such as blood tests or scans.

‌



‌



While breastfeeding is known to reduce breast cancer risk over the long term, women face a higher risk during pregnancy and in the period after giving birth. Some women also have genetic faults that put them at a higher risk of the disease when they are young.

‌



Dr Niki Flaum, who is leading the study and is a consultant oncologist at the Christie NHS Foundation Trust in Manchester, said: “There is an urgent need to find better, more reliable ways to detect breast cancer in women during and after pregnancy.

‌



“We believe breast milk may provide a unique and non-invasive window into what is happening inside the breast. We know surprisingly little about the genetic changes to breast milk, as this bio-fluid has been remarkably under-researched until now.

“Pregnancy-related breast cancer is more likely to be diagnosed at a later stage, when the cancer has already spread, and survival outcomes are significantly worse compared with women of the same age who have not recently given birth.

Dr Zoe Williams shares how to check your breasts for breasts cancer

‌



“Diagnosis is particularly challenging because breast imaging during pregnancy and lactation is often unreliable. If reliable methods for detecting cancer-related DNA in breast milk can be found, we hope future research will test whether this approach could be developed into a screening tool for women with breast cancer or those at high risk.”

Breast cancer is the leading cause of cancer deaths in the UK for women aged 35 to 64. Pregnancy-related breast cancer affects about one in 3,000 pregnancies, but for higher-risk women such as those with a faulty BRCA gene, the risk can be as high as 1 in 50.

The new research is funded by The Christie Charity. It is initially recruiting 40 women producing breast milk – 25 with general population risk and 15 from a high-risk category where there is a family history of breast cancer.

‌



The goal is to set up the Manchester Breast Biofluid Biobank with more than 200 samples for future research. The University of Manchester team will analyse the fluid samples at the National Biomarker Centre at The Christie.

Who donated breast milk for the study?

View 3 Images Hannah said: “Participating in the study was really straightforward. I just gave a blood sample and donated some breast milk and answered a few questions." (Image: University of Manchester/PA Wire )

One of the first mothers to donate breast milk for the study was Hannah Brennan, 31, from Glossop in Derbyshire, who has a 12-month-old girl, Ada, as well as a five-year old daughter and two-year-old son. A registered midwife, who is studying for a PhD at the University of Manchester, she said: “As soon as I saw the research team were looking to recruit women who were breastfeeding, I wanted to do it.

‌



“As I’m doing my doctorate, I’m passionate about people being involved in research. My paternal grandmother died aged 51 from breast cancer and sadly I never met her. However, I was named after her and I’m told I look like her so I’m doing this for her as well as my two daughters.

“Participating in the study was really straightforward. I just gave a blood sample and donated some breast milk and answered a few questions. As a midwife I feel it’s really important to help other women, so if my small contribution can benefit other mothers in the future, I’m just glad to be able to make a difference and would encourage other breastfeeding mums to take part.”

View 3 Images Hannah Brennan and her 12-month old daughter Ada (Image: University of Manchester/PA Wire )

Article continues below

This is a 'major step forward'

Dr Florent Mouliere, who leads the research team analysing samples, said: “Scientists in our laboratories have identified tiny fragments of genetic material shed by cells in some samples of breast milk that have been donated for this study. The DNA structure is unique in breast milk, and we now understand what this DNA looks like, which is a major step forward.”

Louise Hadley, chief executive of The Christie Charity, added: “We are very pleased to be able to fund this important research which could improve early detection of breast cancer in high-risk women, including BRCA carrier, enable screening specifically for pregnancy-related breast cancer and help predict risk of postpartum breast cancer.

“It would also provide reassurance for high-risk women wishing to breastfeed, who are currently often advised to stop early so MRI screening can resume. This support is part of The Christie Charity’s commitment to providing £30 million of much-needed funding by 2030 to enable our brightest researchers to make game-changing discoveries right here in Manchester. We are very grateful for the continued support of all our donors in helping us reach this goal.”

News.title: 'There's no guarantee' - warning for anyone renewing Blue Badge before December 31
News.content:
'There's no guarantee' - warning for anyone renewing Blue Badge before December 31

Experts says the Blue Badge parking permit operates in a different way to many other entitlements

View 3 Images A Blue Badge helps people park closer to their destination (Image: Getty)

People with disabilities are being warned of a little-known rule which could prove costly. Millions of people with mobility problems rely on a disabled parking permit, often known as a Blue Badge.

‌



‌



These allow the holders to park closer to their destination, wherever they might be going, and can include anything from doctor or hospital appointments to days out or shopping trips. However, there are strict rules around who qualifies for one of the permits and how they can be used - and getting it wrong can prove costly with the risk of a £1,000 fine.

‌



Now, the Later In Life Guide has issued a warning to holders that there is one little-known rule that does not work the same way as many other things. It says: "A Blue Badge is one of the few entitlements that quietly stops working on a date printed on its face. There is no reminder, no automatic renewal, and no period of grace afterwards - and councils are allowed up to 12 weeks to make a decision."

‌



View 3 Images A Blue Badge gives the holder the right to use disabled parking bays (Image: Getty)

This means anyone needing to renew or apply for a new Blue Badge in 2026 is no longer guaranteed to get it before the end of this year. While most of the permits will be processed more quickly than that, it could be 2027 before an application made today is completed.

Later In Life explains: "A Blue Badge usually lasts up to three years and does not renew itself. You have to apply again before it expires, and your council can take up to 12 weeks to decide. Starting three months before the expiry date is the safe approach, because there is no grace period once it runs out."

‌



It adds: "Councils usually reach a decision within 12 weeks of receiving an application, so a renewal begun a fortnight beforehand can easily leave you without a valid badge for weeks. There is no penalty for applying early, and the new badge runs from its own issue date rather than shortening anything."

View 3 Images Millions of people hold Blue Badges in the UK

One in 20 people across England holds a Blue Badge. The latest figures showed that 3.07 million people held one of the permits as of March 31, 2025.

‌



A Blue Badge costs up to £10 in England and £20 in Scotland, while it is free in Wales. In England, the scheme and the charge are set by local authorities, so the exact amount you pay can vary.

But even if you have already had a permit, you cannot use it once the expiry date has passed. Later in Life warns: "An expired badge is not valid, whatever stage your renewal has reached.

"Using one can mean a penalty charge and the loss of the parking concessions the badge provides, and no leeway is granted for an application that is still being processed. This is the single strongest reason to apply early rather than on time.

Article continues below

"If the date is already close, contact your council and say so — they can tell you where the application has reached." Currently, the penalty charge can be £1,000 if someone is caught using the badge when it is no longer valid.

News.title: NATO warplanes scrambled and airspace closed as thousands told to 'find safe place'
News.content:
NATO warplanes scrambled and airspace closed as thousands told to 'find safe place'

Airspace has been closed over part of Europe following a suspected drone sighting as Vladimir Putin appears to be continuing to test defences

View 2 Images NATO fighter jets have been scrambled in Lithuania (stock image) (Image: Gregor Fischer/picture-alliance/dpa/AP Images)

NATO fighter jets have been scrambled following a suspected drone sighting over Lithuania with thousands of residents urged to find shelter.

‌



‌



Airspace has been closed over the Baltic state's capital Vilnius and a mobile phone alert sent to residents, telling them to find a safe place, according to local reports.

‌



The suspected drone was detected entering Lithuania's airspace from key Russian-ally Belarus, which the country shares a south and eastern border with. It is thought it could be another example of Vladimir Putin testing NATO defences.

‌



A senior official said fighter jets are investigating the sighting of the object which has not been "fully identified".

View 2 Images Putin has been testing NATO's defences in recent months (Image: Getty Images)

Vilmantas Vitkauskas, head of Lithuania's National Crisis Management Centre, said the object resembles a drone on radar but did not rule out something less sinister, including a flock of birds.

‌



Last month, an Italian figher jet stationed in the country was scrambled after a possible drone sighting which turned out to be birds.

Mr Vitkauskas said authorities received reports from residents of a "possible object outside the territory of Vilnius, moving towards Jonava". "But we cannot confirm this, because these are reports from residents," he told public service broadcaster LRT RADIO.

NATO countries in the Baltic have faced repeated drone incursions since Russia began its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. The number of incidents have risen in recent months as countries along NATO's eastern flank warn of an increasing threat from Moscow.

‌



A drone that entered Lithuanian airspace was shot down by NATO fighter jets last month. Authorities didn’t comment on the drone's origin or purpose, saying further investigation was needed after the incident on September 15, but two senior officials said the device was likely carrying explosives.

Officials in other NATO countries, including the UK, Germany, Denmark and Poland, have in recent weeks accused Russia of involvement in acts such as drone incursions, sabotage, arson and surveillance of defence facilities and in plans to use a drone carrying explosives to attack an airport.

Meanwhile Denmark said the same day as the Lithuanian drone was shot down, that one of its air force helicopters was fired on with flares as it was carrying out surveillance of a Russian frigate in the Baltic Sea.

Article continues below

Strikes close to NATO territory showed Putin’s “desperation and also his desire to sow fear and terror,” NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte said in response. Rutte has pledged to bolster the 32-nation alliance’s own defences along its long eastern border with Russia and its ally Belarus,

News.content:

With Charles Spencer continuing his book tour with the American media, the Mirror’s Pod Save the King have exposed his ulterior motive when discussing his late sister, Princess Diana

Inside Prince Harry's astonishing conversation with uncle after explosive Diana book

‌



‌



Now, Earl Spencer has taken his book tour Stateside, as he has appeared on numerous American talk shows to reiterate his claims made in the book, and continue to hit back at the unprecedented statement made by the palace.

‌



And while Spencer’s book has been flying off the shelves with countless royal watchers immersing themselves in his recollections, the Mirror ’s royal editor Russell Myers believes the Earl may have an ulterior motive for penning the book in the first place.

‌

‌



In the memoir, Earl Spencer recalls sweet memories of his childhood with Diana spent at their ancestral home of Althorp House, where the late Princess of Wales is now buried.

During his book tour in the UK, Charles Spencer appeared on Lorraine, where he insisted he did not set out to create a ‘hit piece’ against the King, but added that he had ‘no regrets’ over including the monarch’s comments.

‌



Earl Spencer told Lorraine: “This book is a celebration of an extraordinary woman from a brother’s point of view. And as a brother, I have every right to write about my sister.

“But I would like to explain that I was not setting out to do a hit piece on the King at all. The comments [from Charles] that I’ve included in the book are totally in context.”

View 2 Images Earl Spencer is continuing his book tour in the US (Image: Ken McKay/ITV/Shutterstock)

Article continues below

The TV host then quizzed Spencer on if he felt he was ‘going against the Royal Family’ by writing the book, to which the earl said: “I’m really not. This is about Diana. It’s impossible to give the full story of Diana’s life without putting in context of certain things that were said.

“This is not a threat at all because I’m not going to do it, but if I wanted to write a hit piece on the Royal Family, I could do that, but that’s not my job. My job is to celebrate Diana, and by doing that, some people might come off not as good as they would like to.”

News.title: Disease-carrying ticks 'living for longer' in UK thanks to hotter summers
News.content:
Disease-carrying ticks 'living for longer' in UK thanks to hotter summers

Before now, it wasn't hot enough for Hyalomma ticks to make it all the way to reach adulthood

View 3 Images Previously, UK summers were not warm enough for these ticks to reach maturity (Image: Getty)

Ticks that carry diseases are staying alive longer in the UK because of the hot weather, according to an expert. Before, it wasn't hot enough for Hyalomma ticks to make it all the way to reach adulthood.

‌



‌



While still rare, it is something health officials are “starting to pick up a bit more”, says Dr Jolyon Medlock, who works as the head of medical entomology at the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA). Hyalomma ticks are the primary vectors of Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever, a serious and potentially fatal virus.

‌



These ticks sometimes show up in the UK by holding onto birds that migrate from the Mediterranean and Africa when the ticks are still young. This is the middle part of a tick's life when they're about as small as a poppy seed. Ticks move to the next stage of their life by moulting, where they shed their hard outer shell.

‌



Dr Medlock told the Press Association: “They would normally come in on migratory birds as a nymph, and then fall off, and they wouldn’t be able to moult. It’s not warm enough. What we’re seeing now in heatwave years is that they can moult through to the adult stage, and we then could be able to pick up records of adults through our tick surveillance.

“These have happened less than probably five times in the last 10 years or so, but it’s something that we and colleagues across northern Europe are starting to pick up a bit more. It doesn’t mean the tick will survive, and it doesn’t necessarily mean it’s an infection risk.”

View 3 Images The hard-bodied ticks are common in Asia, Europe, and North Africa (Image: Getty)

‌



The UKHSA’s Tick Surveillance Scheme was set up in 2005 to map and monitor ticks across the UK. Last year, gov.uk issued Mosquito and tick incidents message, which reads: "Hyalomma ticks can vector pathogens of human and animal health importance. We monitor the importation of this species in the UK using our Tick Surveillance Scheme, along with research projects which look for ticks imported into the country on migratory birds.

"Our data show that Hyalomma marginatum ticks enter the country regularly on migratory birds. Another important species called Hyalomma lusitanicum also enters the country on imported animals, such as dogs. You can report Hyalomma ticks to us using our Tick Surveillance Scheme."

Dr Medlock said there have been records of Hyalomma nymphs on migratory birds from observatories over the last 50 years. He added: “In their native area, they’re vectors of Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever virus, which is a relatively common virus that occurs in the Balkans that started to emerge in Spain recently. So these are the sort of climate-sensitive tick-borne disease pathogens that we might see.”

‌



According to the World Health Organisation, Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever is endemic in Africa, the Balkans, the Middle East and Asia, with a fatality rate of up to 40%. The virus can incubate for one to nine days after a tick bite.

View 3 Images Hyalomma ticks carry and transmit serious, life-threatening disease

It can also be transmitted through contact with infected animal blood or tissues. The onset of symptoms is sudden and can include fever, dizziness, neck pain, headache, sore eyes, nausea, vomiting, mood swings, and confusion.

Article continues below

Elsewhere, milder winters and hotter summers may also lead to a “shift in the seasonality” of ticks more broadly in the UK, according to Dr Medlock. He told PA: “The simple way of collecting ticks is to go and drag a blanket through the undergrowth, and if it’s a hot, humid day, they’re running around quite quickly.

“If you’ve got mild winters, then they will remain active throughout the winter. Usually they say 7C is the critical temperature for activity, I’ve seen them active at 3C. So as we have milder winters and hotter, drier summers, we’ll see a shift in the seasonality of ticks.”

News.content:
Harry and Meghan spotted enjoying pub lunch date as couple seen together for first time since UK return

Meghan has largely kept a low profile since the move while focusing on helping the children settle into their new schools, while Harry has attended a string of engagements both in the UK and abroad

Prince Harry and Meghan Markle have been spotted enjoying a quiet pub lunch together in the Cotswolds.

‌



The Duke and Duchess of Sussex were pictured at The Falkland Arms in Great Tew, Oxfordshire, in a rare public appearance together since the family returned to the UK. The couple stopped for a meal while their children, Prince Archie, seven, and Princess Lilibet, five, were at school.

‌



Both wore sunglasses as they arrived at the 16th-century pub, with Harry seen looking at a menu board outside. Meghan opted for a casual all-black outfit with white shoes, while Harry wore a Santa Barbara fire department cap.

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

‌



Meghan has since been seen getting to know the area around the family’s new home. She was recently spotted at The Falkland Arms with close friend Kelly McKee Zajfen and her young son.

A spokesman for the couple described their behaviour as “reckless” and “irresponsible”.

Harry and Meghan have not publicly visited King Charles since returning to the UK on August 26, although they are understood to have spoken to him by phone.

A friend of the Sussexes said: “They are enjoying exploring the area including local watering holes. Meghan has been spending a lot of time since their move to the UK making sure the children are settled and working on her As Ever brand.
