World.title: Flydubai co-pilot attacked captain with crash axe in ‘terrorist act’: UAE
World.content:
Probe ⁠under way to ​determine ‘all the ⁠circumstances’, including motive, UAE’s prosecutor general says.

The prosecutor general of the United Arab Emirates has said a Flydubai co-pilot “attempted to carry out a terrorist act” during a flight earlier this week, using a crash axe against the pilot inside the cockpit.

State news agency WAM quoted Hamad Saif al-Shamsi as saying on Saturday that the attacker of Wednesday’s flight FZ1073 tried to take control of the aircraft’s flight controls.

He said the investigation is under way “to uncover all the circumstances of the incident, its motives, and related connections, in addition to completing technical examinations and examining physical and digital evidence”.

The final results will be announced as soon as the necessary procedures are completed, al-Shamsi said.

A crash axe is a tool kept in a cockpit to help pilots cut through the plane in emergencies.

The plane carrying 174 passengers was on its way from the UAE’s Dubai to Israel’s Tel Aviv on Wednesday when an unnamed co-pilot wounded Indian pilot Smit Machchhar who opened the cockpit to seek help.

The aircraft briefly plunged about 17,000 feet (5,180 metres) before it was brought back under control by a second paid of new pilots after passengers and crew subdued the attacker.

The flight was diverted and forced to make an emergency landing at Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz International Airport in Tabuk in northwestern Saudi Arabia.

The co-pilot was arrested by Saudi authorities and handed over to the UAE as it leads the probe.

Machchhar was also returned to the UAE.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Friday that ⁠Israel was looking into whether the co-pilot had acted under anyone’s direction, warning that anyone involved would pay a “heavy price”.



Flydubai halted all flights its Israel route after the incident and Israel’s El Al cancelled its scheduled flights, stranding some Israelis in the UAE.

At 22:00 GMT on Friday, the first repatriation flight, operated by Israeli carrier Arkia, arrived at Tel Aviv’s Ben Gurion Airport from Dubai.

World.title: Gaza voters want jobs and security as Palestinian elections approach
World.content:
Ahead of first Palestinian national elections in 20 years, people in Gaza hope to rebuild after Israeli destruction.

Deir el-Balah, Gaza Strip – Ahmad Mohsen, 24, sits in a shop selling prepaid internet access cards in Deir el-Balah. Three years ago, before Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza started, he imagined a different future. He had graduated with a degree in nursing and was preparing to complete the procedures required to obtain his professional licence. He dreamed of working in a hospital, pursuing a master’s degree or taking specialised courses.

But the war pushed him onto a different path.

During the first months of the war, Mohsen worked as a volunteer at Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital in Deir el-Balah, amid large numbers of wounded and dead, before the lack of pay led him to look for other work.

“I got tired, and I wasn’t being paid for my efforts, so I started looking for another job that would give me at least a small income,” he said.

The upcoming Palestinian legislative elections, scheduled for November 28, would be Mohsen’s first national vote, and the first Palestinian legislative election since 2006. Mohsen has his priorities: he wants candidates to address problems facing his generation, including unemployment, security, housing, education and healthcare.

“The first thing I want is to be able to find a stable job with a decent salary so I can support myself and my family, and the second thing is to have security,” he said.

Mohsen’s concerns are common among Palestinians in Gaza, where unemployment sits at about 80 percent. The enclave’s economy has been destroyed following years of Israeli blockade and its war that has killed more than 74,000 Palestinians.



His family owns land east of Gaza’s Salah al-Din Street, in an area Israel restricts access to, leaving him unable to reach it. He hopes that, in accordance with the October 2025 ceasefire agreement, Israel will soon withdraw from the area and allow for reconstruction to begin in the devastated territory.

For Mohsen, elections are not enough if they do not translate into improvements in people’s lives.

“A candidate should put themselves in the people’s place and speak with the people’s voice, not someone else’s voice. They should speak for us, the young people who have been wronged for 20 years through wars and destruction. There needs to be an end to this,” he said.

Democratic memories

Unlike Mohsen, Ghassan Marwan, 53, carries memories of the 2006 elections, which were won by Hamas.

Marwan previously worked as a goldsmith and established a factory that became his family’s source of income.

When he went to the polls in 2006, he hoped the elections would help improve people’s lives, provide security and jobs, and give his children a more stable future. He remembers voting at a school in Nuseirat for a list headed by the independent politician Mustafa Barghouti, and says the experience was transparent and fair.

“I witnessed a great deal of transparency and integrity. It was like a democratic celebration. But unfortunately, that experience was not repeated over the past 20 years,” Marwan said.

Twenty years later, his life has completely changed. He lost his home and his factory in January 2024, during the war. More than 30 years of work can no longer guarantee the stability he had sought for his family.

“After losing your home and your source of income, what else do you want? All you hope for is reconstruction, calm and security in the country,” he said.

What hurts Marwan most, he said, is seeing his children living among tents instead of in the stable home he had hoped to provide. The war has also brought him back to tasks he never imagined he would face after years of work, such as searching for water and carrying it over long distances.

“After all these years, I am carrying water from far away. Am I going to remain in this situation? I am 53 today. In 10 years, I will be in my 60s, and I will not be able to carry this burden,” he said.

Marwan believes these circumstances have also affected people’s interest in politics.



“Our interest in politics has declined, not because it does not concern us, but because of all the frustration and despair that have accumulated. People have become preoccupied with how to get by and secure their daily bread,” he added.

The prospect of elections amid the widespread destruction and displacement around him nevertheless leaves him torn between hope and scepticism.

“Sometimes I feel that talking about elections is almost a joke, because there are no clear conditions for holding them,” he said.

Recovery is priority

The Palestinian Central Elections Commission is preparing to hold the vote in the occupied West Bank, occupied East Jerusalem and Gaza. It estimates that about 1.24 million Palestinians in Gaza will be eligible to vote.

According to Jamil al-Khalidi, the commission’s regional director in Gaza, the process faces logistical and security challenges because of the scale of destruction in the territory and the mass displacement that has occurred since Israel’s war started. The commission has prepared contingency plans to produce election materials locally in case Israel restricts the entry of supplies into Gaza.

For Gaza-based political analyst and writer Iyad al-Qarra, the war has not eliminated Palestinians’ interest in politics, but has instead changed what they expect politics to deliver.

After nearly three years of displacement, destruction and lost livelihoods, he argued that political demands from Palestinians in Gaza have become directly linked to the ability of future leaders to restore a normal life, rather than simply administer institutions or offer political slogans.

Al-Qarra says that the priority is a leadership capable of representing people and meeting their basic needs, foremost among them rebuilding Gaza, restoring infrastructure and the health and education sectors, and creating conditions that allow people to regain their lives and livelihoods.

“There is a widespread desire for leadership that puts Gaza’s recovery at the top of its priorities, given the heavy price the Strip has paid,” al-Qarra said.

More reports are emerging that Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu rejected a Hamas proposal to release all civilian captives taken on October 7, 2023. Netanyahu’s actions have become a key topic less than a month before national elections.

World.title: WHO warns of ‘devastating consequences’ due to delayed aid entry into Gaza
World.content:
The WHO’s representative in Palestine calls on Israeli authorities to “release the pressure on medical supplies”.

Share WHO warns of ‘devastating consequences’ due to delayed aid entry into Gaza on social media

Repeated delays in bringing life-saving medicines, prosthetics and other supplies from Israel into Gaza risk having “devastating consequences” for Palestinians who urgently need them, the World Health Organization (WHO) has said.

Approved aid can enter Gaza only through Kerem Shalom, at the southern tip of the territory, while Rafah, also in the south, is open only for limited movement of people, including patients needing medical treatment abroad, the WHO said on Friday.

“A truck full of non-priority supplies or the right supplies arriving too late, doesn’t save lives. That’s the question that actually matters,” Reinhilde Van De Weerdt, the WHO’s representative in Palestine, said.

Van De Weerdt called on Israeli authorities to “release the pressure on medical supplies”, saying essential medicines “should not be considered as dual use, as they are globally accepted standards on medical items anybody needs anywhere to run a hospital or a clinic”.

She added that one shipment of prosthetics and assistive devices had been rejected four times over the past six months.

“Every rejection means another delay for someone who has already lost a limb and is simply waiting for the chance to walk again,” she said, noting that medicines “by contrast, move relatively well”, with almost 87 percent approved and just over 1 percent rejected.

“Our ask is simple and has not changed: we need the unimpeded and predictable entry of humanitarian and health supplies into Gaza at scale. We also need a multi-crossing model so that aid isn’t forced to trickle down through a limited number of crossings,” Van De Weerdt said.



Four other main entry points into Gaza – Kissufim, Gate 96, Erez and Erez West – remain closed and under total Israeli control.

She praised the “extraordinary health workers” still risking their lives in Gaza, who she said were not receiving enough supplies to give patients the care they needed.

Winter and disease risk

“As winter begins, this urgency to get supplies into Gaza only deepens,” Van De Weerdt said. “Almost two million people are in need of shelter to protect against the cold and the risk of flooding, exposing people to serious health and safety risks, let alone their dignity.”

She said residents faced a heightened risk of preventable disease outbreaks linked to the lack of safe shelter and clean water, and a high number of rats whose bites transmit infection, a threat made harder to track by the destruction of public health laboratories.

The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) warned on Thursday of serious public health risks from the accumulation of solid waste in Gaza City, where sanitation gains remain fragile because of a lack of reliable access to heavy machinery, engine oil, spare parts and fuel funding.

Almost 12 months into a fragile “ceasefire” between Hamas and Israel, marked by continuing Israeli air attacks and other military activity, Gaza’s humanitarian situation remains “overwhelming”, according to OCHA.

World.title: Flydubai co-pilot attacked captain with axe, UAE official says
World.content:
The co-pilot of the Flydubai plane travelling to Israel attacked the pilot with a crash axe in an attempt to take control of the aircraft, the United Arab Emirates prosecutor general has said.

The flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv carrying more than 170 people plunged more than 17,000ft (5,200m) two and a half hours into its journey.

Capt Smit Machchhar said he was lying on the cockpit floor injured when he realised the plane was sinking and he had to act, explaining: "I told myself to go for one last push to open the door from inside."

Passengers aboard the aircraft were then able to enter the cockpit and overpower the attacker, while on-duty crew travelling on the flight landed the plan safely.

A crash axe is usually kept âin the cockpit in case of emergencies.

The UAE attorney general told state media that investigations were ongoing to determine the full circumstances and motives of the incident.

The co-pilot who launched the attack was an Omani national, according to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Netanyahu told Fox News on Thursday that, after being subdued, the attacker called out to the crew, "Kill me, kill me!"

He added: "So, it's clear that he was suicidalâ¦ It looks very likely that he was going to down the plane."

He also said the attacker "underwent Islamist radical indoctrination".

The UAE has begun investigating whether the "incident was linked to any terrorist activity or purpose", according to the country's state news agency.

Machchhar, who was stabbed in the attack, was taken to a nearby hospital before being airlifted to Abu Dhabi, where he is reported to be in a stable condition.

He was in "good health and recovering well", the Indian embassy in the UAE said on Thursday.

The pilot said: "I am confident that the recovery will be there and I will become fit and healthy again."

World.title: Russia strikes second major bridge in Kyiv, mayor says
World.content:
A Russian strike has hit a second major bridge in Kyiv, Mayor Vitali Klitschko has said, as Russia ramps up attacks on critical infrastructure in the Ukrainian capital.

The attack on Saturday morning damaged the road surface and trolleybus overhead wires on the Northern Bridge, Klitschko said, causing traffic to be blocked.

The strike comes after another key bridge in the city, Southern Bridge, was targeted multiple times by Russian drones on Thursday and Friday, with Klitschko earlier warning that such attacks were "tearing Kyiv apart".

The Northern and Southern bridges link the eastern and western parts of the capital and had not been hit before Thursday, signalling a new stage in Moscow's strategy.

Attacks on the Southern Bridge have caused major travel disruption since Thursday, with metro and car travel across it suspended.

Many of the city's residents - which number about three million - rely on the metro to travel across the city.

World.title: G7 to release millions of barrels of oil and diesel after Trump threat
World.content:
The G7 has announced 100 million barrels of oil and diesel will be released to ease supply concerns that have caused prices to skyrocket.

It includes a "substantial release" of diesel within 20 days, with discussions around "additional diesel releases as necessary", G7 leaders said in a statement.

The group of advanced economies, including the US, said the move would begin immediately and would last for four months.

Under the measures, which come after US President Donald Trump had threatened to ban diesel exports, there will not be any "export restrictions on energy and energy products" between G7 members.

The G7 includes the US, UK, Canada, Japan, Germany, Italy and France, with the EU also represented at its meetings.

Donald Trump had warned he would ban diesel exports from the US if European countries did not agree to put more of their own stocks onto the market. That would have eased pressure on prices for US consumers ahead of November's midterm elections, but pushed up prices elsewhere.

On Friday, he said on social media: "Europe has just agreed to release a massive amount of their heavily stocked Diesel Oil. The process will begin immediately."

His Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent had argued US farmers, truckers, and businesses "should not be left carrying the burden" as prices soar.

Speaking later at the White House, Trump said an export ban on diesel was "never really on the table".

Referring to the decision by the G7 to release fuel from reserves, he added that "what Europe did was a great thing."

"Europe has a lot of diesel and they're going to be making a major world contribution - and so are we," he said.

"And we're not going to be doing the export ban, we're going to be doing what we're supposed to do."

Trump had first said he backed a diesel export ban early last week, and was still considering it on Thursday, as his administration put pressure on Europe to tap its supplies.

Diesel is used heavily by the haulage industry and in agriculture, meaning rises in the cost of the fuel feed through into essentials such as food.

World.title: US murderer Christa Pike unconscious and on ventilator after failed execution, lawyers say
World.content:
Pike's lawyers filed an emergency motion on Friday to preserve "any and all evidence" related to her botched execution.

Hospital staff are working to save her life and clear the drug used, pentobarbital, from her system, the filing states.

During the execution attempt, prison officials tried to start intravenous (IV) lines by using at least seven needles on Pike, according to her lawyers.

At one point, Pike herself offered guidance of where they could try.

"One needle was bent in a 90-degree angle when it was removed," the filing states.

While receiving the two doses, "she could be heard crying, whimpering, and breathing loudly throughout the procedure", her lawyers said.

Tennessee Governor Bill Lee ordered an independent review into Pike's botched execution and he halted all executions in the state for the year.

The state's department of correction has defended the method it used, saying "the protocol does not allow for additional procedures beyond what was carried out".

Authorities are yet to say whether they will try again to execute Pike. They have not not offered any explanations about what went wrong.

World.title: Cornell frat house rape accuser 'under siege' online, says lawyer
World.content:
The lawyer for the woman who alleges she was raped at a Cornell University fraternity house says she is "not doing well" as she finds herself "under siege" from online sleuths seeking to identity her.

Thomas Giuffra said the woman known in legal documents as Jane Doe was "incapable of consent" because she was "completely, grossly intoxicated" when she turned up at the home where she says the assault took place.

The woman alleges she was assaulted by seven men at the campus in Ithaca, New York, in 2024.

No charges were initially filed in the case. It has reopened since she filed a civil lawsuit that thrust the claims into the national spotlight, reigniting the possibility of criminal charges.

In an interview on Friday with CNN, Giuffra said: "She's under siege on social media where people are trying to identify her."

He said that postings have "incorrectly" identified other woman as Doe.

World.title: Riot police clash with students as education protests rage in France
World.content:
Darmanin said that 735 of France's 3,700 schools were now affected "one way or another" by the violent protests.

Announcing the arrests late on Friday, NuÃ±ez told France's TF1 television network: "We are sliding into riot and urban violence, and we are using all intermediate means to put an end to it."

Meanwhile, Education Minister Ãdouard Geffray said the movement had been hijacked by non-students.

He told French broadcaster BFMTV that teachers had said "the people in front of me were not my students".

Earlier on Friday, a 17-year-old was arrested on suspicion of attempted homicide after protests in Belfort, north-eastern France, where a police officer was targeted.

BBC Verify has now authenticated two videos that show the man, who was later identified as an officer by a minister, being beaten up.

In the graphic footage, a group of young men are seen chasing him. The officer falls to the ground, and is subsequently punched and kicked multiple times in the head.

At least 65 staff members have been injured in the unrest, the education ministry said.

In the Paris suburb of Pantin police charged at protesters and made arrests after projectiles where thrown at officers.

Meanwhile, in Strasbourg tear gas was deployed as police feared conditions would become more hostile, according to the Reuters news agency.

Rubbish bins have also been set on fire in Rennes and Paris.

"As far as we're concerned, we've won - our school is closed this morning," Lola, a 16-year-old protester, told the AFP news agency on Friday.

She said police actions had made things worse.

"It makes us even angrier - the police have no right to hit us or use tear gas on us," she added.

World.title: Women given shorts at Oktoberfest to prevent upskirting
World.content:
The operator of a popular amusement ride at the Munich Oktoberfest has been handing out free cycling shorts to women, after thousands of voyeuristic videos emerged on social media.

Some videos showing women on the Teufelsrad, or Devil's Wheel, have been viewed millions of times. One is said to have made thousands of euros for a woman who posted it online.

The Teufelsrad is one of the oldest attractions at the Oktoberfest, the annual beer festival which comes to an end this weekend after 16 days. Its circular platform rotates faster and faster until its riders fall off, and the motion and speed often make skirts fly up.

Filming under skirts is illegal in Germany, and carries a two-year sentence in jail.

However, critics believe the law does not go far enough, and the videos of women on the Teufelsrad in their traditional dirndl dresses often show their underwear. Sometimes, the images have been digitally altered to show them naked, according to local broadcaster BR.

World.title: Spanish PM Sánchez loses key housing crisis vote after eviction of woman, 87
World.content:
The Sindicato de Inquilinas (Tenants' Union) activist association which has been co-ordinating protests, announced during the congressional debate that it was abandoning the tent protest in central Madrid. It said it wanted to "take the struggle to all the neighbourhoods, residential blocks and homes of Madrid, wherever there are rental increases, expulsions and abuses each day, and turn the energy of the last few days into a permanent organisation".

Protesters are also calling for a general strike over the housing crisis.

The left-wing coalition government responded to the social anger by hurriedly drawing up the two decree-laws in an effort to defuse the protests.

The first decree included the suspension of evictions of vulnerable tenants until 2030, a two-year extension to rental leases due to expire before 2028, tax increases for tourist apartments, and a restriction on the purchase of residential properties by what the government calls "vulture funds".

The second decree was more controversial, because it included the automatic renewal of rental contracts, a major demand of many on the left and the Sindicato de Inquilinas.

The conservative People's Party (PP) and far-right Vox had already said they would vote against both initiatives, leaving the minority government depending on the support of smaller nationalist parties in Catalonia and the Basque Country.

However, by the eve of the parliamentary session, the centre-right, pro-independence Together for Catalonia (JxCat) had signalled its opposition to both laws, condemning them to failure.

Friday's debate was fierce and at times angry, as supporters and opponents of the decrees clashed in Congress.

"I don't ask you, I beg you to be brave and consistent," SÃ¡nchez said, moments before the two votes took place. "Because they are not just ambitious measures, they are necessary".

He appealed to lawmakers "to put order and humanity into [the housing] market, because if we don't, it will bring down our society".

Social Affairs minister Pablo Bustinduy, of the Sumar alliance, the junior partner in the governing coalition, presented the debate in dramatic terms.

"Today is about defending an international oligarchy which is extracting the rent from salaries earned with the effort of working classes of this country in order to share it out with dividends and they don't even pay taxes in Spain," he said.

"Voting against these decrees today means defending the interests of this oligarchy and turning your back on your own people."

However, Miriam Nogueras, of JxCat, said the decrees had been hastily drawn up and lacked rigour.

She said the decrees "will allow [vulture] funds to keep buying, keep speculating and evictions to keep happeningâ¦ these two decrees would provoke the opposite effect of what they aim to achieve."

The political right has argued that the government's attempts to intervene will frighten homeowners, causing them not to put their properties on the rental market and pushing prices up further.

Juan Bravo of the PP said "housing doesn't get cheaper with decrees, it gets cheaper with more homes".

World.title: FRSC confirms 20 dead in multiple-vehicle crash in Plateau
World.content:
The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) has confirmed the death of 20 people in a multiple road traffic crash along the Hawan Kibo-Jos route in Plateau.

The Corps Public Education Officer (CPEO), Osondu Ohaeri, disclosed this in a statement issued on Friday in Abuja.

Mr Ohaeri said the crash occurred at about 3:32 p.m. after Sopp Water Falls, with brake failure and loss of control identified as likely causes.

He said 25 people were involved in the crash, comprising 23 males and two females.

According to him, five people, comprising three males and two females, sustained injuries, while 20 males died in the crash.

“Four vehicles were involved in the crash, including a Howo Sino truck with registration number AGL 525 YN.

“Others were a Toyota Corolla with registration number AB 129 M and a Toyota Bummer bus operated by Yankari Express.

“The fourth vehicle was a motorcycle whose registration particulars were not available.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“The injured victims were evacuated to Ryom General Hospital and Vom Christian Hospital, while the deceased were deposited at JUTH Mortuary.

“FRSC rescue personnel also cleared the obstruction caused by the crash and restored the affected highway section to traffic,” he said.

Reacting to the incident, FRSC Corps Marshal, Shehu Mohammed, expressed sadness over the loss of lives.

He extended his condolences to the families, friends and associates of the deceased and prayed for the repose of their souls.

Mr Mohammed also wished the injured victims a speedy recovery and directed the crash investigation team to conduct a thorough investigation.

He said the investigation should establish the circumstances surrounding the incident, particularly the reported brake failure and loss of control.

The corps marshal urged motorists, especially commercial and heavy-duty vehicle operators, to prioritise roadworthiness, maintenance, speed management and responsible driving.

Mr Mohammed further admonished drivers to exercise greater caution, stressing that the loss of 20 lives in one crash was not merely a statistic.

“The loss of 20 lives in a single crash represents 20 families suddenly plunged into grief. Behind every number is a name, a home, a family and a future,” he said.

Mr Mohammed, therefore, urged all road users to take personal responsibility for safety, stressing that no journey was so urgent that it should end in death.

(NAN)

World.title: One arrested as troops dismantle terrorists’ camp, rescue kidnap victims
World.content:
The Nigerian Army says troops of 185 Battalion have dismantled a criminal hideout used by suspected terrorists in Anambra State, Nigeria’s south-east.

The army, in a statement posted on its Facebook page on Friday, said the troops also rescued three kidnap victims.

It said the victims were abducted around Osakwa General Area in Ihiala Local Government Area of the state, which prompted the troops to begin the rescue operation in collaboration with the Anambra Vigilante Group.

“On 1 October 2026, troops subsequently conducted a snap operation and arrested one of the suspected kidnappers, identified as Sunday Obi.

“During interrogation, the suspect provided information that led troops to the location of the syndicate’s camp at Abator in Ogbaru Local Government Area, across the Isieke waterside,” it stated.

The army said that the troops subsequently launched another operation at the identified location with canoes to cross the waterways and access the terrorists’ hideout.

“On reaching the area, troops engaged the terrorists with overwhelming firepower, forcing them to flee with gunshot wounds,” the army said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

According to the statement, AK-47 rifles with magazines, three pump-action guns, three locally fabricated Dane guns, 62 rounds of 7.62mm NATO ammunition and 149 rounds of 7.62mm Special ammunition, together with two cartridges and materials, were recovered.

Others were items supporting the terrorists’ operational and logistical activities, including a solar generator, power bank, car battery, two motorcycle batteries, two solar panels and two mobile phones.

“The recovery further exposes the logistical infrastructure sustaining terrorist and kidnapping activities in the area and provides additional intelligence for ongoing efforts to dismantle the wider network,” the army said.

The statement further said the Nigerian Army, through Operation Udo Ka, will sustain “coordinated kinetic and intelligence-driven operations” to dismantle more terrorist enclaves and dislodge the criminals.

“Follow-up operations are underway to apprehend fleeing terrorists, their collaborators, logistics suppliers and other facilitators while troops continue to work with relevant security agencies and local stakeholders to strengthen security and safeguard communities,” it added.

Insecurity in South-east

For years, the South-east has witnessed deadly attacks by gunmen.

The attacks have often been linked to the outlawed Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB).

But IPOB has repeatedly denied its involvement in the attacks.

The group has been agitating for an independent state of Biafra, which it wants carved out from South-east and some parts of South-south Nigeria.

READ ALSO: SSS arraigns four IPOB members allegedly linked to killing of operative

The separatist group was outlawed by Nigerian authorities in 2017 and designated a terrorist organisation, which it has unsuccessfully challenged at various courts in Nigeria.

Its leader, Nnamdi Kanu, was sentenced to life imprisonment for terrorism in November 2025 and has been serving the jail term at the Sokoto prison facility, although he has filed an appeal against his conviction and sentencing.

Meanwhile, the Nigerian security operatives – mainly the police and the Nigerian Army – have been conducting various operations in the South-east to confront gunmen linked to IPOB.

But a recent PREMIUM TIMES report revealed that attacks and killings have reduced by 50 per cent in the South-east since the arrest and imprisonment of a controversial Biafra agitator, Simon Ekpa, in Finland in 2025.

Mr Ekpa, who leads a faction of IPOB called Autopilot, was sentenced to six years’ imprisonment in Finland in 2025 for terrorism related offences.

World.title: PT Health Watch: Can menstrual cups break hymen or affect virginity?
World.content:
As more women consider menstrual cups as an option for managing their periods, questions have emerged about whether using them can affect the hymen or a woman’s virginity.

Some people fear that inserting a menstrual cup could “break” the hymen, cause a woman to lose her virginity or permanently make the vagina “loose”.

Speaking with PT Health Watch, Elizabeth Adewale, a Certified Holistic Sex Educator and Public Health Professional, said many of these concerns stem from misconceptions about the hymen and what it means medically to be a virgin.

Hymen changes

According to Ms Adewale, inserting a menstrual cup can stretch the hymen and, in some cases, may cause a small tear, but “this does not mean that a woman has lost her virginity.”

She explained that the hymen is a thin, elastic fold of tissue around the vaginal opening that varies in shape, thickness and elasticity from woman to woman.

“If it were a seal, menstrual blood and normal vaginal discharge wouldn’t be able to come out,” she said.

Ms Adewale said the hymen can also change for reasons unrelated to sexual intercourse, including physical activities such as cycling, gymnastics and other exercise. She added that some women may have very little hymenal tissue, while in others it may be difficult to see.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The American College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (ACOG) also explains that the hymen is a thin membrane that partially covers the entrance to the vagina and can be stretched or torn through tampon use, sports activities or medical procedures. It also says the presence or absence of the hymen does not indicate “virginity”.

Virginity marker

Ms Adewale said the belief that every woman is born with a hymen that remains intact until her first sexual experience is incorrect.

“The hymen is not a virginity marker,” she said.

She explained that the hymen does not simply disappear after sexual intercourse and can still be present afterwards, although its appearance may have changed.

According to the expert, this means that looking at a woman’s hymen cannot establish whether she has had sex.

The World Health Organisation (WHO) says there is no scientific or clinical examination that can prove whether a woman or girl has had vaginal intercourse. It also states that the appearance of the hymen cannot prove whether someone has had sexual intercourse or is sexually active.

Vaginal elasticity

Another concern is that inserting a menstrual cup could permanently stretch the vagina and make it “loose”.

Ms Adewale said there is no medical basis for this belief.

“The vagina is an elastic, muscular canal,” she said, noting that it can relax, expand and contract depending on what is happening.

She said inserting or removing a menstrual cup does not permanently stretch the vagina.

“Your vagina isn’t going to suddenly become a wide-open hole because you’ve used a menstrual cup,” she said.

However, Ms Adewale noted that vaginal insertion can be painful or difficult for some women.

She explained that women with vaginismus, for instance, may experience involuntary tightening of the vaginal or pelvic floor muscles, making the insertion of a menstrual cup, tampon, finger or penis painful or difficult.

“It’s not because their vagina is too small,” she said.

According to ACOG, vaginismus is an involuntary tightening of the muscles at the opening of the vagina that can make penetration painful or difficult.

Using menstral cup

For women who choose to try a menstrual cup, Ms Adewale advised first-time users not to rush the process.

She recommended relaxing before insertion, washing the hands and cleaning the cup properly, finding a comfortable position and following the manufacturer’s instructions on how to fold and insert the cup.

A woman can squat, sit on the toilet or stand with one leg raised on a stool, she said, adding that taking slow, deep breaths can also help.

“Once you’ve successfully inserted it, allow it to open properly and create a seal, but don’t force it. If you experience significant pain, stop, don’t have to force it,” she said.

She added that first-time users may need time to become comfortable with the process and understand what works best for them.

Ms Adewale said the choice of menstrual product is personal and women should not feel pressured to use a menstrual cup if it does not work for them.

World.title: INVESTIGATION: The fake professor leading a Nigerian university
World.content:
Anthony Kila, the pro-chancellor of Michael and Cecilia Ibru University (MCIU), has long presented himself publicly as a professor and a “Jean Monnet Professor of Strategy and Development”, but PREMIUM TIMES has found that he was never awarded the academic rank.

Mr Kila, appointed pro-chancellor of MCIU in August 2025, has a long list of academic profiles that present him as a well-educated and widely travelled jurist, professor, scholar, accomplished professional, author, and public commentator of repute.

A pro-chancellor chairs the governing council of every Nigerian university. The governing council is in turn charged with the general control and supervision of the administration, policy implementation, finance and assets of the university.

Mr Kila, the MCIU pro-chancellor, has given many interviews to Nigerian newspapers and television stations, where he is frequently addressed as ‘professor’.

Some publications call him a professor of political science, while others refer to him as the Jean Monnet Professor of Strategy and Development. But they are both made up.

This PREMIUM TIMES investigation has now found that no recognised academic institution has ever awarded Mr Kila a professorial title.

This investigation also found that his profile on the MCIU and CIAPS websites contain suspicious academic qualifications and roles used to embellish his academic standing, raising questions about his other academic qualifications.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

In his response to our reporter, Mr Kila said the European Centre for Advanced and Professional Studies (ECAPS) awarded him the professorship. But this newspaper found that the institution is non-existent, present only in Mr Kila’s profile.

When presented with our findings, a spokesperson for Michael and Cecilia Ibru University said the institution has no evidence that Mr Kila is not a professor as he claimed.

PREMIUM TIMES had contacted Thomas Kolo, a former Registrar at MCIU, asking to speak with the university spokesperson. He then passed the phone to someone who identified himself as the spokesperson, but failed to provide his name.

“We don’t debate issues. You can go up with whatever you are going up with. If there’s a need to respond, we will respond when we see the article,” the spokesperson said.

‘Fake Professor’

In his profile on the MCIU and CIAPS websites, he was identified as ‘Prof. Anthony Kila’. In several television and newspaper interviews reviewed by this newspaper, he was also regularly addressed as a professor.

The professorial rank is the highest academic rank awarded to top researchers and educators in Nigerian universities and globally.

There is no evidence that Mr Kila ever taught at any university in Nigeria and abroad or that he was ever awarded the title.

Mr Kila told PREMIUM TIMES that the European Centre for Advanced and Professional Studies (ECAPS) based in Cambridge in the United Kingdom awarded him the professorship in 2016.

However, this newspaper found that the institution doesn’t exist anywhere, except in Mr Kila’s profiles.

A search on the UK Companies House and Nigeria’s Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC), as well as a general online search, didn’t provide any leads, including a website, social media handles, an address, or alumni of the said institution.

Mr Kila also claimed the European Centre for Advanced and Professional Studies (ECAPS) made him a ‘Jean Monnet professor of Strategy and Development’.

The title “Jean Monnet Professor” is associated with the European Union’s Jean Monnet Actions, a programme established to promote teaching, research and debate on European Union integration.

PREMIUM TIMES contacted the European Education and Culture Executive Agency (EACEA), which administers the programme, to establish Mr Kila’s status.

In its response, the Jean Monnet team said Mr Kila does not appear as a Jean Monnet project coordinator for any project, based on information accessible in its directory.

“In other words, within the period for which coordinator data are publicly available, Mr Kila has not been listed as holding the role of Jean Monnet project coordinator since 2015,” the agency said.

PREMIUM TIMES also contacted Jean-Marc Trouille, a professor and co-chair of the AfriquEurope Jean Monnet Network. Mr Trouille is also the Director of the Jean Monnet Centre of Excellence on the EU and Regional Integration in the East African Community.

Mr Trouille said Mr Kila’s status regarding the Jean Monnet programme is ‘highly unlikely’.

“First, I think it is highly unlikely that Prof. Kila would hold a Jean Monnet Chair award,” he wrote to our reporter in an email.

Mr Trouille said he searched for Jean Monnet activity involving Mr Kila and found that the only Jean Monnet module in Nigeria that he was aware of was at the University of Lagos, where Mr Kila did not appear on the team.

Mr Kila also confirmed to this newspaper that he was not associated with the Jean Monnet actions. He, however, failed to explain how he began to refer to himself as a “Jean Monnet professor.”

How to become a professor

A professor is the highest academic rank and is attained through promotion within a university.

According to the National Universities Commission (NUC), which regulates Nigerian universities, the minimum standard for attaining the rank of professor considers a candidate’s academic qualifications, teaching and research experience, publications, postgraduate supervision and contribution to knowledge.

“The first level qualification is to have a doctorate in the area of specialisation,” the NUC said.

It added that a candidate must spend at least three years in teaching, research, and community service at each of the ranks of Lecturer II, Lecturer I, Senior Lecturer, and Associate Professor, meaning a candidate would typically have about 12 years of university teaching and research experience before being considered for professorship.

A former Deputy Vice-Chancellor of the Federal University Gusau (FUGUS), Ahmad Galadima, a professor, also explained that the candidates’ academic achievements are first evaluated at the departmental level through the faculty, then by the university promotion committee.

These include publications, teaching load, quality of teaching, administrative experience, community service, and relationships with colleagues.

Afterwards, their CVs are sent to three high-ranking professors in their areas of expertise for “external assessment”.

“When the requirements are fully satisfied, their CVs are sent for external assessment,” Mr Galadima told PREMIUM TIMES. “Two positive responses are required to promote the staff to the rank.”

In some other countries such as the United Kingdom (UK), Mr Galadima said, the procedure is more stringent.

“Additional requirements like research grants acquired and quality of journal papers considered are top,” he added.

However, there is no evidence that Mr Kila taught at any university or authored any peer-reviewed academic journal.

Mr Kila’s Google Scholar page listed 22 works, including books, journal articles, book chapters and other works, but PREMIUM TIMES found that nine of the 22 records were not authored by Mr Kila.

Of the works actually attributed to Mr Kila, none could be independently established from the review as a peer-reviewed article in a reputable academic journal.

Three entries on the Google Scholar profile are listed as published in the Commonwealth Institute of Advanced and Professional Studies (CIAPS) Journal, a publication associated with an organisation he created.

In his ResearchGate profile, where he identified himself as a ‘full professor’, he listed no publications.

Non-existent institutions

In Mr Kila’s public biographies, he is repeatedly described as an international Director of Studies at the non-existent “European Centre of Advanced and Professional Studies”.

The European Centre for Advanced Studies (ECAS), the institution closest in name to Mr Kila’s so-called ECAPS, was established by the University of Glasgow and Leuphana University.

But the institution said it has no connection with Mr Kila.

“The European Centre for Advanced Studies has no knowledge of this person (Mr Kila),” its Academic Director, James Conroy, told PREMIUM TIMES in an email.

Kila’s suspicious academic claims

Although Mr Kila’s profiles did not state exactly which schools he attended, they listed several qualifications, including LLM, MBA, MSc, PhD, and PGCE.

“Anthony studied in Cambridge, London, Perugia, and Suffolk. He graduated with a first-class degree in political economy and later specialised in political anthropology. He has taught in various colleges and universities in Cambridge, Ipswich, Lecce, London, Perugia, and Siena,” his profile reads.

The newspaper sought Mr Kila’s comprehensive Curriculum Vitae, which would have provided details of the institutions he attended, qualifications obtained, his academic career, and where he obtained his professorship.

Mr Kila initially told PREMIUM TIMES that he did not have a CV readily available because he was no longer a young professional who needed one regularly.

“I don’t really have a CV handy,” he said in a message to our reporter. “I will find time to send you something.”

He subsequently provided a list of his academic qualifications.

He said he obtained a Bachelor of Arts (Honours) in Classic Studies from Università per Stranieri, Italy, in 1989, followed by a Master of Arts in European Studies from the same institution in 1991.

He listed a Postgraduate Diploma in Media and Communication from the University of Essex in 1992 and a Master of Science in International Banking and Finance from City University London in 1994.

According to the list, he obtained a Doctor of Philosophy in Political Economy from the University of Perugia in 1997, followed by a Master of Business Administration from Aston University, Birmingham, in 2002.

He also claimed to have obtained a Postgraduate Certificate in Higher Education from Cambridge in 2006 and a Master of Laws from Cambridge in 2009.

But even these claims contradicted his profiles on the website of his Commonwealth Institute of Advanced and Professional Studies (CIAPS), where he portrayed himself as having graduated with a first-class degree in political economy and later specialising in political anthropology. That claim was repeated on the website of the Michael and Cecilia Ibru University.

However, in a brief resume he shared with our reporter, he told a different story, saying his first degree was in Classical Studies from Università per Stranieri, Perugia, Italy. We are still investigating that claim.

The CIAPS website, through which Mr Kila made several suspicious claims about himself and his business, was unreachable in the past few days. That was after our reporter confronted him with our findings.

The website was repeatedly edited, with Mr Kila’s misleading profile initially removed, before it was eventually taken offline.

This newspaper is continuing investigations into the academic qualifications claimed by Mr Kila. The verification process has been slow because we are still awaiting responses from some of the institutions he claimed to have attended.

However, this newspaper clearly established his fake professorship, while its investigation into his claimed educational qualifications continues.

World.title: Extrajudicial Killings: How police’s Operation Zenda became dreaded by Benue residents
World.content:
Tse Angaador is a farming community about 182 kilometres from Makurdi, the Benue State capital. With an estimated population of about 3,000 residents, the village is in the Gaambe Tiev district of the Logo Local Government Area. The road linking it to the outside world is a narrow red earth track that cuts through cassava and yam fields.

In the early morning of 27 July 2024, the village’s men were concluding the Imôngu, an all-night Tiv traditional funeral rite. The ceremony was being held for Kumawuese Bam, a secondary schoolgirl who had died after an illness. The event was held in front of the bereaved family’s home.

Polycarp Yaapera attended the vigil with his younger brother, Aondoakura, a 34-year-old father of three.

“All of a sudden, I heard gunshots. When I turned, it was the police. I turned back and saw my brother, who was sitting next to me, fall to the ground,” Polycarp said.

He recalled diving behind a mud wall, where he hid for about five minutes until the shooting stopped. From a distance, he saw bodies lying on the ground. His brother, Aondoakura, was among the seven mourners who died.

The gunmen were members of an elite police unit codenamed “Operation Zenda.” The state police command had established the unit in 2008 to tackle rising cases of kidnapping, communal clashes, and boundary disputes in the volatile North-central state. However, Benue residents interviewed by PREMIUM TIMES described the unit as a source of fear, alleging extrajudicial killings, forced disappearances, and violent raids.

A mother bereaved twice

The bereaved mother, Helen Bam, was inside her room with some sympathisers when they heard the gunshots.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“One of the police officers came to my door and kicked it open,” she said. “Other officers joined him, and they started searching everywhere.”

Mrs Bam alleged that the officers took the ₦32,000 cash they found in her room and a smartphone belonging to one of her daughters.

Her son, Lubem, also died in the raid.

“My husband died in 2015 and left me with five children,” she said, her sorrow still heavy, two years later. “Now Kumawuese is gone. Lubem is gone.”

After the burial of the two children, Mrs Bam said she suffered a health episode that required hospitalisation. When PREMIUM TIMES visited Tse Angaador in January 2026, she said she may never recover from the tragedy.

“I do not sleep at night,” she said. “Anytime I see police, I want to ask them to kill me too.”

Where were the bodies taken?

The community’s head, Mbaveluior Yaapera, said the police took the bodies away after the shooting. He alleged that Akegh Ernest, the commander of Operation Zenda, led the team.

“They loaded their bodies into a Hilux van and drove away. We were too afraid to follow,” he said.

An eyewitness

PREMIUM TIMES also spoke with a resident who said he witnessed the bodies being deposited at a private mortuary in Ugba.

The police Hilux carrying the bodies arrived at about 6 a.m., but officers allegedly prevented onlookers from approaching the bodies.

“When police kill armed bandits, they usually display the bodies at Y Junction in Ugba, the headquarters of Logo LGA, for the public to see before taking them to the general hospital,” the eyewitness, who requested anonymity for fear of being targeted, said. “But that morning was different. They drove straight to a private mortuary instead of the general hospital.”

PREMIUM TIMES visited the mortuary, but an official who requested anonymity said he was not allowed to speak about bodies.

Following the shootings, Mr Yaapera said the community contacted Solomon Wombo, its representative in the House of Representatives, and Benjamin Uzenda, the chairman of Logo Local Government Area at the time.

At a meeting in Anyiin, the council boss reportedly told community representatives that the police regretted the killings.

“We were told the killings were an error from the police,” he said. “But they said if we insisted on taking it up and there was an attack by armed herders in future, security would not come to assist us.”

Mr Wombo later provided ₦500,000 to support the burial of the seven men, according to Mr Yaapera.

PREMIUM TIMES made several attempts to reach Mr Wombo by phone, but he did not answer or return the calls. The newspaper also sent him a WhatsApp message asking whether, beyond providing ₦500,000 for the victims’ burial, he had followed up on the circumstances surrounding the killings, engaged the relevant authorities to seek accountability, or taken any steps to prevent similar incidents. The message was delivered, but he did not respond.

PREMIUM TIMES also reached out to Benjamin Uzenda, who was chairman of Logo Local Government Area at the time of the incident, by phone and identified the subject of the report. Mr Uzenda acknowledged the call and agreed to meet the reporter in person later that day to discuss the July 2024 killings and the steps he took following the incident. However, the proposed meeting did not take place, and subsequent calls to Mr Uzenda went unanswered.

The community said the remains of the victims were buried on 10 August 2024 in Tse Angaador. They were identified as Ordughga Tyoapine, Kater Tarpav, Yaapera Ternenge, Nater Setim, Ioryevese Tarpav, Bam Lubem and Yaapera Aondoakura.

Another raid

Six months before the killings in Tse Angaador, another community in Logo Local Government Area witnessed a similar security operation.

At about 10 a.m. on 12 January 2024, a team of police officers arrived in Tse Jikina, Mbavuur Ward, about 31 kilometres from Tse Angaador. Residents said Akegh Ernest, then a divisional police officer in Logo, now commander of Operation Zenda, led the team into the community in two Hilux vans.

According to a resident, Tornyor Orkile, the officers’ mission was to arrest his brother, Iorhom Orkile, an herbal practitioner they accused of supplying charms to armed bandits in the Sankera axis. The suspect, Iorhom, told PREMIUM TIMES that the officers searched his compound without presenting a warrant.

“I am a registered member of the Nigeria Union of Medical Herbal Practitioners. I have not had any contact with bandits, nor have I provided charms to them,” he said.

Residents alleged that the officers assaulted them during the incident. Terpase Mbai said he was hit with a rifle butt, while Mbakaan Mbai said he was ordered at gunpoint to lead the officers to Iorhom’s house.

During a visit in January 2026, PREMIUM TIMES counted 25 burnt and abandoned houses in Tse Jikina.

Zuamo Tornyor, a student at the University of Maiduguri, said his family home was among those destroyed.

Court documents seen by PREMIUM TIMES show that Tornyor Orkile filed a suit against the police, Operation Zenda and its commander, Akegh Ernest. The case was later struck out after the judge handling it was transferred. Mr Orkile said he was pressurised to drop the case.

Death under Zenda

On 16 May 2022, nearly two years before the police raid on Tse Jikina and the killings in Tse Angaador, two brothers, Emmanuel and Terna Chado, were in Tor Mkar Mbazerem, Shangev Tiev, in Konshisha Local Government Area to watch a football match. After the game, Terna left Emmanuel in Tor Mkar Mbazerem and returned to his residence in Awajir.

Later that night, Emmanuel heard that Terna had been arrested after a phone call directed him to report at the local police station. The family said the arrest followed police tracking of phone calls involving Terna and several people, including Tersoo Bukem and Aondoakaa Akaakaa.

The family never saw Terna alive again.

In court documents reviewed by PREMIUM TIMES, the police claimed that Terna died in custody. Their account was that on 17 May 2022, he was taken along to arrest a suspect, Mr Bukem, when a stray bullet struck him during an exchange of gunfire.

The police also told the court that Terna was buried on 19 May 2022.

Court awards ₦50m

Another brother, Charles Chado, subsequently filed a fundamental rights enforcement suit at the Federal High Court in Makurdi, accusing the police of extrajudicial execution of Terna.

In suit No. FHC/MKD/CS/147/2023, Charles sued the Commissioner of Police, Benue State Command, Justin Gberindyer (the then commander of Operation Zenda) and two others.

On 15 March 2024, Justice R. J. Egbe delivered judgement against the police and awarded the family ₦50 million in compensation.

However, the family said it has not received the compensation. “To date, the Nigeria Police have not paid one kobo to our family,” Emmanuel said.

Terna left behind a son. For the Chado family, the judgement established a violation of its son’s right to life but did not answer the central questions about his death, including where the alleged gunfire occurred and why he was buried without the family’s knowledge.

Arrested, not seen again

Unlike Terna Chado, whose death was later confirmed in court, the fate of Paul Achov remains officially unresolved.

According to Ukan Kurugh, a human rights activist handling the case, the 27-year-old was arrested at City Bay, a relaxation spot in Makurdi, on 2 August 2025. Mr Kurugh said a police situation report he obtained labelled Mr Achov as a member of a criminal gang allegedly terrorising the Makurdi-Lafia highway. However, no evidence or formal charge was presented to his family.

In October 2025, the lawyer said he petitioned the Force Headquarters in Abuja, the National Human Rights Commission, and the Police Service Commission. He later received information from a police source that Mr Achov had been killed, a claim the lawyer challenged the police to disprove by accounting for the missing man.

Mr Achov’s younger sister, Ruth, 22, said officers at the Daudu Police Station initially claimed that he was detained over a shooting incident. She said when their cousin later returned to the station with food, he was told Mr Achov was not there.

“If they have evidence, they should charge him to court. If he is innocent, they should clear his name,” she said.

Ruth, who said she and Paul were orphans, said she last saw him on the day of his arrest. She said her brother is a Philosophy graduate of Benue State University who returned to farming and crop trading after failing to secure formal employment.

The family’s demand is simple: produce Paul Achov alive, charge him if there is evidence against him, or account for what happened to him.

Death of Philip Kpentemen

According to a family member who requested anonymity for safety reasons, Fanen Kpentemen was arrested at his workplace in Makurdi on 20 September 2025, over a complaint by a woman, Fatima Ameh, that she was defrauded through his WhatsApp account.

Ankyo Moses, whom the family identified as an Operation Zenda operative, allegedly led the team that arrested Mr Kpentemen.

“Fanen was arrested on a Friday, and by Saturday he was dead,” the family member said.

However, in a 26 September press statement, the police spokesperson, Udeme Edet, stated that Mr Kpentamen was arrested as an armed robbery suspect and had led Operation Zenda officers to a hideout at Tse-Tamen settlement, Ugondu, Makurdi, where they recovered a locally made pistol and five cartridges.

According to the police, the suspect later attempted to escape but was rearrested by local youths who lynched him before officers intervened. He said the suspect was taken to the teaching hospital, where a doctor confirmed him dead.

The family disputes the police account, and his death remains surrounded by conflicting accounts, including allegations of torture and questions over why his family was not promptly informed of his death.

Another death in custody

On 11 January 2026, Tordue Shapila, 35, was arrested at his family home in Apir village, Makurdi. His father, Christopher Shapila, said armed men who identified themselves as police Operation Zenda officers broke into the compound around 4 a.m. and arrested him and another man, Stephen Achoon.

For weeks, the family said investigating officer Solomon Mnyim denied them access to him, even though they continued taking food to the facility and were assured that he was in good health.

On 4 March, his lawyers, Hanaze, Wendeh and Associates, filed an application before the Chief Magistrate Court in Makurdi seeking his release or arraignment. Two days later, the court ordered the police to release him on bail or produce him in court within 24 hours.

The police did neither.

On 18 March, a lawyer following up at the Benue State Police Command was told that Mr Shapila had died. The police said he had been taken to Gboko during police investigation and was killed in an exchange of gunfire after suspected associates attacked officers. His body was reportedly deposited at the Benue State University Teaching Hospital mortuary.

The family rejected the account.

In a petition dated 23 March, the family’s lawyers demanded an investigation, an independent autopsy, his body for burial and ₦5 billion in compensation. They also threatened legal action against the police and officers linked to Operation Zenda.

Zenda commander

Operation Zenda Commander Ernest Akegh, a superintendent of police, denied wrongdoing when presented with allegations surrounding the unit and earlier operations in Logo, including the July 2024 killing of seven men in Tse Angaador.

“I want to assure you that any work I do, I do it in line with the law,” he told PREMIUM TIMES, defending his own records at the unit.

Mr Akegh said when a suspect dies during police operations, autopsies are conducted to determine the cause of death. However, he declined to provide medical or autopsy reports relating to the cases raised by PREMIUM TIMES, directing the requests to the police commissioner or the command’s public relations officer.

Police state their position

When contacted, Benue police spokesperson Udeme Edet said she was not the police spokesperson at the time of the July 2024 operation in Tse Angaador that resulted in the death of the seven young men.

“That question you are asking me; I will not be able to answer it because I was not here on the seat. I was not the PPRO,” she said.

On the 2025 death of Philip Fanen, she said the Benue State Police Command stands by its earlier public statement absolving the police of any culpability.

“Police made an official report concerning the matter,” she said.

When asked whether an autopsy was conducted and if PREMIUM TIMES could obtain a copy of the autopsy report, she replied, “I will get back to you later.” She did not provide any further response on the topic.

The spokesperson was also asked about the disappearance of Paul Achov, who was arrested in August 2025 and has not been seen by his family since then. She did not answer the question. She set a time for this reporter to call for a response but did not return the call or subsequent calls.

Government defers responsibility

The Director-General of the Bureau of Homeland Security, Jacob Gbamwuan, said allegations of extrajudicial killings involving security agencies were too serious for the state government to determine without a formal investigation.

“These are heavy allegations,” he said. “There must be a committee. There must be a body that will sit down and come to a conclusion that this is what is happening.”

When asked whether the government was willing to set up an investigative committee to examine the allegations, Mr Gbamwuan said any complaints would first have to be formally submitted and handled through the appropriate channels.

“If our Benue people have such complaints, such complaints will be taken up officially,” he said. “The position of such a committee will be the position that the government will adopt.”

He added that Operation Zenda operates under the Nigeria Police Force, which he said would be responsible for setting up any such committee.

READ ALSO: Police speak on alleged extrajudicial killings of citizens in their facility

“The police are even the ones who should set up that committee,” he said.

Lawyer demands accountability

Rommy Mom, a human rights lawyer and president of Lawyers Alert, said the allegations and other abuses must be investigated and those responsible sanctioned.

“When police officers carry out a wrong and go unpunished, it emboldens them to do worse,” he said.

Security funding

The Benue State Government has been spending more on internal security in recent years, as terrorism-related and other forms of violent criminality continue. The state allocated ₦9.27 billion to security in 2023, ₦12 billion in 2024 and proposed ₦15.60 billion for 2025.

As the government increases its security spending, questions persist over who is accountable for how those funds are used and whether the institutions funded to protect citizens are fulfilling that duty.

For families who say their loved ones were killed, disappeared, or died in police custody, the concern is that agencies funded to protect citizens do not become a source of fear and terror.

This report is with the support of the Centre for Journalism Innovation and Development (CJID) under a journalism support initiative funded by the Royal Norwegian Embassy.

World.title: Independence anniversary: Mbah pardons, commutes sentences of 13 inmates
World.content:
In commemoration of Nigeria’s 66th independence anniversary, Governor Peter Mbah of Enugu State has approved the pardon, release, and commutation of sentences of 13 inmates of the Nigerian Correctional Centres, Enugu State.

This is in the exercise of his power of Prerogative of Mercy under Section 212 of the 1999 Constitution (as amended) and in consultation with the Advisory Council on Prerogative of Mercy, Enugu State.

According to a statement released by the Mbah’s media aide, Uche Anichukwu, on Independence Day, the Governor’s approval was conveyed to the Comptroller, Nigerian Correctional Service, Enugu State Command by the Attorney General and Commissioner for Justice, Osinachi Nnajieze.

The beneficiary inmates are Kenneth Ozioko, Moses Saliyat, Promise Ndudim Olung, Chijioke Ugwu, Samuel Ani, and Eugene Odo.

Others are Celsus Emeachi, Caleb Jatto, Calistus Eze, Gabriel Onu, Timothy Ani, Ernest Okeke, and Ejike Nwodo.

While some of the inmates were pardoned and released, some had their death sentence commuted to life imprisonment.

Mbah’s decision was predicated on reports of ill health and or proven reform in character, and following recommendation by the Correctional Services to the Advisory Council on Prerogative of Mercy, chaired by the State Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Membership of the Council equally comprises representatives of the Nigerian Correctional Service, Carmelite Prisoners Interest Organisation (CAPIO), and the Catholic Institute for Development, Justice and Peace (CIDJAP), among other reputable bodies in the justice sector.

Section 212 (1) of the 1999 Constitution (as amended) provides that: “The Governor may (a) Grant any person concerned with or convicted of any offence created by any law of a state a pardon, either free or subject to lawful conditions; (b) grant to any person a respite, of the execution of any punishment imposed on that person for such an offence; (c) substitute a less severe form of punishment for any person for such an offence; or (d) remit the whole or any part of punishment for any punishment imposed on that person for such any offence or of any penalty forfeiture otherwise due to the state on account of such an offence.”

Section 212 (2), however, provides that the powers of the governor under subsection (1) shall be exercised after consultation with an advisory council of the state on the prerogative of mercy as may be established by law of the state.

World.title: Guber candidate offers free fuel to Okada, Keke operators in Gombe
World.content:
The African Democratic Congress (ADC) governorship candidate in Gombe State, Bala Tinka, provided free fuel to commercial motorcycle and tricycle operators as part of activities marking Nigeria’s Independence Day.

The one-day intervention, which was scheduled from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m. on Thursday, was implemented at designated filling stations in Gombe metropolis.

Mr Tinka had announced the initiative during an interview with a local radio station in Gombe monitored by our correspondent.

He said the gesture was intended to ease the financial burden on commercial transport operators, who he said had been affected by the rising cost of petrol.

“On October 1st, from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m., any Okada rider and Keke Napep operator should go to our designated filling stations and collect fuel free of charge,” Mr Tinka said.

He described the intervention as a modest way of joining Nigerians in celebrating Independence Day while providing relief to people struggling with increased transportation and fuel costs.

The ADC candidate also said the initiative could become part of a broader palliative programme if he is elected.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Beyond the fuel intervention, Mr Tinka outlined a number of policy proposals covering healthcare, agriculture, local contracting and water supply.

He promised free healthcare for children below five years and elderly people aged 70 and above, saying inability to pay medical bills should not prevent vulnerable residents from accessing treatment.

“We will provide free healthcare for our children under the age of five and for our elderly parents. No child should die because the parents cannot afford hospital bills, and no old person should be left to die,” he said.

On agriculture, Mr Tinka said a future ADC administration would review the procurement and distribution of fertiliser, with greater emphasis on local wholesalers and agro-dealers.

He argued that purchasing agricultural inputs from businesses operating within the state would keep more money in Gombe and stimulate economic activity.

“If we buy from local wholesalers, the money will stay in Gombe, it will circulate among our people and boost our local economy. That is how to grow Gombe,” he said.

The businessman also pledged to give qualified indigenous contractors greater opportunities in the execution of government projects.

According to him, contracts requiring specialised expertise not available in Gombe could still be awarded outside the state, but competent local professionals would receive preference where they have the capacity to deliver.

“We have competent engineers, builders and contractors in Gombe. We will patronise them to help our local experts grow. We will only go outside when it is absolutely necessary,” he said.

On the persistent water shortages affecting parts of Gombe metropolis and other communities, Mr Tinka said his administration would pursue what he described as a lasting solution rather than relying on temporary measures.

He proposed a comprehensive assessment of the causes of the water crisis before implementing measures to address the problem.

“Water is life, but our people have suffered for too long without water. We will not do temporary fixes. We will identify the root cause and bring an end to this perennial water scarcity in Gombe,” he said.

Mr Tinka emerged as the ADC governorship candidate for the 2027 election after the party’s primary held in May 2026.

He subsequently called on residents of Gombe State to support the ADC, promising an inclusive administration focused on improving the welfare of citizens if elected.

World.title: Police repel bandit attack in Sokoto, recover two rocket launchers
World.content:
The police in Sokoto State say they repelled an attack by suspected bandits on Tsabre village in Isa Local Government Area and recovered two rocket launchers abandoned by the attackers.

The attack occurred at about 1 a.m. on Friday, according to a statement by the police spokesperson in the state, Ahmad Rufa’i.

Mr Rufa’i said a large number of armed men entered the community and fired shots, causing panic among residents.

He said the divisional police officer in Isa mobilised tactical teams, including the Anti-Kidnapping Unit and the Violent Crime Response Unit, after receiving a distress call.

The security personnel engaged the attackers in a gun battle, forcing them to retreat into a nearby forest, the spokesperson said.

Mr Rufa’i said the attackers fled but did not disclose whether any of them were killed or how many were injured.

The statement also did not say whether any residents or security personnel were killed or injured during the attack.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

A search of the surrounding area afterwards led to the recovery of two rocket launchers and two empty AK-47 magazines, according to the police.

Other items recovered included a Tecno keypad phone without a battery, a torchlight, an army jungle hat, a sweater cap, five pairs of sandals and a rain jacket.

The police did not announce any arrest or provide details about the type and condition of the recovered rocket launchers.

The Commissioner of Police in Sokoto State, Hayatu Shaffa, commended the officers involved in the operation and urged residents to report suspicious activities.

He also asked members of the public to alert security agencies if they notice people with suspected gunshot wounds seeking medical attention.

World.title: UAE investigators say flydubai co-pilot was planning ‘terrorist act’
World.content:
An Israeli airline El Al aircraft is parked on the tarmac at Ben-Gurion Airport near the city of Lod on October 2, 2026. Israel’s flag carrier El Al said on October 2 it had cancelled repatriation flights from Dubai, which it had planned due to flydubai suspending service to Tel Aviv following an in-flight attack. (Photo by JACK GUEZ / AFP)





UAE investigators have said the co-pilot of a flydubai flight to Israel this week was planning a “terrorist act” and used the cockpit’s emergency axe to attack the captain, but they did not reveal his motive.

Initial findings from the UAE’s investigation into the attack also did not confirm his nationality, according to a report Saturday from the country’s state news agency WAM, but a Saudi source has confirmed to AFP that he was Omani.

Media reports have also said he had been barred from flying in his home nation over concerns about extremist views.

The reports came as the first flight carrying Israelis home from the United Arab Emirates landed in Tel Aviv after services were suspended following the attack, according to Israel’s airport authority website.

“The co-pilot had attempted to carry out a terrorist act” and had “attacked the captain in the cockpit with the emergency axe and tried to take control of the aircraft”, WAM quoted UAE Attorney General Hamad Saif Al Shamsi as saying, referring to initial findings of an investigation.

The co-pilot is still in custody in the UAE. Multiple media outlets overnight identified him as Omani national Hamam al-Hammami and said he had been banned from flying in Oman over concerns about his extremist views.

During the flydubai flight, the plane’s Indian captain was assaulted by the co-pilot but the captain managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers and crew to overpower the attacker and force an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.

Passengers described rushing the cockpit and a fight for control after the plane plummeted — losing around 17,000 feet of altitude in the span of a minute, according to the Flightradar24 website.

– ‘Radical indoctrination’ –

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said the suspect had undergone “Islamist radical indoctrination” and had attempted to crash the plane.

The Wall Street Journal reported Friday that Omani authorities had banned the pilot from flying over concerns he had adopted radical ideological views, citing people familiar with the matter.

CNN, citing two sources familiar with the matter, reported the pilot was removed from a job at Oman’s national airline last year over concerns about extremist views.

Al Arabiya, citing an informed source, also reported that Omani authorities determined that the co-pilot held extremist views.

The broadcaster said he had spent time in Syria, raising concerns he may have been influenced by radical groups there.

ABC News, citing senior intelligence and law enforcement officials familiar with the investigation, reported the suspect had allegedly been found in possession of extremist materials while he was a trainee.

US President Donald Trump warned on Thursday that if Iran was found to be linked to the attack the country would be “hit very hard”.

Netanyahu has said Israel would check how he had been cleared to work on flights to the country.

“We have constraints that say that you can’t have pilots from countries that don’t have diplomatic relations with Israel. Obviously he was able to go through that,” Netanyahu told Fox News.

World.title: FRSC confirms 20 dead in multiple crashes on Plateau route
World.content:
FILE IMAGE

The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) has confirmed the deaths of 20 people in a multiple road traffic crash along the Hawan Kibo-Jos route in Plateau.

The Corps Public Education Officer (CPEO), Mr Osondu Ohaeri, disclosed this in a statement issued on Friday in Abuja.

Ohaeri said the crash occurred at about 3:32 p.m. after Sopp Water Falls, with brake failure and loss of control identified as likely causes.

He said 25 people were involved in the crash, comprising 23 males and two females.

According to him, five people, comprising three males and two females, sustained injuries, while 20 males died in the crash.

“Four vehicles were involved in the crash, including a Howo Sino truck with registration number AGL 525 YN.

“Others were a Toyota Corolla with registration number AB 129 M and a Toyota Bummer bus operated by Yankari Express.

“The fourth vehicle was a motorcycle whose registration particulars were not available.

“The injured victims were evacuated to Ryom General Hospital and Vom Christian Hospital, while the deceased were deposited at JUTH Mortuary.

“FRSC rescue personnel also cleared the obstruction caused by the crash and restored the affected highway section to traffic,” he said.

Reacting to the incident, FRSC Corps Marshal, Malam Shehu Mohammed, expressed sadness over the loss of lives.

He extended his condolences to the families, friends and associates of the deceased and prayed for the repose of their souls.

Mohammed also wished the injured victims a speedy recovery and directed the crash investigation team to conduct a thorough investigation.

He said the investigation should establish the circumstances surrounding the incident, particularly the reported brake failure and loss of control.

The Corps Marshal urged motorists, especially commercial and heavy-duty vehicle operators, to prioritise roadworthiness, maintenance, speed management and responsible driving.

Mohammed further admonished drivers to exercise greater caution, stressing that the loss of 20 lives in one crash was not merely a statistic.

“The loss of 20 lives in a single crash represents 20 families suddenly plunged into grief. Behind every number is a name, a home, a family and a future,” he said.

Mohammed therefore urged all road users to take personal responsibility for safety, stressing that no journey was so urgent that it should end in death. (NAN)

World.title: Obasanjo, Jonathan, Gowon pay tribute to ex-Aso Villa chaplain William Okoye
World.content:
Okoye

Former President Olusegun Obasanjo has described the late Rev. William Okoye as a statesman of faith and fearless voice of truth.

Obasanjo stated this in a tribute read by Bishop Godwin Isaac at the Night of Tributes for Okoye, held at the National Christian Centre, Abuja, on Friday.
