Olayinka said the Nigerian stock market had performed exceptionally well during the nine-month period, but noted that the final three months of the period had witnessed some drag on the rally recorded in the first half of 2026.

“The outlook for the full year is positive, as a possible post-listing market-wide rally around Dangote Refinery IPO could be a step up to what the market witnessed in the first half of 2026. It is going to be an interesting market,” he said.

The market’s September performance provided further evidence of its resilience, with total market capitalisation rising by N5.37 trillion, or 3.4 per cent month-on-month, from N157.739 trillion at the end of August to N163.105 trillion at the end of September.

The renewed international attention on Nigerian equities has also been strengthened by the country’s return to frontier-market status under FTSE Russell.

Nigeria returned to the global index provider’s frontier-market classification on September 21, 2026, after a three-year absence.

Market participants expect the reclassification to improve the visibility of Nigerian equities among international institutional investors and potentially support additional capital inflows from funds tracking frontier-market benchmarks.

World.title: 2027: Akume, Wike Rally North-central, Rivers Support for Tinubu
World.content:
Olawale Ajimotokan in Abuja

The Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Senator George Akume and Minister of Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, have mobilised stakeholders from the North Central geopolitical zone and Rivers State towards the re-election of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and Vice President Kashim Shettima in the 2027 presidential election.



Akume, who is the Grand Patron of the North Central Grassroots Mobilisation Network and Wike yesterday were at different campaign trails in Abuja and Akpor Kingdom in Obio-Akpor Local Government Area of Rivers State to shore up the grassroots base for the President.

At a strategic meeting in Abuja with the National Chairman All Progressives Congress (APC), Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda and other political stakeholders and leaders of the mobilisation network, including Governor of Nasarawa State, Alhaji Abdullahi Sule and other political stakeholders, Akume said the initiative was designed to take the campaign for the President beyond the FCT and into communities across the North-central geo- political zone.



He said the North-central Grassroots Mobilisation Network was established to mobilise support and votes across the zone for the Tinubu-Shettima ticket.

The SGF equally outlined three major activities earmarked by the network to drive its mobilisation campaign.



These included the North Central Grand Rally, scheduled for October 10, 2026, in Lafia, Nasarawa State, a comprehensive medical outreach programme to be implemented across states in the zone and a North Central Grassroots Advocacy Tour and Town Hall Meetings covering the 19 senatorial districts across the six North Central states, as well as the FCT.

According to him, the medical outreach, to entail comprehensive eye screening and treatment, including refraction and prescription of spectacles, cataract assessment and selected surgical services where facilities permit, glaucoma screening and diabetic eye screening among the services to be provided is intended to complement the political mobilisation with humanitarian services for people at the grassroots.

He stated further that the advocacy tour and town hall meetings would provide an opportunity for direct engagement with communities across the North central.



The initiative, he said, was initiated by the National Coordinator of the network and the

Executive Secretary of the Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund), Sonny Echono, his team and other stakeholders and endorsed by the APC National Secretariat.

He urged political actors, ministers, governors, party stakeholders and grassroots leaders to approach the assignment with commitment, unity and confidence, stressing that the North-central is crucial in the 2027 electoral process.

He expressed confidence in the capacity of the region’s political structures and grassroots stakeholders to effectively organise and mobilise support for the President across communities in the zone.

In his remarks, Yilwatda stated that the North-central stakeholders had resolved to mobilise substantial support for President Tinubu ahead of the 2027 general election.



The stakeholders affirmed their commitment to working collectively across the six states of the zone and the FCT to strengthen grassroots mobilisation and demonstrate their solidarity with the President.

He said supporters and members of the APC would be mobilised from across the North-central to participate in the rally in Lafia and publicly demonstrate their support for the President, with plans for a medical outreach programme in selected communities across the zone.

He added that the stakeholders also resolved to establish a reconciliation committee to address grievances and promote unity among party members and political stakeholders across the North-central.



He said resolving internal differences would strengthen the mobilisation effort and enable stakeholders to work together ahead of the 2027 election. The group is expected to reconvene next week to intensify preparations for the Lafia rally and coordinate the broader grassroots mobilisation programme across the zone.



Echono said the mobilisation programme was aimed at uniting the North-central as a cohesive bloc while demonstrating the zone’s support for Tinubu ahead of the 2027 election.

He described the 2027 general election as an important opportunity for the geopolitical zone to strengthen its collective voice and advance its common interests within Nigeria’s political landscape.

The Chairman of the North Central Governors Forum and the Governor of Nasarawa State, Sule commended the SGF and the coordinator of the North-central mobilisation initiative for bringing stakeholders together toward ensuring the victory of the party in the forthcoming elections.

He stressed that the party has a political advantage to deliver for the APC with six states now under the APC and with a supportive Federal Capital Territory Administration, noting that the presence of the APC National Chairman and the SGF also provides additional institutional strength for the mobilisation effort.

Wike, at a strategic consultative meeting with stakeholders of the Akpor Kingdom, remarked that politics is driven by the collective interest of the people rather than perpetual animosity.

He declared that his political alignment with President Tinubu remains unshakable, rallying the political structure of Rivers State to consolidate support for the President.



He also reiterated his vow to resign as minister should the President lose FCT and Rivers.

“My interest in Rivers State is for God to use me as a vessel to help our people. I am back here not for what I will get, but for what I will be to raise my people,” Wike declared.

He maintained that expanding the political base was essential for delivering democratic dividends.

He said, “There is no permanent enemy in politics. What we have is permanent collective interest. It is all about the interest of our people. The more you are in number, the happier you become. Leadership is like a waste dustbin. If you cannot absorb things, both the good and the bad, then you cannot be a true leader.”

Wike, accompanied by the Rivers State APC governorship candidate, Kingsley Chinda and other political leaders, asserted that his return to grassroots mobilisation in Rivers State for Tinubu was to leverage his position as a vessel to uplift the state and its people.

“You know how difficult, you know how impossible it looked, but he made it possible for us to produce the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory,” Wike told the gathering.

He charged political actors in the state not to be distracted by social media criticism regarding his open-door policy toward former detractors, asserting that true political strength lies in numerical superiority.

World.title: PDP Candidate, APM Supporters, Accord Aspirant, 3,000 Others Join APC in Oyo
World.content:
The political landscape in Oyo State witnessed a major realignment yesterday as a wave of defections hit the camps of the governing Allied Peoples Movement (APM), the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and Accord, with a candidate, an aspirant and thousands of their supporters crossing over to the All Progressives Congress (APC).

The PDP candidate for Ibadan North East II State Constituency, Hon. Hammed Taoreed Ademola, abandoned his party’s ticket and led about 1,000 supporters into the APC, while a staunch loyalist of Governor Seyi Makinde in Oluyole Local Government Area, Hon. Mustapha Kazeem, popularly known as “Oba Oluyole,” also dumped the APM and joined the APC with more than 1,000 supporters.

Similarly, an Accord aspirant from Ibadan North East II, Hon. Adedapo Ojo, crossed over to the APC alongside hundreds of his supporters, with the defectors declaring their confidence that the APC would form the next government in Oyo State.

The first defection ceremony, held at a private facility on Old Ife Road, Ibadan, attracted several prominent APC stakeholders, including the state chairman, Moses Alake Adeyemo; the party’s governorship candidate, Senator Sharafadeen Alli; his running mate, Adesoji Adedeji; and the APC candidate for Oyo South Senatorial District, Hon. Aderemi Oseni, among others.

Speaking at the event, Ademola, popularly known as “Lucky,” said his decision to abandon the PDP ticket was informed by what he described as the political reality on the ground.

“I did my due diligence and came to realise that any ticket apart from the APC ticket is a mere tissue paper which cannot take a candidate anywhere in 2027.

“We are here in our hundreds to formally join the APC, and we promise to do our best in the interest of the progressive party and our dear country, Nigeria,” he said.

In his remarks, Ojo, otherwise known as “Bibire,” described Accord as a distraction, urging voters to keep faith with the APC.

“We thought about making Accord a credible alternative in the state, but we later realised that the APC is far ahead of the other parties.

“Without wanting to waste our time, energy and resources on an unproductive exercise, we decided to pitch our tent with the APC, and here we are today,” he said.

Addressing the new members, Adeyemo assured them of full integration into the APC and equal opportunities with existing members.

He urged them to immediately begin mobilising for the victory of all APC candidates in the 2027 general election, which he described as another opportunity for Nigerians to consolidate the gains of democratic governance.

Also speaking, Alli outlined aspects of his programme for Oyo State and pledged to run an inclusive administration that would treat all zones of the state fairly if elected governor in 2027.

“It is a thing of joy that reasonable individuals are abandoning their parties to join the APC at a time like this. The hope is getting brighter every day, and it is now important for us to get more prepared because Oyo State deserves the best from May 2027.

“We have been saying that we will run an all-inclusive government which every indigene and resident of the state will be proud of. Workers and pensioners will get their salaries and allowances regularly, and we will work towards ensuring that their earnings support a decent standard of living.

“The work environment will be conducive for all workers, including civil servants and teachers, while there will be training and retraining to improve their productivity.

“Within our first six months in office, a standard ICT hub will be established in Ibadan, and this will be replicated in Oke-Ogun, Ogbomoso, Oyo and Ibadan before January 2029.

“We will ensure that no zone is left out in the distribution of infrastructure and basic amenities. Each of the 33 local government areas will have a general hospital that is well staffed and equipped to cater for the basic medical needs of our people,” Alli said.

In a separate mass defection in Oluyole Local Government Area, more than 1,000 APM members announced the end of their political association with Governor Makinde and formally joined the APC.

The defectors, led by Mustapha Kazeem, popularly known as Oba Oluyole, were received at the APC secretariat in Oke-Ado, Ibadan, by the state chairman, Adeyemo, alongside other members of the State Executive Committee.

Speaking on behalf of the defectors, Kazeem criticised Makinde’s handling of political relationships and accused the governor of failing to adequately reward loyalty and sacrifice.

He said the group had consequently resolved to seek a new political platform in the APC.

“Governor Makinde is not the best person to work with in any political struggle because he does not appreciate loyalty, good human relations and sacrifice, despite being a beneficiary of a collective struggle.

“The few people who get empowered by the governor are even worse, as the one in Oluyole Local Government Area victimised most of us for more than seven years.

“It came to a point where we could no longer pretend, and this made us see the light in the progressive fold. It is an established fact that the APC is the only political party that is worth its name.

“APM is Governor Makinde’s private estate, and we cannot be part of it again. To this end, we are no longer interested in the deceit and propaganda which gave Makinde an unmerited mandate to rule us. We say enough is enough,” he added.

APC chairman in Oluyole Local Government Area, Dotun Oladipupo, formally presented the defectors to Adeyemo, who handed them brooms—the APC’s symbol—to signify their admission into the party.

Adeyemo urged the new members to put their previous political differences behind them and commit themselves to the APC’s programmes and electoral activities.

Other party leaders at the event included the APC State Secretary, Hon. Fatai Adesina; State Financial Secretary, Hon. Tunde Elegbede; Dr. Felicia Opatunde; Olawale Sadare; Olalekan Oladejo; Alhaji Lateef Akinsanya; APC candidate for Oluyole Federal Constituency, Hon. Tolulope Akande-Sadipe; and the party’s candidate for Oluyole State Constituency, Hon. Hakeem Lawal, among others.

World.title: Carte Blanche coming up: Autistic children left in the dark for weeks
World.content:
Carte Blanche investigates why hundreds of autistic children were left without electricity. Image: Video screenshot

The Sunday, 04 October episode of Carte Blanche investigates how hundreds of autistic children were left without electricity for three weeks at a centre specifically designed to support children with special needs.

The children were forced to cope in darkness as government departments reportedly squabbled over who should pay the electricity bill, raising questions about how the situation was allowed to continue for so long.

The investigation examines the impact of the prolonged power outage on the children and asks why their needs were seemingly not prioritised.



Credibility among South African viewers

Carte Blanche is a South African investigative journalism television series that airs on M-Net every Sunday at 19:00.

Its first episode aired on 21 August 1988 and over the last 34-plus years has earned credibility among South African viewers for its investigation into corruption, consumer issues, and current events.

World.title: SOLD OUT: MTN8 final between Orlando Pirates and Sundowns
World.content:
The Premier Soccer League (PSL) has announced that tickets for the MTN8 final between Orlando Pirates and Mamelodi Sundowns are sold out.

Pirates will take on Sundowns in what will be a repeat of the 2023 MTN8 final which was also played at Moses Mabhida Stadium.

Kick-off on Saturday, 10 October is at 18:00.



As reported by The South African, this will be the 11th MTN8 final hosted at the iconic Moses Mabhida Stadium.

And according to eThekwini Municipality City Manager Musa Mbhele, there are no bribes involved in terms of who hosts the finals.

Now, Sundowns are aiming to eliminate the memories of 2023 in what will be only their third MTN8 final at the venue.

In the last two finals, they won one (against Cape Town City in 2021) and lost one (against Orlando Pirates in 2023).

Sundowns were involved in a penalty shout-out in both finals while Pirates won three of their seven MTN8 finals at Moses Mabhida Stadium in 90 minutes.

World.title: Sharks vs Leinster: Who are the ‘Durban’ WAGS?
World.content:
The Sharks host reigning United Rugby Championship champions Leinster at Hollywoodbets Kings Park on Saturday 3 October. Who are the women backing the boys in black?

THE SHARKS VS LEINSTER

The Sharks clash against Leinster kicks off at 18:30 SAST. It is now round two of the URC, and coach JP Pietersen welcomed back six Springboks. André Esterhuizen returns from international duty to captain the side. Thomas du Toit starts at loosehead. Ox Nché and Eben Etzebeth are among the replacements.

Leinster arrive in Durban after a narrow opening-round defeat to the Lion. Hooker Rónan Kelleher is leading the team. Vusi Moyo is at flyhalf and faces one of the biggest tests of his young career against the champions. Lock Jason Jenkins will also have extra motivation, as he is a former Leinster player. Take a look at the weather for today’s game here.



So, who are the ladies backing the boys in black tonight?

MEET THE SHARKS WAGS

ANLIA ETZEBETH

Singer and actress Anlia Etzebeth is the wife of Eben Etzebeth. The couple tied the knot after he moved from France to join The Sharks in Durban. The pair have two beautiful daughters together.



MABEA ESTERHUIZEN

Mabea is the wife of the Sharks captain, Andre Esterhuizen, who was recently named Springbok captain for the Test against Australia in Perth. The couple are raising three children and are reportedly planning a coastal home in the Umhlanga and Sibaya area north of Durban.



JANDRE KOCH

Vincent Koch and his wife Jandré Koch have been together for around 15 years and married for about eight years. They have two children: son Luca and daughter Jané; Luca has already started playing rugby.



NADINE VAN DER MERWE

Edwill van der Merwe and Nadine van der Merwe married on 16 December 2023 in an intimate wedding ceremony in Cape Town. They had been dating since 2014 and became engaged in September 2021. The pair have one child together.



LOU-MARIE JENKINS

Jason Jenkins is married to Lou-Marie Taljaard. The pair got engaged in November 2023 and married in July 2024 at Zorgvliet Wine Estate in the Cape Winelands. Lou-Marie is a model who now goes by Lou-Marie Jenkins following their wedding.

World.title: Mnangagwa reveals what made Chivayo’s death a national loss
World.content:
Zimbabwe President Emmerson Mnangagwa has visited the Chivayo family home in Gletwyn, Harare, to offer his condolences following the deaths of businessman Wicknell Chivayo, his wife Lucy “Lulu” Muteke-Chivayo and three others in a helicopter crash.

Mnangagwa said he was accompanied by senior government officials when he visited the family home, where he expressed his “deepest personal condolences” to the bereaved family.

The visit came after the fatal helicopter crash in rural Marondera on Wednesday afternoon, which left the nation mourning.



Mnangagwa pays tribute to Chivayo

In a statement, Mnangagwa described Chivayo as a man who had a “grand vision” for his family, Zimbabwe and the wider African continent.

The President also highlighted the Chivayo family’s philanthropic activities, saying their generosity had touched lives in several sectors.

According to Mnangagwa, the family’s contribution extended across public service, religion, culture and sport.



His comments add to the growing tributes following the death of the prominent businessman, who was widely known for his high-profile lifestyle, business interests and charitable activities.

Mnangagwa also mourned Lucy Muteke-Chivayo, who died alongside her husband in the crash.

Three others also remembered

The President said the country was also mourning the two crew members and a security aide who died in the helicopter accident.



“During this moment of profound heartbreak, we stand together in unity, compassion, and prayer with the bereaved families,” Mnangagwa said.

He described the accident as a tragedy that had left the nation “numbed and in deep shock and grief.”

The deaths have prompted an outpouring of condolences from Zimbabweans and prominent figures across the region.



The helicopter crashed in the Marondera area on Wednesday afternoon.

Authorities confirmed that there were no survivors.

The cause of the crash remains under investigation.



Meanwhile, funeral proceedings for the Chivayo family have shifted to the family’s Gletwyn residence, where relatives, friends and associates have gathered to mourn.

Mnangagwa concluded his message by praying for comfort for the bereaved families and for the souls of those who died to rest in eternal peace.

World.title: RIP: SA musician Babsy Mlangeni dies aged 83
World.content:
South African musician Babsy Mlangeni has died at the age of 83 after suffering a short illness.

RIP: BABSY MLANGENI DIES AT 83

South Africa is mourning Babsy Mlangeni, the celebrated singer, guitarist and composer who has died at 83. Mlangeni’s passing comes after suffering a short illness. He reportedly passed away on Thursday night 1 October.

He was born as Bernard Mlangeni in Orlando East, Soweto, in 1943. Mlangeni lost his sight as a child. He went on to attend the Athlone School for the Blind in Bellville, Western Cape, where he learned to play the guitar. That instrument carried him through a career spanning nearly six decades, at a time when visually impaired musicians faced significant barriers.



In 1962 he became a founding member of the All-Rounders. Their 1967 debut album, Coming Home, helped define a sound later known as South African soul. He then built a household name as a solo artist, with hits including Sala Emma, Bua Nnete, Botsotso, Umadlembathini and Special Angel. Sala Emma, reportedly inspired by his wife, became a South African classic. His music crossed language lines, with songs in isiZulu, isiXhosa and Setswana.

He received a South African Music Awards Lifetime Achievement Award in 2017, and another Lifetime Achievement Award at the National Arts and Culture Awards in 2025.

TRIBUTES POUR IN FOR THE LATE MUSICIAN

Tributes have poured in from across the country. President Cyril Ramaphosa also paid tribute to the musician,

“Heartfelt condolences to his family, fans and the music fraternity. uBaba Mlangeni leaves us with a catalogue of hits like Sala Emma and other creations that made him an icon and inspired the creative sector in our country during the course of six decades. We pay tribute to the soothing and beautiful tunes he contributed in many languages to our musical heritage as we remember his outstanding talent and creativity,” read the tweet.

With Heritage Month still ringing in our ears, it is a particularly sad moment for us to acknowledge the passing of our beloved township soul pioneer Babsy Mlangeni, aged 83.



Heartfelt condolences to his family, fans and the music fraternity.



uBaba Mlangeni leaves us with a… pic.twitter.com/PBPcUFek9x — Cyril Ramaphosa 🇿🇦 (@CyrilRamaphosa) October 2, 2026

Gauteng MEC for Sport, Arts, Culture and Recreation Lebogang Maile said Mlangeni’s music became part of the “soundtrack of the lives of generations of South Africans”.



MEC Lebogang Maile sends condolences on the passing of music legend, Babsy Mlangeni.#RIPBabsyMlangeni pic.twitter.com/8jbzUPYTBz — Gauteng Dept. of Sport, Arts, Culture & Recreation (@GautengSACR) October 2, 2026

Deputy Minister of Sport, Arts and Culture Peace Mabe described him as part of the living history of the creative sector. The South African Music Rights Organisation (SAMRO) called him an influential voice in South African music. Maile also credited him as a mentor to younger artists, including the late falsetto star Steve Kekana.

Away from the stage, Mlangeni challenged assumptions about disability and inspired other visually impaired artists. Fans have also sent their condolences to the family and celebrated his life.

World.title: Weather Report: Disruptive rain and thunderstorms across the Cape
World.content:
Severe thunderstorm and disruptive rain warnings are active across the Northern, Western and Eastern Cape today. Image: ChatGPT

Saturday, 3 October’s Weather Report shows a real contrast across the country.

The interior enjoys a mild, mostly dry day, while the Northern Cape, Western Cape and Eastern Cape all face disruptive rain and thunderstorms.

The South African Weather Service (SAWS) has issued a Yellow Level 2 warning for severe thunderstorms and disruptive rain, covering the eastern parts of the central and eastern Northern Cape, the Beaufort West Municipality in the Western Cape, and the western parts of the Eastern Cape.



Gauteng enjoys a mostly clear day.

Johannesburg climbs from a chilly 9°C to a pleasant 22°C.

Pretoria is the warmest spot in the province, reaching 23°C, while Soweto and Vereeniging both sit at 22°C.

WHERE TODAY’S INTERIOR STAYS DRY AND MILD

North West stays partly cloudy and cool, turning cloudy in the afternoon with isolated showers and thundershowers in the west.

Mahikeng climbs from 10°C to 24°C under cloudy skies, while Rustenburg reaches 25°C.

The Free State stays overcast for much of the day.



Bloemfontein ranges from 10°C to 23°C, with Bethlehem reaching 24°C and a chance of slight rain.

Limpopo enjoys mostly clear skies. Polokwane climbs from 9°C to 19°C, while Tzaneen and Musina both reach 23°C.

Mpumalanga also stays mostly clear.

Mbombela climbs from 10°C to 21°C.

WHY THE THREE CAPE PROVINCES FACE TODAY’S HEAVIEST RISK

The Northern Cape sees showers and thundershowers across much of the interior.

Kimberley climbs from 13°C to 22°C, Upington reaches 25°C, and De Aar sits at 22°C. SAWS warns that heavy downpours, hail, excessive lightning and gusty winds could cause localised flooding of settlements, roads and bridges over the eastern parts of the province.

The Western Cape stays partly cloudy.

Cape Town sits between 13°C and 18°C, Stellenbosch reaches 18°C, and Paarl climbs to 20°C.

George faces slight rain. The same severe thunderstorm and disruptive rain warning applies specifically to the Beaufort West Municipality.

The Eastern Cape faces the wettest day of the weekend. Gqeberha sees rain showers with an 80% chance of rain, ranging from 15°C to 18°C.

East London holds steady around 20°C, with a 60% rain chance.

SAWS warns the disruptive rain here could cause localised flooding of settlements, roads and bridges, persisting into Sunday.

KwaZulu-Natal faces a warm but stormy day.

Durban sees showers and thundershowers, ranging from 18°C to 23°C. Richards Bay climbs to 29°C, while Newcastle stays partly cloudy at 25°C.

It’s a genuinely split weekend forecast, dry and mild inland, wet and disruptive along the Cape coastline.

Worth keeping a close eye on local updates if you’re anywhere near the Northern Cape, Western Cape or Eastern Cape today.

Are you in one of today’s warning areas, and how are you preparing?

World.title: SASSA pensioners asked for R5 000, got nothing instead
World.content:
The bad news is official for SASSA pensioners. The October payment date – Friday 2 October 2026 – has rolled through and, for the first time in two years, there was no top-up. It’s an even harder landing after what highly active pensioner groups had been marching for.

Numerous marches on parliament this year have seen SASSA pensioners pushing for R5 000 a month. It’s a ballpark even the EFF’s Julius Malema echoed on his campaign trail, pledging R4 500. And despite total silence from the agency, many were still hopeful an October top-up might still materialise at the eleventh hour …

DEVASTATION FOR SASSA PENSIONERS

What SASSA pensioners got instead was … nothing. Their grants sit exactly where they were in April 2026: R2 400 for beneficiaries aged 60 to 74 and R2 420 for 75 and older. Worse still, the R80 increase earlier in the year barely stretched far enough to begin with. Followed by war in the Middle East, SASSA Old-Age Grant recipients have watched the cost of living outpace that miserly bump month after month.



However, there might be a reason to look ahead to something other than dread. Running the Treasury’s own published numbers reveals something encouraging. That is, if South African Social Security Agency sticks to its current plan, next year’s increase could offset the October bummer. Here’s how Treasury sees its Old-Age Grant budget and beneficiary numbers:

2025: R115.7 billion budget, 4.19 million beneficiaries

budget, beneficiaries 2026: R121.8 billion budget, 4.26 million beneficiaries

budget, beneficiaries 2027: R129.6 billion budget, 4.33 million beneficiaries

WHAT COULD THIS MEAN FOR SASSA PENSIONERS?

Is new SASSA minister Dina Pule to blame for the total inactivity around increases? Image: File

What matters here is the gap between how fast the budget grows and how fast the beneficiary count grows. It is this gap that effectively funds the actual per-person increase. In 2026, the budget grew by roughly 5.14%, against beneficiary growth of just 1.60% – that’s a gap of 3.54 percentage points. However, for 2027, figures suggest budget growth of 6.20% against beneficiary growth of only 1.62% – therefore a wider gap of 4.58 percentage points.

Extrapolating those percentages could mean an increase of roughly R100, pushing the SASSA Old-Age Grant to around R2 500 for those 60 to 74, and R2 520 for those 75 and older, in April 2027. None of this is confirmed, of course. And for an agency that cannot even rectify the date clash with November 4 elections, five months is long enough for anything to happen …



But what do you think? Are SASSA pensioners entitles to R5 000 per month, do you think? Please share your thoughts in the comments section below …

World.title: Several Johannesburg areas set to have a 10-hour water outage
World.content:
Johannesburg Water will interrupt the water supply to Stretford and Orange Farm, including all extensions, on Tuesday, 13 October 2026. The outage will run from 8:00 to 18:00, leaving residents with low pressure or no water for up to 10 hours. The utility announced the planned maintenance in its daily water supply status update for 2 October.

The interruption will affect all streets in Stretford and Orange Farm, including every extension. Both areas fall under Johannesburg Water’s Region G, which covers the city’s southern parts. Residents can expect anything from low water pressure to no water at all during the outage.

Johannesburg Water says the work involves a dummy run for the tie-in of new infrastructure. The new infrastructure is part of a project to relocate existing services. The utility says the work will bring improved service delivery and more reliable water supply in the area once it is complete.



Johannesburg Water: Prepare before the taps run dry

Households should store enough clean water for drinking, cooking and basic hygiene before 08:00 on Tuesday. Filling containers, bottles and buckets the night before can help families get through the day. Residents should also store water for flushing toilets, since the outage covers most of the working day.

Johannesburg Water will only provide an alternative water supply if the dummy run takes longer than 24 hours. Residents should therefore not expect water tankers during the planned 10-hour window. Schools, clinics and businesses in the affected areas may also need to make their own arrangements.

How to report problems

Residents who experience problems during or after the outage can log a call with Johannesburg Water. The utility’s contact numbers are 010 061 4470 and 086 056 2874. Residents can also send an email to Fault@Jwater.co.za.

World.title: How Are South African Women Supposed to Trust the System?
World.content:
There is something deeply unsettling about being a woman in South Africa right now.

We are repeatedly told that our safety matters. We are told that government is listening. We are told that more resources will be allocated, that the police will do more, that cases will be prioritised and that the law will be strengthened.

But for how long are women expected to keep hearing the same promises while the fear remains?

On Tuesday, President Cyril Ramaphosa addressed the nation about the government’s response to gender-based violence and femicide, following the discovery of the bodies of 11 women in Ekurhuleni since July. His address came in the same period that suspended Deputy National Police Commissioner Lieutenant-General Shadrack Sibiya appeared in the Randburg Magistrates’ Court facing five charges, including rape, sexual grooming of a minor and trafficking in persons. The allegations involve a 16-year-old girl and an 18-year-old woman. Sibiya has denied the allegations and has told the court that his sexual encounter with the 18-year-old was consensual.

How are women supposed to trust the people and institutions tasked with protecting them when a senior police official is himself before a court on serious sexual-offence charges?

This is not about declaring Sibiya guilty before the court has reached a decision. He is entitled to due process. But the allegations alone raise an uncomfortable question about trust in institutions that are supposed to protect women and children.

The police are one of the first places survivors are expected to turn to. We are told to report abuse, report threats, report missing people and trust that the criminal justice system will respond.

But trust is not created through speeches. It is created when a woman reports abuse and is taken seriously. It is created when evidence is processed on time. It is created when case dockets do no not disappear. It is created when a protection order actually protects someone.

President Ramaphosa himself acknowledged that what has been done has not been enough. In his address, he pointed out that seven years ago, in September 2019, he stood before the nation to speak about the same crisis.

That is long enough for a child to grow into a teenager. Long enough for a teenager to become a young woman. Long enough for families to bury daughters, sisters, mothers and friends while another generation grows up hearing that they must simply be careful.

And that is perhaps where the problem lies.

Women are being told to be careful.

Don't walk alone.

Don't walk at night.

Don't trust strangers.

Watch your drink.

Share your location.

Check your surroundings.

Get home before dark.

But how much more can women change their lives to accommodate the violence of men?

At some point, the question has to shift from “What can women do to stay safe?” to “What are institutions and society doing to stop men from harming women?”

The President announced several measures in his address. Government says more resources will be allocated through the Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement. Sexual Offences Courts are being expanded, forensic and DNA processing is being strengthened, and the law has been tightened to make it more difficult for perpetrators of gender-based violence and domestic abuse to obtain bail.

He also directed the police and Justice Department to conduct a national case-recovery operation focusing on unresolved murders, attempted murders, rape and serious sexual offences involving women and children. Within 60 days, government must identify unresolved cases, cases awaiting forensic evidence, cases where suspects have been identified but not arrested, and cases where investigations or prosecutions have been unreasonably delayed.

There will also be women's safety audits to identify broken streetlights, overgrown public spaces, abandoned buildings, unsafe transport routes and poorly secured parks. Government says the results will be published so communities can see what has been identified, what has been fixed and what remains outstanding.

These are important commitments.

But South African women have heard commitments before.

In 2019, government spoke about strengthening the criminal justice system, addressing case backlogs and delays in DNA testing, improving rape kits and increasing resources to fight gender-based violence.

So this time, the question should not only be: What is government promising?

It should be: How will we know that it has happened?

If there is going to be a 60-day audit, South Africans must be able to see the results. If there are unresolved rape and murder cases, communities deserve to know whether those cases are moving. If there is a forensic backlog, we need to know whether it is actually being reduced. If municipalities identify dangerous public spaces, we need to see whether those spaces are being fixed.

Because a promise without implementation eventually becomes another speech.

The President said that visible policing in Ekurhuleni has been significantly increased. But even he acknowledged that the country cannot simply “police our way out” or “arrest our way out” of gender-based violence. Prevention has to happen before a woman is murdered.

Women should not have to become prisoners of precaution simply because the country has failed to make them safe.

The President said no woman should have to calculate where she can walk, what time she can travel, what she can wear, whom she can trust or whether saying no could put her life in danger.

That should not be a presidential speech.

It should be the reality of being a woman in South Africa.

Seven years after government first stood before the nation to confront this crisis, we should not still be asking women to wait for change.

We should be able to see it.

Because South African women do not need another reason to be angry.

They need a reason to feel safe.

By Dikeledi Ramabula

World.title: Record fuel prices in October now unavoidable
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - A fuel price shock for motorists next week is now unavoidable.

The latest data suggests that petrol will push higher than R30 per litre for the first time in history and diesel will also reach a record high.

A combination of higher oil prices and a weaker Rand is waging war on the pockets of consumers.

Data from the Central Energy Fund suggests an increase of R3.29 for 95 unleaded petrol and R3.19 for lower sulphur diesel.

95 unleaded petrol rose to a new record above R28 per litre in June this year before stabilising.

It's now set to rise to just above R30 per litre in Gauteng.

Diesel hit a record price above R31 per litre in May, and it's now set to soar to a new record of R33.24.

Brent crude oil has fallen today by around 3% to trade below $100 per barrel but that won't put the brakes on next week's price hike.

Fuel prices change on the first Wednesday of each month.

World.title: Beyond Game Day | Why Are South African Sports Bodies in So Much Trouble? | 02 October 2026
World.content:
South African Sport's Next Competitive Edge Is Better Governance

South African sport does not have a talent problem. The more uncomfortable question is whether its institutions are consistently good enough to convert that talent into sustained success.

That distinction matters because the health of a sporting system is easy to misread from the scoreboard. A national team can win while its development pipeline is weak. An exceptional athlete can succeed despite poor administration. A federation can produce medals while simultaneously fighting leadership disputes, disciplinary battles or financial pressure. Results can hide institutional weakness for a surprisingly long time.

That tension runs through the latest Beyond Game Day conversation between Thabiso Sithole and Vata Ngobeni. Their discussion moves from young South African footballers needing meaningful senior opportunities to Springbok squad depth and Temba Bavuma's leadership. But beneath those different sports sits one recurring idea: performance depends on the quality of the system surrounding the athlete.

Recent developments make the governance question difficult to dismiss. SASCOC president Barry Hendricks was suspended in September pending an internal judicial process after an investigation found prima facie grounds for complaints to be referred further. SASCOC stressed that the suspension was not a finding of wrongdoing and that due process must run its course.

The problem is that this is not an isolated governance story. Swimming South Africa president Alan Fritz and CEO Shaun Adriaanse were provisionally suspended by the Aquatics Integrity Unit in August, while Athletics South Africa president James Moloi has remained suspended through disciplinary proceedings concerning alleged misuse of a federation credit card. Again, allegations and suspensions are not convictions. But the accumulation of leadership disputes across major codes creates a wider institutional question.

Governance failures eventually reach the field because sporting bodies make decisions about selection structures, funding, development pathways, coaching, safeguarding and international participation. When leadership becomes consumed by internal disputes, those functions compete for attention with disciplinary hearings, legal costs and organisational survival.

The financial environment makes that even more important. SASCOC reported a R25.67-million deficit for the financial year ending March 2026 after revenue fell sharply from the previous year. At its September AGM, acting president Lwandile Simelane identified funding, infrastructure and safeguarding among the challenges facing the sector.

That is why governance should not be treated as the boring administrative layer sitting beneath “real sport”. It is part of performance infrastructure.

The same principle applies to player development. Producing a talented junior generation means little if clubs do not give those players competitive minutes. Building Springbok depth requires exposing combinations to pressure rather than merely assembling them in training. Leadership recognition matters because culture is shaped by whose contribution institutions choose to value. Those are sporting questions, but they are also systems questions.

South Africa has enough sporting talent to create moments of excellence almost regardless of the structures around it. The bigger ambition should be to build institutions capable of making excellence repeatable.

Winning despite the system is inspiring. Winning because the system works is a far stronger model.

Catch up on all previous Beyond Game Day episodes here: https://www.enca.com/beyond-game-day-podcast

World.title: King Charles to evoke colonial 'darkest days' on Caribbean tour
World.content:
LONDON - King Charles III will acknowledge the "darkest days" of colonial rule and slavery while touring Caribbean countries on a visit beginning this month, a Buckingham Palace spokesperson said Friday.

The king will first visit the Bahamas and Guyana alone, followed by a trip to Antigua and Barbuda with Queen Camilla, where Charles will give a speech at a meeting of Commonwealth heads of government, the palace said.

Charles, 77, who is still receiving treatment for cancer, will visit former colonies that are now independent from Britain and are members of the British Commonwealth.

He remains head of state in the archipelago nations of the Bahamas and Antigua and Barbuda, a role that is largely ceremonial.

The palace spokesperson told reporters the king's visit, from October 27 to November 4, would not "shy away from the 'darkest days of our past' as His Majesty has described them".

Charles used the phrase in a speech in Barbados when he attended the ceremony in which it became a republic in 2021, removing his mother, Queen Elizabeth II, as head of state.

He also said then that the "appalling atrocity of slavery" stains Britain's history.

The palace said Charles had worked to acknowledge "the wrongs of the past" and "right inequalities that endure", and on this trip would "renew his personal, wholehearted and continuing commitment to that process".

The UK government reiterated last month its rejection of calls for the payment of slavery reparations after a Jamaican delegation filed a petition addressed to Charles on the issue.

It called on the monarch to refer three questions on the legality of the transatlantic slave trade to the Caribbean island's highest court of appeal based in London.

Modern British royals have expressed remorse for the brutal slave trade that enriched their ancestors, but like the UK government have not issued an official apology for the slave trade.

The palace said discussions about the colonial legacy and the slave trade were "important" but "primarily matters for governments to address".

On a 2022 Caribbean tour, Charles's son William and his wife Kate were met with anti-monarchy protests and calls for slavery reparations.

Charles's younger brother, Prince Edward, later that year cancelled a visit to Grenada after pro-republican protests there.

In Antigua and Barbuda, a state named after its two main tropical islands, the royals will attend a parade to mark 45 years of independence.

Guyana, the only English-speaking country in South America, is a republic and so Charles will be making a state visit on the 60th anniversary of its independence from Britain.

The trip will feature plenty of meetings with local people and will focus on "the vibrant present and promising future of each country", the palace said.

The programme includes meetings with cricketing legends in Antigua and Barbuda, where the West Indies team is based, and meeting conservationists responsible for Guyana's rain forest.

World.title: England's Carse charged by cricket body over nightclub incident
World.content:
LONDON - England bowler Brydon Carse has been charged with breaching the England and Wales Cricket Board's (ECB) conduct regulations following a nightclub incident.

The charge, which follows an investigation by England's Cricket Regulator, refers to events that took place on August 23 when Carse was handcuffed by police officers after a celebratory night out in Derby with his Durham teammates.

It was later confirmed he had been arrested on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly before being "de-arrested" after agreeing to depart.

Derbyshire Police had said they were investigating an alleged assault in connection with the incident but in September determined no further action would be taken.

"Following a Cricket Regulator investigation, Brydon Carse has been charged with breaching regulation 3.2 of the ECB professional conduct regulations," said a statement from the compliance body.

In the aftermath of the incident Carse was withdrawn from the England squad for the second Test against Pakistan and has not played international cricket since.

"I think he just needs time away from the international scene," England white-ball captain Harry Brook said last month.

"He's working on a few things behind the scenes and hopefully he'll be ready at some point in the future."

Carse's misdemeanour was the latest in a series of alcohol-fuelled controversies that have dogged England since a disastrous tour of New Zealand and Australia at the end of last year.

Test captain Joe Root said he had been "hacked off" that the Carse incident took attention away from his winning return as skipper against Pakistan.

On Thursday, Carse was left out of the squad for the one-day tri-series against Pakistan and Sri Lanka later this month.

World.title: Amazon vows $1 bn for data center towns, decries 'myths'
World.content:
VIRGINIA - Amazon on Friday pledged more than $1 billion over five years for US communities that host its data centers, the latest tech giant seeking to win over residents increasingly hostile to the AI-fueled construction boom.

The "Built Together" program, unveiled by Amazon Web Services chief Matt Garman in a 3,000-word blog post, will fund free community college degrees and trades training as well as energy-efficiency upgrades for schools and homes.

The company also announced a "Data Center Commitment," promising that its facilities will not drive up local electricity bills and that it will publish annual figures on energy and water use.

Garman said AWS would stop using nondisclosure agreements with government agencies on its projects, a practice that has become a major flashpoint for the movement opposing data centers.

Microsoft made a similar move in March, the first major tech firm to do so.

Garman cast the buildout as a national security imperative on par with the 1950s interstate highway system.

He warned that with more than 100 local moratoriums under consideration nationwide, the United States "could be writing its own losing ticket" in the AI race and that "the consequences would last generations."

He also took aim at what he called myths about data centers, disputing as false arguments that they drive up power costs, deplete water supply and cause pollution from diesel fumes.

Citing "widespread reports," Garman said some countries were deliberately seeding misinformation in the United States to slow construction, an argument also made by the Trump administration.

Disinformation researchers and fact-checkers say such claims overstate the role of foreign influence campaigns in a grassroots movement that spans the political spectrum and nearly every US state.

President Donald Trump, a vocal champion of the buildout, has warned that communities rejecting the facilities would "end up being backwards and poor."

Amazon's rivals have made similar overtures.

In January, Microsoft pledged to fully cover its data centers' power costs and stop requesting local tax breaks, and OpenAI promised that its Stargate data centers would not raise local electricity prices.

In March, Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, Oracle and xAI signed a White House pledge to provide their own power for new data centers and pay for any grid upgrades they require.
