World.title: US Treasury approves waiver for Iranian flights to Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Minister of Foreign Affairs Fuad Hussein announced on Friday, October 2, 2026, that U.S. Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent has agreed to exempt religious pilgrimage flights to holy sites in Iraq from secondary sanctions imposed on Iranian aviation, following intensive bilateral talks held in Washington.

The decision resolves mounting diplomatic friction surrounding the status of Najaf International Airport, granting legal clarity for passenger arrivals while shielding Iraqi aviation infrastructure from punitive measures.

In a statement shared on X (formerly Twitter) and reported by the 964 Network, Hussein outlined that discussions with Bessent encompassed the overarching trajectory of U.S.-Iraqi economic and security ties, regional fiscal stability, and the spillover impacts of American sanctions enforcement on the domestic Iraqi economy.

Hussein specifically raised the operational paralysis facing Najaf International Airport—a vital national transport hub serving millions of international religious pilgrims annually—emphasizing that economic restrictions should not impede lawful civilian travel or religious observances. Secretary Bessent acknowledged Iraq’s sovereign concerns, formally approving a targeted waiver for flights directed toward the holy shrines.

During the diplomatic session, Hussein reaffirmed Baghdad’s appreciation for past U.S. and International Coalition support in the campaign to defeat Daesh (ISIS), while reiterating the federal government’s constitutional roadmap under Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi to monopolize arms under the state and maintain sole authority over war and peace.

Commending Washington’s accommodation, Hussein noted that recognizing the importance of religious freedom and facilitating pilgrim transit reflects shared values of mutual respect and tolerance, reinforcing a stable, long-term bilateral partnership between Iraq and the United States.

World.title: ITEX 2026: Iraqi AI and tech startups expand
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi, regional, and international technology enterprises showcased cutting-edge solutions in artificial intelligence, network synchronization, and enterprise digital transformation during their participation in the Iraq International Information and Communications Technology Exhibition in Baghdad.

The participating companies expressed strong ambition to expand operations and capture growing commercial opportunities in Iraq’s rapidly developing technological sector.

Hassan Abdul-Baqi Khalaf, founder of domestic startup Al-Burhan for AI Image and Video Recognition, told the Iraqi News Agency (INA) that the venture originated from registered patents specializing in automated media verification and tamper protection against digital forgery and deepfakes.

Khalaf—a computer science student at the American University of Iraq – Baghdad (AUIB) collaborating with a doctoral partner in mathematics and physics—highlighted that their platform processes requests for more than 3,000 daily active users across private corporate clients and the public.

Delivering up to 95 percent accuracy in identifying manipulated content, the company is leveraging its inaugural exhibition presence to pursue operational partnerships with federal entities, specifically the Ministry of Interior, to detect fabricated media and enhance sovereign cyber verification tools.

International infrastructure providers also underscored their entry into the domestic market. Engineer Ahmed Mustafa of Canada’s Al-Mamas, an IT and network engineering specialist, revealed that the firm is seeking to establish an operational foothold in Iraq following successful deployments in the UAE, Qatar, and Egypt.

Al-Mamas holds exclusive distribution rights across the Middle East and North Africa for precision German-manufactured timing and synchronization hardware, which is critical for maintaining ultra-low-latency architectures across telecommunications networks, industrial automation, data center facilities, and distributed artificial intelligence systems.

Highlighting regional corporate expansion, Samer Al-Yasin, sales director for Qatar-headquartered conglomerate Mannai Corporation, affirmed that Iraq represents a fertile and attractive destination for long-term tech investment.

Marking its second exhibition appearance in Baghdad, Mannai—which employs over 15,000 personnel across the Gulf—formally established its Baghdad branch three months ago and is actively preparing to launch regional offices in Erbil and Basra.

Al-Yasin emphasized that the group is deploying enterprise digital transformation, cloud integration, and systems architecture tailored for federal ministries, banking institutions, and healthcare providers, aiming to transfer its regional technical expertise to drive national modernization and support sovereign institutional revenues.

World.title: Baghdad hosts major motorsports festival to celebrate Iraqi sovereignty day
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Baghdad hosted a mass motorsports festival on Friday, October 2, 2026, to celebrate Iraqi Sovereignty Day and National Day, organized under the auspices of Iraqi National Olympic Committee President Aqeel Muften and drawing substantial public crowds alongside national sports figures.

The festival, co-organized by the Iraqi Automobile and Motorcycle Federation and secured by the Baghdad Operations Command, showcased competitive and exhibition motorsport performances to highlight domestic stability and nationwide celebrations marking the complete withdrawal of foreign forces.

Farooq Al-Rubaie, President of the Iraqi Automobile and Motorcycle Federation, told the Iraqi News Agency (INA) that celebrating Sovereignty Day honors the resilience and immense sacrifices made by the armed forces and citizens over challenging decades.

Noting the passionate grassroots fanbase for motorsports across Iraq, Al-Rubaie emphasized that staging the festival serves both an athletic and patriotic duty, projecting the reality of a secure and revitalized capital. He urged local and regional media outlets along with content creators to spotlight Iraq’s stability, community engagements, and peaceful public life during major national milestones.

Baghdad Operations Command Media Director, Major General Abbas Hamid, stated to INA that Sovereignty Day—coinciding with Iraq’s National Day—reflects the sovereign resolve of the Iraqi people.

Hamid confirmed that joint security formations under the Ministries of Defense and Interior, alongside military intelligence branches, established comprehensive security perimeters around the capital to safeguard wide-ranging cultural, artistic, and athletic gatherings.

Reaffirming that Baghdad is entering an era defined by urban reconstruction and civic stability, Hamid reiterated the full readiness of security apparatuses to protect public safety and preserve social cohesion across all urban centers.

World.title: Iraq inks data center MoU with Huawei as tech giant employs 10,000 across country
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Communications formalized a strategic partnership with global telecommunications giant Huawei on Friday, October 2, 2026, signing a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to construct modern enterprise data centers across the country.

Finalized during the 5th Iraq International Information and Communications Technology Exhibition and Conference (ITEX 2026) in Baghdad, the agreement was concluded under the sponsorship and in the presence of Minister of Communications Mustafa Sanad between the state-owned General Company for Communications and Informatics and Huawei’s executive leadership.

The initiative is aimed at bolstering Iraq’s sovereign cloud hosting, elevating service quality, and broadening international technical cooperation.

On the sidelines of the expo, Huawei confirmed the extensive scope of its commercial footprint in Iraq, revealing that it actively partners with more than 240 domestic Iraqi enterprises across diverse sectors.

Rafid Abbas Al-Khafaji, Vice President and Board Member of Huawei Iraq, told the Iraqi News Agency (INA) that this marked the company’s inaugural participation as an exhibitor at ITEX, expressing admiration for the high caliber of domestic and multinational engagement.

Al-Khafaji noted that Huawei presented specialized end-to-end solutions spanning oil and gas digitalization, telecommunications, smart transportation, healthcare systems, artificial intelligence, and modular data center architecture.

Reviewing the company’s continuous commercial presence in Iraq since 2003, Al-Khafaji emphasized that Huawei remained fully operational through all domestic security and economic challenges, including uninterrupted on-site work by its Chinese engineering teams during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Today, the corporation operates four major regional branches in Baghdad, Basra, Erbil, and Sulaymaniyah, supporting a wider ecosystem of over 10,000 employees.

Addressing public misconceptions, Al-Khafaji clarified that while Huawei is widely recognized among consumers for consumer smartphones, handset sales represent the smallest segment of its business portfolio by volume.

The firm’s enterprise and carrier operations form the backbone of its Iraqi footprint, servicing major mobile network operators alongside key sovereign institutions, including the Ministries of Oil, Transport, Interior, and Defense, as well as the General Secretariat of the Council of Ministers.

Beyond central government networks, Huawei is driving provincial smart security solutions—such as Babylon Governorate’s integrated municipal surveillance network—while advancing intelligent electric vehicle systems and cloud infrastructures designed to anchor Iraq’s next-generation digital economy.

World.title: Russia ‘tearing Kyiv apart’, mayor says, as strikes paralyse traffic
World.content:
Kyiv – Russian attacks on key infrastructure were “tearing Kyiv apart”, the city’s mayor said Friday, as strikes on a bridge linking the capital’s east and west brought traffic to a standstill.

President Volodymyr Zelensky accused his Russian counterpart, Vladimir Putin, of ripping up the rulebook of armed conflict by sanctioning massive attacks on civilian areas, an accusation the Kremlin has rejected.

The grinding conflict, which began with Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022, has largely focused on ground fighting in the east, with Kyiv largely spared from the devastation wrought near the frontline.

But Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko said the city should now be on a war footing.

“The capital is in a very dramatic situation,” he posted on Telegram. “It’s no longer possible to pretend that we can live now as we lived in peacetime.

“The enemy is tearing Kyiv apart.”

His message came as the authorities shut one of Kyiv’s main bridges and restricted movement on a second after another wave of deadly strikes by fast-moving, jet-powered drones.

Long lines of stationary cars and buses were gridlocked on main roads as commuters sought alternative routes — or even made their way on foot.

“I’ve been travelling for three hours… to get to work,” said Tetiana Osypenko, a 49-year-old seamstress whose bus was stuck in a traffic jam.

“There’s just no way to get there. Nothing. It’s impossible to cross the bridges today,” she told AFP.

Traffic built up due to the complete closure to all vehicles going in both directions on the Southern Bridge, one of eight bridges connecting the east and west of Kyiv over the Dnipro river.

It was hit several times on Thursday and Friday morning.

The Paton Bridge, further north, was open in one direction only, though there were no reports that it had been struck.

In a post on X, Zelensky accused Putin of last month declaring there were “no rules now”, citing unnamed intelligence and people around Putin.

“The Russians couldn’t occupy us. So now they are doing massive attacks and massive killings,” Zelensky said.

The Kremlin made no immediate public response to the claim, which Zelensky first made in an interview with the Financial Times.

– Daily disruption –

Kyiv has been increasingly under aerial bombardment in recent months, putting the city on near-constant alert and disrupting daily life.

Air raid sirens warning of approaching threats in the skies sound almost round the clock, urging the city’s estimated three million people to seek shelter.

Repeated strikes on trains and petrol stations have already hit the rail and road networks while attacks on energy facilities threaten power and heating as winter approaches.

Osypenko, the seamstress, said she would not get home because of the traffic jams. Previous disruption to subway services during air raids forced her to spend the night in a metro station near the Southern Bridge.

Not being able to work costs her money, compounding the financial pressures caused by the war, she added. “You just spend the whole day feeling completely beaten down.”

The latest Russian attacks killed one person and wounded at least two other people when a 25-storey residential building was hit in southeast Kyiv.

– ‘Political will’ –

Zelensky urged tougher sanctions to prevent Russia from manufacturing its new jet-powered drones, which are faster and harder to intercept.

Russia’s production of the weapons was “critically dependent” on foreign components, he wrote on social media on Friday.

“Every Russian drone can actually be stopped right at the production line. What is needed is the political will of these countries,” he added.

Zelensky has repeatedly called on Ukraine’s Western allies for more military support, particularly for US-made Patriot missile interceptors.

On Thursday, he said Ukraine had used its FP-7 tactical ballistic missile in combat for the first time, without disclosing where or what it had been used against.

He also said Ukraine was testing five of its own interceptors against drones.

Ukraine’s military on Friday said it struck an oil refinery in Volgograd and another facility in Samara, both in southwest Russia, for allegedly supplying fuel to Russian forces.

Kyiv also dismissed reports that its F-16 fighter jets — another key tool used against jet-powered drones — could be grounded due to delays in maintenance inspection and the supply of parts.

But Zelensky told the Financial Times that around half of Ukraine’s fleet was spending lengthy maintenance periods in Europe.

World.title: Man City verdict a ‘big topic’ for England players, says Tuchel
World.content:
London – Thomas Tuchel said that Manchester City were the talk of the England camp after the club were found guilty of multiple breaches of Premier League financial rules, but insisted that the case would not affect his selection for Saturday’s match in Croatia.

The findings by an independent commission, announced earlier this week, have sent shockwaves through English football.

City, the dominant Premier League force over the past 15 years, face severe sanctions, which could include expulsion from the top division.

Marc Guehi and Elliott Anderson are the only two City players remaining in Tuchel’s squad for the Nations League match in Rijeka after Nico O’Reilly was forced to withdraw due to injury.

“We had some time off and some time between the matches, and it’s a big subject,” Tuchel told his pre-match press conference on Friday.

“Of course the players talk about it, and City players talk about it, and we talk to them, but only briefly.

“They’re ready to go for tomorrow, that’s what they show on the pitch and that’s what they show in camp, but of course it’s a big topic.”

City deny wrongdoing and on Friday lodged an appeal against the ruling.

But unless they can overturn the decision of the commission, they are likely to face at least a points deduction, which would threaten their place in the Premier League.

Tuchel was asked if the club’s players would still be in his mind for selection should they be playing regularly in the lower divisions.

“There’s always a possibility,” he said. “I think I would always try to pick the best team for the camp, for the occasion, for the tournament, and I will never rule out that they don’t play in the top flight in their country.

“So we need to look at this from case by case.”

England’s clash with Croatia, which will take place behind closed doors, is their third of four Nations League games in the current international window.

The Three Lions were beaten 3-2 by world champions Spain on home soil last weekend, but bounced back to beat the Czech Republic 2-0 on Tuesday.

World.title: US posts weak job growth data in September
World.content:
Washington – Employment in the United States grew by 29,000 jobs in September, missing analysts’ expectations significantly, with the unemployment rate rising slightly to 4.2 percent, government data showed on Friday.

Adding to the weak data, the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) also revised down job figures for July and August by a combined 60,000 jobs, the department said in a statement.

The revision to July’s data showed that the world’s largest economy lost jobs that month, as opposed to posting a gain of 21,000 as previously reported.

The data comes ahead of key midterm elections in November where President Donald Trump’s Republican Party is facing a stern test over his handling of the economy.

Analysts polled by Dow Jones Newswires and the Wall Street Journal had expected the US economy to add 84,000 jobs in September.

– Health care leads –

Employment in most major sectors was largely unchanged, the BLS reported, with health care posting notable gains of 17,000.

The sector has propped up the labor market in the United States in the last year, as an aging population requires more care both in hospitals and at home.

Still, September’s gains in the sector were slower than its average monthly gain of 33,000 over the last year.

The financial sector continued its downward slide, losing 7,000 jobs in September and bringing its overall slump from a recent peak in May 2025 to 129,000.

Most of the losses in that sector have been among insurance companies.

– Fed implications –

Average hourly earnings for all employees were up 3.0 percent, the BLS said, with wages continuing to lag behind stubbornly high inflation — meaning most workers are seeing real wage losses.

Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren seized on the data to criticize Trump’s performance since taking office last year.

“Paychecks are growing at their slowest rate in nearly seven years, outside of the Covid-19 pandemic,” she said in a statement.

“Since the start of Trump’s war, real wages have fallen 0.7 percent as his failed agenda keeps pushing prices up,” she said, referring to the US war against Iran launched in late February.

The conflict has plunged the Middle East into violence and sent global energy prices skyrocketing, as Tehran’s retaliatory action has targeted Washington’s regional allies and choked a key trading route.

The data comes after the US Federal Reserve — which has a dual mandate to maintain inflation at a long-term two-percent target while ensuring maximum employment — raised interest rates last month to address high prices.

The US labor market has been largely in balance this year, with modest job gains and a relatively steady unemployment rate.

That steadiness has allowed the Fed to focus on the inflation side of its mandate, but any weakness in the labor market may give policy makers pause.

Raising interest rates tends to cool inflation but can also limit economic activity, which can affect the job market.

This week, two key Fed policymakers indicated that the central bank may not raise rates again at its October meeting, although markets continue to expect a further hike before the end of the year.

Friday’s jobs data “lends support to the less hawkish Fed officials that indicate no need to rush and deliver the next rate hike at the end of this month,” said Kathy Bostjancic, chief economist at Nationwide, in a note.

She added that this could release some pressure on bond yields — which have been spiralling in part due to expectations of interest rate hikes.

Nancy Vanden Houten at Oxford Economics, however, disagreed, expecting upside risks to inflation to continue to dominate Fed policymakers’ thinking.

“We think the upside risks to inflation are still a bigger concern for the Federal Reserve and expect they will raise rates at the end of the month,” she said.

World.title: Ethiopia’s conflict: the regional dimension
World.content:
Addis Ababa – Renewed fighting between the Ethiopian government and Tigrayan rebels has worsened regional tensions, with Ethiopia and Eritrea breaking diplomatic ties on Thursday.

Heavy fighting resumed between federal forces and the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) last week, and fighting has been ongoing across several fronts in northern Ethiopia.

The geopolitics of the Horn of Africa are fiendishly complex, with shifting alliances and the involvement of many outside actors with conflicting interests.

Here is what is at stake for the countries concerned:

– Eritrea –

Ethiopia accuses Eritrea of backing the TPLF, including with troops, which it has denied.

On Thursday, they expelled each other’s diplomats and shut down their respective embassies.

Eritrea gained independence from Ethiopia in 1993, and the two sides fought a brutal border war between 1998 and 2000.

Relations improved markedly with the rise of Ethiopia’s Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed in 2018, and Eritrea even fought alongside Ethiopia during the last civil war against the TPLF in 2020-2022.

But relations have since cratered, with Eritrea fearing landlocked Ethiopia plans to invade and seize access to the Red Sea.

“The TPLF is silently allied with its former foe, Eritrea, with supply lines chiefly secured through Tigray’s northern border,” the Chatham House think tank said in a report.

Eritrea’s “priority is to keep war away from its own territory”, it added, before cautioning the country’s actions increase the risk of regional escalation.

– Sudan –

The Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) have close ties with the TPLF and Eritrea. Tigrayan fighters have reportedly fought with the SAF in Sudan’s civil war.

Ethiopia is accused of assisting the United Arab Emirates in supplying the SAF’s opponent, the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), which it has denied.

Sudan was accused of funnelling weapons and supplies to the TPLF during the last war. There were clashes along the shared border in August, suggesting it remains an active concern for the Ethiopian government.

– Egypt –

Egypt is strongly opposed to Ethiopia’s new Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam, which it says will affect downstream Nile waters. It has forged closer ties with Eritrea and Somalia in an apparent anti-Ethiopia front.

Ethiopia expelled an Egyptian diplomat on Thursday, without giving a reason. Cairo responded by expelling an Ethiopian diplomat.

– United Arab Emirates –

The UAE has invested deeply across east Africa as it seeks security partnerships to counter rivals and control the Red Sea, as well as agricultural land, and investments.

It has been one of Abiy’s principal backers, giving him a $3 billion loan and investment package when he came to power in 2018, and building his giant new palace in Addis Ababa, as well as providing military drones and logistical support during the last civil war.

In return, it is alleged that Ethiopia has helped funnel arms to the UAE’s allies in Sudan, though that is denied by both countries.

– United States –

Washington was closely involved in the peace deal that ended the last civil war in 2022.

Its focus has lately been on the Red Sea — and its efforts to contain Iran and its proxies. As a result, it allowed sanctions on Ethiopia and Eritrea to end, with the ill-timed claim that the “national emergency… has expired”.

– Somalia –

Ethiopia’s relations with Somalia were ruptured in January 2024 when Addis Ababa signed a sea-access deal with the breakaway region of Somaliland.

Relations were ultimately restored with Turkish mediation and the deal with Somaliland seemingly put on the back burner.

World.title: FSSAI steps up festive food crackdown as adulteration raids intensify
World.content:
NEW DELHI: With festive demand for sweets and milk products rising, food safety authorities have stepped up enforcement across the country, with thousands of kilograms of suspected adulterated food already seized or destroyed in Delhi-NCR.

The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has now directed all states and Union territories to intensify inspections and sampling during Navratri and Diwali.

In Delhi alone, food safety teams have destroyed more than 4,100 kg of suspected adulterated khoya and paneer during enforcement action last month, while samples of khoya, paneer, chhena and ghee are being collected from markets for testing.

In neighbouring Mewat, officials have seized and destroyed more than 10,000 kg of adulterated paneer in last months, with around 50 raids conducted in areas identified as production hubs. Officials said the supply chain extends to Jaipur, Mathura, Gurugram, Faridabad and Delhi, raising concerns over the movement of adulterated paneer into the wider National Capital Region.

Against this backdrop, FSSAI on September 29 directed food safety authorities across the country to step up surveillance and enforcement against adulterated, counterfeit and unsafe food products during the festive season.





The regulator has specifically identified milk and milk products, sweets, snacks and savouries, edible oil, beverages and ghee for heightened scrutiny.

States have been asked to conduct inspections and sampling at identified hotspots and sensitive locations. The directive also asks authorities to record inspection, sampling and outcome data on the Food Safety Compliance System (FoSCoS) and Food Safety Compliance through Regular Inspection and Sampling of Food (FoSCoRIS) on a real-time basis.

The national directive also allows states to focus on products specific to local consumption patterns, including kuttu atta and singhada atta in northern and western regions.

World.title: Delhi Police registers 3 FIRs over protests demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation
World.content:
No individual or organisation has been named as an accused in the FIRs

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Delhi Police on Saturday registered three FIRs in connection with Fridayâs protests by student organisations, political parties and civil society activists who attempted to gather at Jantar Mantar demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Two FIRs were registered at Parliament Street police station and one at Connaught Place police station, a senior police officer said. The cases invoke Section 223 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which deals with alleged disobedience of an order duly promulgated by a public servant.No individual or organisation has been named as an accused in the FIRs, the officer said. However, details of organisers and organisations that proposed or participated in the demonstrations have been included in the contents of the cases.The FIRs follow a day of protests across central Delhi, where thousands of opposition activists, students and youth organisation members attempted to march towards Jantar Mantar. Police detained around 1,000 protesters as they tried to cross barricades and reach the designated protest site.The demonstrations involved the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), All India Students' Association (AISA), Students' Federation of India (SFI), National Students' Union of India (NSUI), Indian Youth Congress (IYC) and other organisations.Protesters were demanding Kumarâs resignation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and alleged mass deletion of voters.Police had repeatedly announced that gatherings were not permitted at Jantar Mantar. Protesters were stopped at several locations, including Firoz Shah Road and Ashoka Road, with some attempting to push past barricades. AISA president Neha Bora and several other activists were among those stopped.AAP leaders Saurabh Bharadwaj, Atishi and Sanjeev Jha were detained, while Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh was stopped while heading towards the protest. NSUI president Vinod Jakhar and activists from SFI and other student groups were also detained.Security was stepped up across central Delhi, with around 5,000 Delhi Police and paramilitary personnel deployed. Entry and exit gates at 12 metro stations were closed and internet services were suspended in parts of central Delhi amid the protests.

World.title: After Chandrayaan-3, ICMR asks scientists to attempt the ‘impossible’ in healthcare
World.content:
NEW DELHI: After

made India the first country to successfully land near the Moonâs south polar region, the government is now asking scientists to attempt something equally audacious in healthcare: develop something the world has never tried before.

The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) has launched its âFirst in the World Challengeâ, inviting researchers to develop breakthrough vaccines, drugs, therapeutics, diagnostics and other health technologies that have never been thought of, tested or tried anywhere in the world.

The initiative will offer up to Rs 8 crore for a single project, depending on how advanced the proposed innovation is. ICMR describes it as a high-risk, high-reward programme, acknowledging that some projects may fail but saying successful ones could bring about a major change in healthcare.

The grants will be released in stages: up to Rs 1 crore for proof-of-concept, Rs 4 crore for prototypes and Rs 8 crore for final products or implementation models. Funding will be linked to deliverables, with ICMR reviewing each stage before approving the next.

The opportunity is open beyond ICMR scientists. Researchers from government medical colleges, Institutes of National Importance, universities, recognised research laboratories and eligible NGOs can apply.





Indian startups, micro, small and medium enterprises and industry are also eligible.

The scheme targets genuinely new health technologies, not incremental improvements. ICMR will first check whether a proposal is truly âfirst in the worldâ, followed by assessment of its relevance and potential impact by a panel of experts, innovators, policymakers and scientists.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The programme aims to take innovations from the lab to deployment, requiring researchers to detail regulatory, validation, commercialisation and technology-transfer plans, as well as demonstrate the technologyâs clinical need, advantages over existing options and readiness for deployment.

Applications will open on October 7 and close on November 30, with results due on December 31. Each proposal must include at least one co-principal investigator from the principal investigatorâs institution. ICMR says the initiative is willing to back high-risk ideas with uncertain outcomes but potentially transformative gains, in pursuit of breakthroughs no one has achieved before.

World.title: Nearly half of India’s medical colleges fail to comply with NMC disability-unit directive
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Nearly half of Indiaâs medical colleges (44.5%) have failed to set up Enabling Units mandated by the National Medical Commission for students with benchmark disabilities. Of 798 colleges, 355 remain non-compliant, with several naming sanitation inspectors, residents, tutors and head clerks as single points of contact, according to an affidavit filed by the Commission in the Supreme Court on Tuesday.At Maharashtra Government Medical College, Nandurbar, a sanitation inspector, has been designated as the coordinator of the Enabling Unit. Other colleges have named residents, tutors and head clerks as points of contact.Dr Satendra Singh, disability-rights activist and doctor associated with Doctors with Disabilities: Agents of Change, questioned the choice of personnel for the role. âItâs unheard of for a sanitation inspector or head clerk to be made in-charge of such a committee in a medical college. They have neither the designated administrative or academic responsibility for undergraduate or postgraduate training nor the training or authority to deal with disability accommodation, clinical training, patient safety or assessment.âHe added, âThey cannot take or escalate decisions on postings, duty hours, assistive devices, accessible infrastructure, examination accommodations or clinical-rotation modifications. Tutors and residents are also a floating population, often at an institution for only a limited period. How would a postgraduate student in pharmacology, who may not even be an alumnus of that institution, know what assistance a wheelchair-using medical student needs in an operation theatre or have the authority to direct the theatre staff?âThe NMC circular does not prescribe a doctor or clinical faculty member as the single point of contact. It does, however, assign the Enabling Unit responsibility for reasonable accommodation, academic and clinical support, barrier-free access, coordination, record-keeping and information dissemination.The compliance exercise was undertaken following the Supreme Courtâs August 4, 2026 order in Anmol vs Union of India, which directed the NMC to seek college-wise compliance with its July 27 circular through Deans and Principals.The court warned that if colleges failed to respond or follow the directions, âa serious view will be taken against the individual colleges.âThe NMCâs affidavit said 515 of 798 colleges had responded by September 28: 443 reported full compliance, 26 partial or ongoing compliance, and 46 submitted only the committee-constitution order. As many as 283 colleges did not respond. Majority of NMC-designated medical assessment boards and appellate boards themselves fail to comply, despite NMC warning that âserious viewâ would be takenThe commission had set September 10 as the deadline and issued reminders on September 23 and 24, the latter warning that late submissions would not be accepted and show-cause notices would follow. Colleges were required to provide details of the unit, its members and POC, functionality, accessibility, communication to students, records and compliance status.

World.title: Pacific to pacify ties? Washington sends US admiral to India as relations face strain
World.content:
NEW DELHI: American admiral Samuel J. Paparo, who leads US Indo-Pacific Command, is in India from 3 to 8 October. It is his second visit this year.

The US Embassy said the trip is meant to push forward the "major defense partnership" and deepen cooperation between the two militaries.

Its list of topics includes digital transformation, emerging technologies and regional strategic stability. It also names "defense energy resilience" and an "increasingly competitive technology landscape", though it does not spell out what either would involve.

Press release by the US Embassy in India.

On his earlier trip, Paparo visited Delhi, Chandimandir and Bengaluru. He met the Chief of Defence Staff and the Navy chief, and discussed security along India's western and northern borders.

Last month, Paparo conducted a series of key bilateral and multilateral meetings on the sidelines of the 28th Indo-Pacific Chiefs of defence conference in Victoria, Canada, held from August 31 to September 2.

According to the US Pacific Command (US PACOM), Paparo highlighted "the importance of strong bilateral and multilateral relationships in advancing regional security and deterrence".

Throughout the conference, the US commander engaged in discussions with the Defence Cooperation Council and the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue (Quad), and joined military leadership from Asean nations.





Paparo also connected with defence counterparts from Australia and the United Kingdom for an Aukus dialogue, and conferred with Adm. Giuseppe Cavo Dragone, chair of the Nato Military Committee.

US Pacific Command noted that Paparo carried out bilateral discussions focused on "strengthening operational cooperation, information-sharing, maritime security and readiness across the Indo-Pacific" with senior representatives from numerous partner nations.

The participating countries included Bangladesh, Brunei, Cambodia, Canada, France, India, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, Mongolia, New Zealand, the Republic of Korea, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam.

What Washington has put on record

Paparo's visit comes after a run of statements in Washington. An update on how the 2026 National Defense Strategy is being carried out, sent to the Senate Armed Services Committee, places India under the heading of burden-sharing, the idea that allies and partners should take on more of the load.

"Finally, and crucially given its regional standing and power, we are also building on our strong defence relationship with India, with the recent signature of a 10-year bilateral defence framework and a separate framework to strengthen undersea cooperation," the update said.

Testifying before lawmakers in April, Paparo said the relationship with India had seen "transformative growth through increasingly complex military exercises, defence sales, and strategic dialogue".

However, the recent Trump tariffs and the punitive measures against India for buying Russian oil, and a stuck trade deal has undoubetly strained the ties between both nations.

Paparo had also pointed to cooperation on maritime security and underwater awareness, including India's planned purchase of MQ-9B drones through US foreign military sales. He also described India as one of the partners he visits and coordinates with most often.

He said India "continues to be a source of stability within South Asia", and cited its investments in Sri Lanka and its agreements with Mauritius, which he said help keep strategic infrastructure "free of adversarial influences". On Pakistan, he noted that recent military exchanges had extended beyond traditionally disputed areas, but said India's main focus remained "maintaining deterrence and credible warfighting capability within the region writ large.

"

The China question in the background

None of this is discussed in isolation from China as Paparo himself has said Beijing's actions, along with its deepening ties to Russia and North Korea, make for a complex challenge to regional stability. He calls alliances and partnerships Washington's "greatest asymmetric advantage", and the Quad, which brings together the US, India, Japan and Australia, is part of that picture. Though Quad his been pushed to a back burner under the Tump 2.0.

At a regional security conference in Malaysia, Paparo said some actors were using "false claims of legitimacy" to justify coercion. "That's not the rule of law. That's the rule by law. That distinction between law as a tool of order versus law as a weapon of raw power, is the defining fault line of our time," he said. He added that the US was deterring China "through strength, not through confrontation".

In the South China Sea, Manila has accused Beijing of dangerous manoeuvres, water cannon attacks and attempts to block resupply missions around a disputed shoal. China denies this. Philippine defence secretary Gilberto Teodoro said, "China is everywhere â¦ this is a matter of concern," and pointed to a recent Chinese ballistic missile launch into the Pacific.

At the congressional hearing, Representative Adam Smith said partners needed reassurance. "We need to maintain those relationships. We need to let those folks know that we are there and they can depend on us," he said.

World.title: 'I am Hanuman to Rahul Gandhi': Ajay Rai after being replaced as UP Congress chief

on Saturday called himself a âHanumanâ to Congress leader

, saying he would continue to follow the partyâs national leadership and carry out its political fight regardless of the position he holds.

I thank Rahul Gandhi and the top leadership for their faith in me and extend my best wishes to Aradhana Mishra Mona. World.title: Asian Games 2026 LIVE: India clinch cricket gold after beating Pakistan in final
World.content:
India beat Pakistan in a thrilling Asian Games final on Saturday (October 3, 2026) to clinch the gold medal and retain the title they won at the 2023 Hangzhou Games, with Abhishek Sharma’s 61 and Tilak Varma’s unbeaten 51 powering India to a formidable 211. Pakistan came under sustained pressure during the chase, with India’s spinners leading the charge as both Axar Patel and Washington Sundar finished with figures of 2-29. The victory sees India successfully defend their Asian Games cricket title and add another gold medal to their tally.

Meanwhile, Teenager Kumkum Mohod kept her composure under pressure to clinch gold in the women’s individual recurve event at the Asian Games, defeating South Korea’s Oh Yejin in a shoot-out. Also Read | Asian Games 2026 medal tally

World.title: Stop filing FIRs against BJP leaders; review those filed over Form 7 applications, former CM B.S. Yediyurappa urges Karnataka DG&IGP
World.content:
A BJP delegation led by former Karnataka chief minister B.S. Yediyurappa, State unit president B.Y. Vijayendra, Leader of Opposition in the Assembly R. Ashok and Leader of Opposition in the Council Chalavadi Narayanaswamy met the Director General and Inspector General of Police on October 3, urging him to ensure that FIRs registered in connection with Form 7 applications during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls be dealt with strictly according to the law.

In a memorandum, the delegation alleged that criminal cases were being registered against BJP workers and political activists for submitting Form 7 objections, and that the police machinery was being subjected to political pressure.

Statutory mechanism

The BJP said Form 7 is a statutory mechanism provided by the Election Commission of India for electors to object to inclusion of names or seek deletion of existing entries from electoral rolls. It argued that the mere filing of multiple or bulk Form 7 applications cannot, by itself, constitute a criminal offence.

The delegation referred to FIRs reportedly registered in Bhalki in Bidar, Belagavi and Narasimharaja in Mysuru, involving provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. It said any criminal liability must be established on the basis of evidence showing individual involvement, including whether an applicant knowingly furnished false information or forged documents.

The BJP also cited provisions in the SIR guidelines and the Manual on Electoral Rolls, 2023, claiming that there is no prescribed limit on the number of Form 7 applications that can be submitted and that objections are subject to verification by election officials.

The delegation further raised concern over the alleged circulation of Form 7 applications containing applicants’ names, mobile numbers and signatures on social media, and sought an inquiry into the source of the disclosure.

The BJP urged the DGP to ensure that police action remains politically neutral and that any genuine violations are proceeded against strictly according to law and due process.

Warning by Leader of Opposition

Speaking after submitting the memorandum, Mr. Ashok warned, “If police officers misuse their power, they will have to regret it later. An NDA government is going to come to power in the state. Then we will settle accounts with the police officers.”

World.title: Two migrant workers killed as borewell rig overturns onto house in Keralam
World.content:
Two migrant workers were killed when a borewell drilling lorry overturned onto a house near Varakkad junction in West Eleri village in Kasaragod district of Keralam in the early hours of Saturday.

The deceased have been identified as Devendran, a native of Madhya Pradesh, and Manase, alias Manasir, from Chhattisgarh. The accident occurred between 1 a.m. and 2 a.m.

The Tamil Nadu-registered vehicle reportedly lost control while negotiating a steep downhill stretch of a subsidiary road leading to the main road at Varakkad. It then crashed into a nearby house and overturned on top of it.

The impact caused damage to the house, but the family members inside escaped unhurt. They were asleep when the lorry crashed into the building.

A nearby electric post was also damaged in the accident, disrupting power supply to the area. The vehicle owner and other workers accompanying the deceased have been informed of the incident.

The bodies of the two workers have been kept at the mortuary of the district government hospital in Kasaragod. Police reached the spot and initiated further procedures. Following the inquest and postmortem examination, the bodies will be handed over to their relatives.
