Of course, people should go and vote. Why not? It isn’t that difficult to do. If people say it is important, and one can demonstrate civic engagement in that sense, I believe one should go and vote.

As for whom to vote for, that is a separate question. I do not have the right to engage in campaigning here right now, but one should also look at the retrospective. Various political forces have existed throughout Abkhazia’s history; you are younger, but Alkhas and I remember the blockade times and the post-blockade period when the new team came in. We must also understand for ourselves which political force is minded to help Abkhazia, and which political force recognized Abkhazia’s independence. These are different teams with different viewpoints, so here too, I believe our choice is straightforward; we simply need to understand it all.

Alkhas Gagulia: We have spoken at length about relations with Russia—it is our strategic partner—but an event took place in the Turkish parliament recently. People view it in different ways, and opinions vary. In my view, it is a very landmark event when 30% of the Turkish parliament raised the issue of ending the isolation of Abkhazia. Recognition was not on the table, and there were differing opinions regarding the motives behind that speech. It turned out to be primarily the opposition party. But anticipating your answer, I would say—as one Chinese sage or general secretary put it—it doesn’t matter what color the cat is, as long as it catches mice. What is your view on this initiative, and what, in your opinion, actually happened there?

Adgur Ardzinba: Alkhas, your late relative Gennady Leonidovich Gagulia once told me a story about cats and mice too. He said that when you try to play political cat-and-mouse, make sure that you are not the mouse. Yes, of course, it is a positive signal. Incidentally, our organization issued a statement on this matter. The signal itself is positive, even if, as some note, it represents an element of internal political struggle to attract our large diaspora and secure votes. Even if that is the case, it remains positive. It shows the role and significance of our diaspora, which we utilize very weakly—and not only in Turkey. But that is a vast, separate topic. Therefore, it is a positive signal, and that is how we assess it. However, actions and deeds matter most. Words are fine—we approve and welcome them—but deeds are what count. Russia went ahead in 2008 and established diplomatic relations with Abkhazia, recognizing our independence. Those are real actions.

Alkhas Gagulia: There was a caveat there, if I am not mistaken, that there was no question of any recognition.

Adgur Ardzinba: When politicians speak about it to attract votes, again, it is still a good thing that the topic of Abkhazia and ending its isolation is being discussed, forming a positive agenda to attract votes. But I very much hope it will not remain mere words.

Alkhas Gagulia: Adgur Ardzinba of 2024 and Adgur Ardzinba of 2026. What advice would you give today to the person you were back then?

Adgur Ardzinba: That is a good question; I hadn’t thought about it. That is actually too short a time frame. I wouldn’t have changed much.

Georgi Berzenia: Significant events have occurred. First of all, the elections. They surely brought about some…

Alkhas Gagulia: Takeaways from the elections. What mistakes were made?

Adgur Ardzinba: Look, yes, of course, we made a whole host of mistakes. But it is not a given that if I had told my former self to avoid those mistakes, other mistakes wouldn’t have been made instead. Mistakes are part of any process.

Alkhas Gagulia: Nor is it a given that he would have listened?

Adgur Ardzinba: I will tell you this: it has been a rather interesting period of time. I consider myself fortunate. I feel fortunate in that—and I say this sincerely—the Abkhazian people, a portion of the Abkhazian people, and a substantial portion at that, entrusted me with this responsible mission. That is a great, immense honor. There is nothing above that, Alkhas. Any obstacles or hurdles are minor by comparison. When serving your people is not mere rhetoric but a reality—if done sincerely and from the heart—there are no obstacles. That is the highest honor.

Therefore, what would I advise my former self? I would advise him not to doubt, because a person always experiences doubt when faced with immense difficulties. Alkhas, we speak about this so casually now. For instance, when people entered the building in November 2024, some said they shouldn’t have entered, while others asked what would have happened had they not entered. Someone had to take responsibility. Other politicians were there; we were all together. While we achieved a certain goal on the one hand, on the other hand, during all those days—and I slept inside that building for three nights to ensure people wouldn’t clash with one another—it was a difficult period, followed by the election process.

Naturally, any person experiences doubt. Our recent presidential elections were unique—they were engaging and event-filled. But those elections were particularly interesting because our team faced such a formidable, serious opponent equipped with vast resources. When you have a very serious opponent, it mobilizes you immensely. I assure you, had that not been the case, the elections might have turned out very dull. Instead, they unfolded the way they did.

Alkhas Gagulia: To be honest, I dream of dull elections for all branches of power.

Adgur Ardzinba: We are speaking about personality and perception right now. Yes, I too dream that our country, like Switzerland, could have dull elections. But if we talk about what existed then versus now, it has been a very fascinating period during which I came to respect my people even more. I feel immense pride in being part of this nation—small in numbers perhaps, but possessing a grand spirit and a vast heart—a people that cannot be intimidated, no matter how hard anyone tries. And with such a spirit in our hearts, we are bound for success.

I am absolutely certain that we will succeed in everything. All those misunderstandings and unpleasantries, including those in relations between Abkhazia and Russia, are entirely surmountable. I am confident that… Look, we are talking about certain incidents right now, and they are indeed unpleasant. Yet we had a period when the entire country was under a blockade for six to seven years. We were under a blockade—the whole country. Now we are talking about a few individuals being unable to travel, whereas back then it was the entire country.

Even then… Vladislav Grigorievich Ardzinba—for which I will always be grateful to him—was a great, exceptionally wise man. He always maintained that we must orient ourselves toward a union with the Russian Federation; that time would pass, people would change, and understanding would arrive. And he was right. Although you remember, Alkhas, how many different proposals there were, delegation after delegation, yet we did not deviate from our path. All these misunderstandings taking place are simply part of the process. Just as there are mistakes on our side, there are mistakes on theirs as well.

I am confident that everything will be fine. The main thing is to remain vigilant. Times are very dangerous. I will repeat it endlessly: defense and security.

Alkhas Gagulia: Well, I want to say thank you for today’s broadcast, for coming to join us so that a thorough conversation could take place on all the questions that interested us. The only thing I would like to add, of course, is that while we spoke about priority tasks—about defense and education—all of this stems from a single overarching priority: our sovereignty and our independence. If that serves as the main guidepost, everything else is meant to serve that exact priority. There are no other options. You mentioned my age twenty times today; in any case, my generation accepts nothing less. We lost far too many people for this land, and it is thanks to them that we stand on this land today. That is what I want to say to every single politician, without exception, on both sides. Thank you for the broadcast and for coming. I look forward to our next meetings.

Adgur Ardzinba: Thank you, friends. I believe that while our conversation was lengthy, it was candid, and we answered a number of questions. If we missed anything, I think we will have another opportunity to meet. As for sovereignty, Alkhas, that concerns not only your generation. The younger generation and the youth—the rising generation with whom I interact—see no other path across all generations than the building of an independent, sovereign Abkhazian state in Abkhazia. If anyone thinks otherwise, that would be their mistake. All of us have stood, are standing, and will continue to stand for this. Fundamentally, our entire conversation has been dedicated to strengthening that sovereignty, to making our state less vulnerable.

Today, our state is vulnerable. Let us be frank. To eliminate these weak points, we need systemic work, the establishment of priorities, societal consolidation, and defense to preserve our territory, as well as our language—which you raised, Georgi—and our culture. All of this is vital, because knowing a language alone does not make you Abkhaz. The upcoming parliamentary elections are also crucial; the quality and substantive content of that body are of great importance. All of this, as was rightly stated, Alkhas, exists in order to preserve, strengthen, and pass down. Thank you.

Georgi Berzenia: Thank you for an engaging conversation.

The terminology, place names and views expressed in this article are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect the editorial position of this website.

World.title: ‘We will decide in the coming months’: Pashinyan on choosing model for Armenia’s new nuclear power plant
World.content:
Pashinyan on building a new nuclear power plant in Armenia

Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan has announced a change in the government’s position on the technology and design of a new nuclear power plant.

“I have said dozens of times before that we do not need anything more [powerful] than a modular nuclear power plant. That was our position. But now we have to understand that a modular plant will most likely not be enough to meet our needs,” Pashinyan said.

He explained that the government changed its position because of the construction of AI factories. Armenia now needs to import electricity to meet their power requirements.

Discussions continue over which technology would best suit the new nuclear power plant. The Armenian government expects to make a decision on the issue by the end of 2027.

A day earlier, the prime minister met a delegation led by Alexey Likhachev, director general of the state-owned Rosatom corporation. They discussed proposals from the Russian side.

Armenia is currently working to extend the operating life of the Metsamor nuclear power plant until 2036. Russia has taken part in efforts to extend the plant’s operating life and modernise it throughout this period. The plant originally entered service in 1977.

At the same time, Yerevan is discussing the construction of a new nuclear power plant with several countries, including the US. The prime minister has repeatedly said in recent months that the nuclear power issue is not a geopolitical choice for Armenia: “We will choose the proposal that serves us best.”

Pashinyan does not rule out accepting the Russian proposal

Speaking about the upcoming decision on the technology for the new nuclear power plant, the prime minister stressed that before Armenia signed memorandums of understanding with the US on 8 August 2025, Armenia had a surplus of electricity.

“We had to think about where to direct this surplus energy. A year later, Armenia had become a country with an electricity deficit,” he said.

According to Nikol Pashinyan, this resulted from the construction of two AI factories in Armenia during that period:

“The point is that, given the scale of the investment projects already approved, Armenia has faced an electricity deficit. In other words, these projects are fully absorbing the surplus we have. So we need to decide what to do next.”

The prime minister said the government would make a decision in the coming months. Pashinyan also said that Armenia could accept the proposal put forward by Russia:

“It is quite possible that building a 1,000 MW plant will prove to be the most logical solution. However, I cannot say for certain at this stage because experts are still assessing the issue.”

“The unit should be at least one, with a capacity of at least 1 GW” — Likhachev

Rosatom director general Alexey Likhachev told journalists some details of Russia’s proposal after talks in Yerevan. Likhachev said Armenia would continue to rely on nuclear energy for decades to come. Russia therefore plans to “formulate the most competitive proposal” for building a new reactor unit in the coming months.

“And in our view, this unit should be at least one, with a capacity of at least 1 GW,” Likhachev said.

According to him, the proposal involves a VVER-1000 reactor, a pressurised water reactor with a capacity of 1,000 MW.

The head of Rosatom stressed that this proposal is “the best currently available on the global market”. He added that Rosatom has built and continues to build VVER reactors of this type in India and Iran:

“They combine very high economic efficiency, namely a low cost of electricity, with all the necessary Generation III+ safety systems.”

Details of talks with Rosatom director general in Yerevan

The Armenian prime minister’s office said Pashinyan and Likhachev discussed:

work to extend the operating life of the existing second reactor unit at the Armenian Nuclear Power Plant;

Russia’s proposals for building a new reactor unit.

At the same time, the prime minister told Likhachev that the Armenian government was continuing to consider proposals from other international partners.

Pashinyan stressed that the final decision would depend solely on economic considerations. These would include price, quality, safety, construction timelines and guarantees.

The statement also said Alexey Likhachev described cooperation with Armenian partners as constructive. The Rosatom chief also provided detailed information about the construction of not only large VVER reactors, but also small and medium-sized reactors.

World.title: Right beside us, provocations are rained down on us day and night in Azerbaijani - President Ilham Aliyev
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 3. Right beside us, provocations are rained down on us day and night in Azerbaijani, President Ilham Aliyev said during his speech at the 8th Congress of the New Azerbaijan Party (YAP).

"Our ideological work, including that carried out by party activists, must be conducted in such a way that Azerbaijani realities, the ongoing developments in our country, and the highly positive atmosphere are constantly discussed publicly. Today, such large-scale construction work is being carried out in Azerbaijan that I do not know which country has a comparable level of development – not only in Garabagh and East Zangezur, where unprecedented development is underway, but across every single region. Therefore, the time has come to properly structure ideological work, abandon clichés, and move away from purely formal events. Modern ideological work must be conducted. Our advantage is that, unlike some countries, we do not need to invent myths. In some nations, leaders try to claim past achievements as their own or exaggerate their roles by distorting history; we do not need this. What we need is for the truth to reach every citizen – at a time when there is a wide range of information sources, including in the Azerbaijani language. Attention must be paid to this as well.

Why is a resource created in the Azerbaijani language in a foreign country? Is it to help us? No, it is to carry out provocations against us, mislead our people, and poison the minds of our youth. That is it. Whenever you see a resource created in Azerbaijani abroad, know that this is its goal. One does not need to look far for facts; right beside us, provocations are rained down on us day and night in Azerbaijani. Or in Western countries, Azerbaijani-language resources have been established. Why? To shatter this unity, subject Azerbaijan to their will, turn us away from our path of independence, and subsequently govern us. That is the goal. Therefore, this domain is as vital as physical security, and who should be at the center of this work? Of course, the members of the New Azerbaijan Party," President Ilham Aliyev noted.

The 8th Congress of the New Azerbaijan Party (YAP) was held yesterday at the Heydar Aliyev Center in Baku.

A total of 960 delegates were elected by YAP's district and city organizations to attend the congress.

As part of preparations for the 8th Congress, reporting conferences were held at 84 local party organizations from September 7 to 19. A total of 16,239 people attended the conferences.

The reporting conferences heard reports on work carried out to fulfill the tasks set after the 7th Congress and discussed the results achieved.

World.title: Older generation probably remembers well even their performing Namaz - President Ilham Aliyev
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 3. The older generation probably remembers well their sweet words, toasts raised to health, their fluent speech in the Azerbaijani language, and even their performing Namaz, President Ilham Aliyev said during his speech at the 8th Congress of the New Azerbaijan Party (YAP).

"I would like to share some thoughts regarding the tasks ahead today. I periodically make statements about the work that needs to be done, including in interviews and speeches. I believe that the situation in the world is changing so rapidly today that there is a great need for this. First of all, one of the main tasks is to increase our military power. A question may be asked: we have won a glorious Victory, Armenia was forced to sign a capitulation act. Today there is no conflict between Azerbaijan and Armenia, there is no war, there is tranquility at the borders. The peace agreement has been initialed, and contacts are already taking place. Azerbaijan has even started trade with Armenia. Why is this necessary? The answer to this, in my opinion, is very clear and obvious. This is always necessary, for every country. Because our people faced this tragedy. Our people faced the ingratitude of the Armenians. That is to say, the older generation probably remembers well their sweet words, toasts raised to health, their fluent speech in the Azerbaijani language, and even their performing Namaz," President Ilham Aliyev noted.

World.title: Activists who have exhausted entire world with this “green agenda” have now come to realize that no economy can develop without oil, gas, and fuel - President Ilham Aliyev
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 3. Activists who have exhausted the entire world with this “green agenda” have now come to realize that no economy can develop without oil, gas, and fuel, President Ilham Aliyev said during his speech at the 8th Congress of the New Azerbaijan Party (YAP).

"Even those activists who have exhausted the entire world with this “green agenda” have now come to realize that no economy can develop without oil, gas, and fuel. You remember well how many groundless accusations were leveled against us during COP29 and on its eve, claiming that a climate conference should not be held in an oil-producing country. Well, Canada produces 10 times more oil than we do. It can be held there, but not here?! Once again, it was a biased approach. However, I want to say that today, serious discussions are taking place even among those who put forward the thesis of the “green transition.” Well then, let them not buy our gas, our oil, or our petroleum products. How will their economies develop? That is why Azerbaijan, rich in energy resources, is becoming a very serious geopolitical and security factor today. Because energy security means the national security of every country, and our role will grow even further," President Ilham Aliyev said.

The 8th Congress of the New Azerbaijan Party (YAP) was held yesterday at the Heydar Aliyev Center in Baku.

A total of 960 delegates were elected by YAP's district and city organizations to attend the congress.

As part of preparations for the 8th Congress, reporting conferences were held at 84 local party organizations from September 7 to 19. A total of 16,239 people attended the conferences.

The reporting conferences heard reports on work carried out to fulfill the tasks set after the 7th Congress and discussed the results achieved.

World.title: High-ranking representatives of countries hostile to each other meet in Azerbaijan - President Ilham Aliyev
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 3. High-ranking representatives of countries hostile to each other meet in Azerbaijan within the framework of international events, President Ilham Aliyev said during his speech at the 8th Congress of the New Azerbaijan Party (YAP).

"As I have said, our steps regarding foreign policy are received with great appreciation in the world. Our prestige is growing. We are joining many new formats. Today, it would be difficult to find a second country – though perhaps there is one – that builds such multifaceted international relations as Azerbaijan, maintains contact with many countries and, one could say, all major poles, and defends its own interests. In any case, this is a unique experience. It is enough to recall the events of just the past month for everyone to see that high-ranking representatives of countries hostile to each other meet in Azerbaijan within the framework of international events. Meetings and events aimed at reducing certain international risks are also held in Azerbaijan.

Why is Azerbaijan chosen? First, because there is trust in us. They know that Azerbaijan is a reliable partner. Second, many countries have now joined various camps or wish to do so. We, however, do not join any camp and will not join one – we do not need to. For a country with a relatively small territory and population, it is naturally not easy to establish itself as an independent actor on the global stage and gain respect. There are many reasons for this, and I would not want to elaborate too much on that. Quite simply, among our future tasks, our foreign policy needs to be not only active, but also proactive rather than defensive. Of course, our country's role in international organizations is undeniable. Everyone remembers well that we led the second-largest institution after the UN for four years, having been elected by a unanimous decision. In November of last year, a very significant event occurred: Azerbaijan was admitted as a full member of the Consultative Meetings of Central Asia. We are not located in Central Asia; we are located in the South Caucasus. But look at how close Azerbaijan is to these countries and how vital our political, economic, transport, energy, and other projects are to them that this unprecedented event took place," President Ilham Aliyev noted.

World.title: Uzbekistan, Pakistan’s Water Con discuss 500-hectare olive project
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 3. Uzbekistan and Pakistan’s Water Con discussed an investment project to establish a 500-hectare olive plantation in the Jizzakh region, including plans to process the harvest and produce finished products in Tashkent on Oct. 2.

This was reflected in the statement by Uzbekistan's Ministry of Agriculture, following the project planned for Yangiyabad district of Jizzakh region.

The discussions focused on selecting olive varieties suitable for local conditions, introducing modern irrigation technologies, establishing the plantation and developing processing facilities.

Water Con representatives presented proposals for implementing the project and reviewed the results of a preliminary technical assessment of the 500-hectare site designated for the plantation.

“The project is aimed not only at establishing an olive plantation, but also at developing processing capacity and creating conditions for the production of value-added products,” the Agriculture Ministry said, summarizing the discussions.

The project is being developed under a memorandum of understanding signed between the Jizzakh regional administration and Water Con. The agreement provides for the establishment of a working group to organize preparatory activities, while the Pakistani company is expected to consider financing the plantation and necessary infrastructure.

Moreover, the sides discussed land and water availability and the technical requirements for implementing the project.

Following the meeting, the parties outlined further steps to conduct a detailed technical and organizational assessment, clarify land and water supply opportunities, and prepare an investment proposal for the project.

The proposed plantation could contribute to the development of Uzbekistan’s agricultural processing sector by combining crop production with local processing and finished-product manufacturing.

World.title: China and U.S. are world's two superpowers; there is no third - President Ilham Aliyev
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 3. China and the United States are the world's two superpowers; there is no third, President Ilham Aliyev said during his speech at the 8th Congress of the New Azerbaijan Party (YAP).

"We have strategic partnership declarations and agreements with many EU member states – Azerbaijan maintains such a format with 10 member states. I can say that two historic events have occurred recently: we established strategic partnership relations with both China and the United States. A comprehensive strategic partnership declaration was signed with China, and a Strategic Charter was signed with the United States. These are the world's two superpowers; there is no third. Matters are naturally discussed and competition exists between these countries, and establishing rules based on mutual understanding between them is a crucial factor for the whole world. Azerbaijan is a strategic partner to both of these superpowers.

Our population and territory are not large. What is it? This reflects the trust in us, the attitude toward us, and the belief in our word. There is no one left in the world who does not know that our word is as valuable as our signature. Whatever we say, we stand by it. We have never played double games, nor have we displayed hypocrisy or deceit toward any country – even though we have repeatedly faced such conduct ourselves and continue to face it today. But we can never be like them. We are people who respect ourselves; we live with dignity and conduct our policy with dignity. Through our example, everyone can see that this is possible: to defeat the enemy single-handedly, dictate your terms to the enemy, force them to sign an act of capitulation despite suffering 30 years of hardship, and then stop at the right time to achieve peace so that no more blood is shed. We do not need an eternal war; that was not our choice. In the Second Garabagh War, we stopped at the right time, and in September 2023, we also stopped at the right time, although various options existed. Strategic foresight, strategic thinking, and prioritizing the core interests of our people dictate this policy. There is no place for emotions in politics. If we had surrendered to emotions, today, a third Victory Arch would likely have been erected in the center of Yerevan," President Ilham Aliyev said.

World.title: Azerbaijan and Switzerland discuss cooperation on security (PHOTO)
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 3. Elchin Amirbayov, Representative of the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan on special assignments, discussed regional and international security issues, as well as prospects for bilateral cooperation in this area, with Gabriel Lüchinger, Swiss National Security Advisor, Trend reports.

According to the information, the meeting took place as part of Amirbayov’s working visit to the Swiss Confederation.

The parties exchanged views on the prospects for a peaceful resolution of ongoing armed conflicts in the Eurasian region. In addition, they explored opportunities to expand cooperation between Azerbaijan and Switzerland in the security sector, including on cybersecurity, hybrid threats, and other areas of mutual interest.

Meanwhile, security issues are regularly discussed within the framework of the Azerbaijan-Switzerland dialogue. In particular, in August 2026, Azerbaijani Foreign Minister Jeyhun Bayramov and the head of the Swiss Federal Department of Foreign Affairs and OSCE Chairperson-in-Office Ignazio Cassis focused on issues of regional security, energy security, and digital security during talks in Baku. Earlier, in March 2026, the foreign ministers of the two countries also discussed international and regional security during a telephone conversation, emphasizing the importance of resolving crises through diplomatic means.

World.title: Iran moves to regulate FX market through foreign currency sales
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 3. Starting today, four banks in Iran — Mellat, Tejarat, Saderat, and Saman — have begun selling foreign currency as part of measures to regulate the foreign exchange market.

According to the Central Bank of Iran, starting today, all Iranian citizens over the age of 18 can meet their foreign currency needs up to $10,000 by presenting a valid ID.

The Central Bank of Iran intends to provide up to $2 billion in foreign currency under this program. In the first phase, $1 billion worth of foreign currency will be sold to customers through banks and bank exchange offices.

Meanwhile, foreign currency prices relative to the Iranian rial have risen significantly recently amid the imposition of restrictions and sanctions against Iran, as well as various economic challenges.

The Central Bank of Iran’s current exchange rates show that 1 U.S. dollar is worth 1.75 million rials, 1 euro is worth 2.31 million rials, and 1 Azerbaijani manat is worth 1.03 million rials.

Moreover, on the black market, 1 U.S. dollar is bought and sold for 2.63 million rials, 1 euro for 2.96 million rials, and 1 Azerbaijani manat for 1.56 million rials.

World.title: Sharks could linger off Perth coast despite whale carcass removal
World.content:
Some of Perth's most seasoned swimmers are taking a break from the ocean after a whale carcass lured sharks close to shore, with an expert warning that the predators could be attracted to the area for weeks.

Several sharks have been spotted lurking off some of Perth's most popular beaches in recent days after a whale carcass washed up at City Beach on Monday, just over a week after a fatal shark attack at Sorrento Beach.

The City of Perth Surf Life Saving Club cancelled the Surf Life Saving WA (SLSWA) Enduro Championship at City Beach today, while placing all club-based training on hold until further notice.

City Beach remains closed after a beached whale attracted sharks to the area. (ABC News: Mya Kordic)

City Beach, Floreat Beach and Swanbourne Beach have all been closed.

But the heightened shark activity in recent days has also discouraged swimmers and surfers further along the coastline.

Cottesloe's community ocean swimming group PodSquad is taking a break from its daily 2-kilometre morning swim.

"Even though the [Cottesloe] beaches are open at the moment, we're taking a break for a few more days," the group's founder Shane McGurk said.

PodSquad founder Shane McGurk wants to see the shark tagging program expanded. (ABC News: Mya Kordic)

"Our numbers will drop off now, understandably — it's a very emotive issue. [Some] people have a different relationship with these sort of events, about how they manage.

"Some want to get straight back in [and get] back on the horse, so to speak, and others want to take a break and come to terms with the tragedy at Sorrento, and also the whale at City Beach."

Calls for more tagging, AI drones

Ahead of each summer, around the end of October, the Town of Cottesloe installs a shark barrier at Cottesloe Beach.

Third person killed by sharks in WA this year The often-heated debate over how to protect beachgoers from sharks is likely to get hotter after the death of a third person this year.

But this year, it is due to be installed a couple of weeks early — on Wednesday, depending on weather conditions and seaweed movement.

Mr McGurk said PodSquad members would initially swim within the enclosure when members returned to their morning routine, and they would like to see the enclosure installed early again next year.

The group also called for an expansion of the shark tagging program and for investment in AI-powered drones that are capable of identifying shark species when the animals come in close to shore.

He said that could enhance the data available to swimmers when they were making decisions about whether to get into the water.

"We just want to know where the sharks are, and when we know where the sharks are we can keep safe," he said.

Cottesloe volunteer surf lifesavers did the first patrol of the season on Saturday morning. (ABC News: Mya Kordic)

Sharks could linger for weeks

Curt Jenner from the Centre for Whale Research in Western Australia said while the whale carcass had been removed from City Beach, sharks could still be attracted to the area for weeks.

"Whales are full of blubber and that blubber will break down into oil very quickly and that gets straight into the sand," he said.

"Sharks are cued in, on a molecular level, to detect small traces of oils or blood or anything like that and so they'll be tasting that for weeks to come."

Centre for Whale Research director Curt Jenner says traces of the whale will attract sharks to the area for some time. (ABC News: Mya Kordic)

Mr Jenner said sharks were also attracted to the south-west coastline between September and December because that time was the peak of the southern migration for humpback whales.

The predators also follow other prey, such as blue fin tuna, into the southern ocean.

"If you were going to be cautious about being in the water, this is the time," Mr Jenner said.

World.title: David Fifita leads Australia in wild mismatch against PNG
World.content:
A rag-tag Australian side has outclassed Papua New Guinea 60-10 in the annual Prime Minister's XIII clash in Port Moresby.

The Australians scored 11 tries and exposed the PNG side's defensive frailties almost at will in what was the 20th men's Prime Minister's XIII match.

It was hardly a conventional game at the National Football Stadium on Saturday, with Australia switching on and off as players became accustomed to their makeshift position.

Ezra Mam spent time at fullback. Jock Madden appeared to be playing on an edge. Jamal Fogarty stood in the centres, and Josh Curran kicked a goal.

At one stage they had three regular hookers on the field.

In one piece of consistency, captain David Fifita started and finished the match as a devastating left centre.

Commentator Cooper Cronk mused it was coach Ben Teo's way of keeping the Aussies engaged after a long, hard season.

It was at times chaotic and they dropped the ball a lot, but it was fun. Less so for the PNG side, who were not just outclassed but also ill-disciplined, missing 47 tackles — 28 in the first half alone.

With the PNG Chiefs' arrival in the NRL fast approaching, it is clear the next level of local players are still a long way from that standard.

On a positive note, earlier on Saturday the Junior Kumuls scored a historic first win over the Australian Schoolboys, 18-10.

If Kangaroos coach Kevin Walters hasn't settled on his squad for this month's Rugby League World Cup, several players put their hands up.

Regular back-rower Fifita, who showed his class and power in the centres on Saturday, first appeared in the PM's XIII game seven years ago and looked destined for higher honours that never arrived. Maybe that time is approaching again.

Mam and fellow half Lachlan Galvin showed more than one glimpse of their brilliance, while hulking front-rower Tom Hazelton was one of the best players on the field.

For former NRL and current London Broncos coach Jason Demetriou, who will guide the PNG Kumuls at the World Cup, there was not a lot to love.

Sylvester Namo should be there, while uncapped centre Stanford Talita and fullback Sanny Wabo were dangerous at times and could find their way into Demetriou's squad.

In the women's game, Australia was also successful, dishing out a 66-6 thumping of their hosts.

The PNG women's Prime Minister's XIII scored a point for the first time in three years, but the Aussies still came out on top in a big way. (AAP: NRL Photos/Anthony Kourembanas)

PNG might have scored for the first time in three years, but Australia was a class above, crossing for 12 tries to one to rack up the biggest winning margin in the fixture's history.

While the standard of PNG's second-tier players has improved alongside the growth of the national women's competition, the Santos Cup, so too has that of the Australians.

Several showed they would not be out of place if called up to coach Jess Skinner's Jillaroos for this month's 2026 Rugby League World Cup.

Jada Taylor scored three tries and was almost impossible to handle at times, showing her versatility by playing on the wing, despite playing her club football at fullback.

Half Kasey Reh, centre Tahlia O'Brien, hooker Taneka Todhunter and back-rower Tayla Preston were others who impressed in what was effectively an audition in front of Skinner for a grander stage.

PNG Orchids coach Craig Sandercock, who this year guided Wests Tigers to their first NRLW finals series, would also have enjoyed the opportunity to see the next generation of PNG players.

There was no doubt they were outclassed, and they struggled for time with the ball, having just 37 per cent possession.

However, they had an 85 per cent completion rate and tried hard in defence, before tiring late in each half.

AAP

World.title: Tornado rips through NSW south coast, causing damage around Ulladulla
World.content:
A tornado has torn through parts of the New South Wales south coast, causing significant damage around Ulladulla.

Just after 1pm today, the region was issued with a severe thunderstorm warning for damaging winds, large hailstones and heavy rainfall.

The Bureau of Meteorology has confirmed a tornado did move through the area, describing the event as "very unusual".

Vision shows the rotating column of air making its way across a residential area.

In other vision from outside a local cafe, staff can be seen scrambling to remove tables and chairs before heavy rain and strong winds sweep through violently, sending umbrellas flying.

The NSW State Emergency Service (SES) said they had received more than 90 calls for assistance across the state, including 29 around Ulladulla.

Crews are responding to roofs being ripped from homes, dislodged tiles and skylights, and fallen trees and powerlines.

Dozens of properties have also being hit with power outages.

An SES incident management team has been set up in Ulladulla, with crews from nearby Nowra — which has received close to 17 millimetres of rain since 9am— and surrounding areas responding.

The SES expects calls for assistance to increase, with severe thunderstorms expected to continue into the evening.

World.title: One Nation promises law-and-order boost in Victorian campaign launch
World.content:
One Nation has launched its campaign for the Victorian state election, promising to fund law-and-order measures by scrapping the Suburban Rail Loop and Treaty.

One Nation Victoria leader Warren Pickering was joined at the launch by the party's national leader Pauline Hanson and its candidates for the upcoming election, as the party unveiled its policies.

The ABC was not invited to the campaign launch at Melbourne's Crown Casino, and was barred from entering the event.

Pauline Hanson's entrance was met with applause and cheers as attendees rushed to film on their phones. (ABC News)

The event heard speeches from the two leaders, MP Rickie-Lee Tyrrell and candidates Colleen Harkin and Mark Nicholson.

Mr Nicholson led the attendees in a rendition of Advance Australia Fair before making an impassioned speech, saying "if I have it my way, Dan Andrews and Jacinta Allan, they'll be in prison by Christmas".

Ms Hanson received a hero's welcome at the event, making an impassioned plea for the roughly 750 supporters in attendance to back the party's Victorian candidates.

Pauline Hanson invoked Ned Kelly and the Eureka Stockade during her speech in Melbourne. (ABC News)

"What I've provided is a vehicle; now you are the engine, now you drive it," Ms Hanson said.

The Queensland senator spent much of her speech attacking the incumbent Labor government's record on crime, corruption and Victoria's growing debt, saying Victorians had been "treated like mugs".

Victoria's election is nearly here — it's time to have Your Say Before Victorians head to the polls on November 28, we want to hear about what matters to you most.

She also addressed comments made by Premier Ben Carroll, who last month said that the rise of One Nation in Victoria terrified him.

"If you're listening, Ben, don't be scared of me. I tell you what mate, he should be scared of you," Ms Hanson said, pointing to the gathered crowd.

Support for One Nation has surged in Victoria, with polling suggesting the party will seriously challenge both Labor and the Coalition in the upcoming election.

One Nation pledges boosts to law and order

Law-and-order measures featured as the centrepiece of One Nation's policy launch on Saturday, taking up the first several pages of a 63-page policy booklet.

One Nation has promised heavy investment into law and order including bolstering police numbers by recruiting ADF veterans through an accelerated program.

"The policy that I'm most proud of, and probably the most important to Victoria, is our crime policy," Mr Pickering said.

"We're proposing to utilise some of the estimated 10,000 suitably qualified contemporary veterans in this state to lean into the police force."

Warren Pickering says he is most proud of One Nation's crime policy. (ABC News)

One Nation said it would target youth crime in the state by imposing harsher penalties on violent young offenders.

The party plans to reduce the age of criminal responsibility for children to 10 years old, charge young offenders of serious violent crimes as adults, and hold parents liable for fines and property damage caused by their children.

The party said it would introduce "carefully governed AI" to cut down on administrative burdens and free up frontline officers, while providing sign-on bonuses and accommodation allowances.

One Nation revealed its 2026 election policies at an event on Saturday. (ABC News)

The judicial system has also been targeted for major investment under One Nation with pledges to increase the number of magistrates, fund a 24-hour bail court and build three new magistrates' courts in Melbourne's outer suburbs in a bid to speed up the judicial process.

It also promised to introduce UK-style self-defence in the home laws, and explore a "tightly controlled trial" of giving Victorians legal access to capsicum spray.

Suburban Rail Loop, net zero and Treaty on the chopping block

One Nation said it would fund its investments with a range of cuts to government projects, agencies and services.

The party announced it would scrap the Suburban Rail Loop (SRL) project, diverting the funds to infrastructure such as the Airport Rail line and the electrification of the Melton line.

One Nation says the SRL project will be scrapped if it is elected. (Supplied)

Government agencies and public sector jobs would also be targeted for cuts under One Nation, with the party pledging to review the state's public entities and agencies, and introduce expiry dates for the bodies.

It also said First Peoples' representative body Gellung Warl would be abolished and the statewide Treaty scrapped.

Climate policies were also earmarked as targets for One Nation cuts.

The party pledged to scrap all net-zero targets and subsidies, cancel transmission projects such as the VNI West and Western Renewables Link and reverse the ban on gas connections in new homes.

One Nation supporters were displaying their allegiances proudly at the campaign launch. (ABC News)

One Nation said it would also repeal the statewide ban on nuclear energy.

But the party stopped short of committing to scrapping taxes, saying it would instead wind back land tax increases and increase the threshold for payroll tax.

Rival parties dismiss One Nation launch

Ms Hanson took aim at rival political parties during her speech on Saturday, saying Victorians now had trust issues with the Liberal Party and that the opposition had not done its job.

The ABC guide to the 2026 Victorian election To learn more about the key electorates, candidates and swing seats in the coming election, head to this guide from the ABC's Chief Elections and Data Analyst Casey Briggs.

When asked about those comments, Opposition Leader Jess Wilson refused to mention Ms Hanson's party by name.

"I know that Victorians are looking for a change of government this year, and the only way to do that is to elect a Liberal and Nationals government," Ms Wilson said.

Government minister Nick Staikos dismissed the campaign launch by One Nation on Saturday entirely, saying it was "not a serious political party".

"We don't share anything in common with that party, we will not be making deals with that party," Mr Staikos said.

"They are importing the worst of American politics to our state."

About two dozen protesters rallied outside Crown in Melbourne in opposition to One Nation. (ABC News)

A small group of protesters was seen outside the One Nation event on Saturday, with about two dozen people holding signs and banners claiming that the party was racist.

"We've seen Hanson calling for an end to immigration, she says mass immigration is a problem and we think that's absolutely scapegoating the problems," protester Julie Monteiro said.

World.title: Olympic star takes on challengers at pool's grand reopening
World.content:
Diane Kasprzak is very fond of Glenorchy War Memorial pool.

"When my children were young, I used to bring them to this pool," Ms Kasprzak said.

"And at 14 years of age, my daughter met her future husband, and they're still happily married 28 years later.

" Her daughter is now one of the first lifesavers here. "

Loading

Ms Kasprzak was one of hundreds lapping up the pool's reopening weekend on Saturday.

Built in the 1960s and dedicated to those who served in World War II, the Glenorchy pool was closed in 2023 after an independent report identified a number of safety issues.

Memories of Hobart's last outdoor public pool All three of Hobart's public 50m swimming pools used to be outside, but the only one left won't open this summer — and could close permanently.

Among the problems identified were faults in the pool shell, structural issues with the concrete grandstand and an urgent need to update the electrical switchboard.

The pool was facing long-term closure, but the community rallied to keep it open.

Now, three years later and after $7.5 million of repairs, it's reopened just in time for summer.

Glenorchy Mayor Sue Hickey said it had been a long time coming.

"It's been an extraordinary amount of work … everything from the electrics, the plumbing, the painting," Cr Hickey said.

A swimming carnival at the Glenorchy Pool, sometime in the 1980s. (Supplied: Anne Henderson)

Another image of the pool, from the 1980s. (Supplied: Anne Henderson)

"We've even had staff right up until late at night cleaning things, making sure everything was spectacular for the opening — even shooing away a few ducks.

" It's been three long summers that [the community has] missed their pool and now they have it back in all its glory. "

Test your speed against an Olympic medallist

Among the offerings at Saturday's celebrations was a chance to race against Olympic bronze medallist and Tassie local, Max Giuliani.

Giuliani said there was a real chance there were some prospective Olympians in the midst.

"I've lost a few races today," he said.

"There's been a couple of guys that I didn't think would be very good at swimming - I've given them 25 metres ahead of me and they've smoked me to the wall.

" You never know which day is your last, and if I lose any more, I may have to retire. "

600-plus sausages sizzled

Glenorchy City Council alderman Steve King spent much of the day working the barbecue — an offering so popular that volunteers had to make a quick dash to the supermarket.

"I was here 60 years ago as a kid, and then my daughter's here and my grandson, so three generations at the pool. It's just great," he said.

He quipped the only disappointment of the day was his performance against Giuliani.

"[Giuliani] gave me half the length of the pool, and I was halfway down my half length, so three quarters of the way, and something went past me like a rocket and I gave up," he said.

" I was shattered. "

Long-term solution still needed

While celebrating the pool's reopening and upgrades, Mayor Sue Hickey said it wasn't a forever fix.

Loading...

She said the council was still pursuing financial backing for a new aquatic centre, which has been costed at $84 million.

"We're still aware that this is a very old facility," she said.

"Whilst we've done absolutely everything we can to ensure [Glenorchy War Memorial Pool] is open for as long as we possibly can, we do know that in the future we have a desperate need for a full aquatic centre."

World.title: Saints hit rock bottom, Essendon claim breakthrough AFLW victory
World.content:
St Kilda have kicked just a single point, the club's lowest ever score in an AFLW match, as the Western Bulldogs scored a 30-point victory in Ballarat.

Incredibly, the Saints only managed the behind in the final 90 seconds of the game in a horror afternoon for the winless club.

The Bulldogs were barely better in tough conditions in Ballarat, with sideways rain and winds limiting the hosts to just three goals 13 on a day were accuracy in front of goal suffered.

Rylie Wilcox, Sarah Hartwig and Cleo Buttifant scored the goals for the Bulldogs, while Isabelle Pritchard (35 disposals, six clearances) was outstanding in the testing, cold conditions.

For the Saints, only Ashleigh Richards's point spared the cellar dwellers the ignominy of a bagel.

Earlier, star midfielder Madison Prespakis steered battling Essendon to an eight-point comeback victory over GWS for its first win of the season.

Essendon recorded its first win of the 2026 AFLW season. (Getty Images: AFL Photos/Mark Metcalfe)

The Giants got out to a game-high 25-point lead at the start of the third quarter and appeared on track for a second win of the season, before Prespakis kicked into overdrive and the Bombers lifted their pressure.

The star on-baller racked up 13 disposals, six contested possessions, three clearances and a goal in the third term to put Essendon on her back and inspire a terrific 6.7 (43) to 5.5 (35) comeback at Henson Park on Saturday afternoon.

"Genuinely just so proud of the resilience of the group," skipper Bonnie Toogood told Fox Sports.

"And it's been a challenging season, I suppose, and the persistence through adversity, particularly today.

"The first half wasn't what we were planning on, but to come out in the third like we did and just big moments by individuals — bloody inspiring."

The victory relieves some pressure on Bombers coach Natalie Wood and leaves St Kilda as the league's only winless team.

It was a devastating loss for Cam Bernasconi's Giants, who kicked five of the first six goals then only scored one point in a second half where they were completely overwhelmed by Essendon's manic pressure.

Madison Prespakis was sensational, with 13 disposals, six contested possessions, three clearances and a goal as the Bombers came from behind. (Getty Images: Jason McCawley)

Essendon had trailed by just four points at the final change when star forward Toogood gave the Bombers a massive rev-up at the huddle.

"I'm passionate and emotional all the time — it could be the Italian in me," Toogood said.

"They were on the back foot … I was like, 'We've got 'em — lean into that, we've got them, our football is working.'"

Essendon hit the front when it went from end to end and Daria Bannister tumbled home a long-range goal.

Then Emily Gough kicked a terrific checkside from a forward-50 stoppage that sealed victory.

Prespakis finished with a mammoth 35 disposals and five clearances, and she was well supported by Maddi Gay (21 disposals) and Georgia Gee (15), along with ruck Steph Wales (20 disposals, 14 hitouts, eight clearances).

Toogood (eight marks, one goal) and Gough (two goals) were influential in attack, while Alex Morcom and Amy Gaylor (nine intercepts apiece) were strong down back.

The Giants' best were Alyce Parker (25 disposals, eight tackles, two goals), Tilly Lucas-Rodd (26) and Cambridge McCormick (22).

Essendon (16th, 1-7) face the finals-chasing Western Bulldogs at Whitten Oval on Friday, while GWS (15th, 1-7) have the daunting task of facing red-hot Geelong at Kardinia Park next Saturday.

AAP/ABC

World.title: FOMO and 4am wake-up call get Pallister in the ocean
World.content:
Is there anything Lani Pallister can't do?

On Friday night, Pallister wrapped up a hugely successful Australian short course championships with a fourth gold medal in the 800-metre freestyle to seal her spot in the 24-strong squad for the world championships.

Then, the 24-year-old rushed up to Queensland's Sunshine Coast to claim honours in the 1.2-kilometre Bluff to Bar ocean swim at Alexandra Headland on Saturday morning, after a 4am wake-up call.

"I'd get really bad FOMO [fear of missing out]," Pallister said when asked why she made the trip.

"It's important to give back … Alexandra Heads Surf Club helped make me the athlete I am today."

Lani Pallister won her third-straight Bluff to Bar race. (Supplied: Alexandra Headland Surf Lifesaving Club)

Pallister's dedication to her surf club cannot be doubted after she posted a story on her Instagram feed tagged at 4:38am to get her flight for an 11:20am race on the Sunshine Coast.

And the Paris Olympian made sure the early wake up was worth it, leading a stacked field from start to finish to claim a third-straight victory in the event.

Competing in a point-to-point ocean swim couldn't have been more different from the 125 tumble turns she completed in competition at the Sydney Olympic Park Aquatic Centre in the past four days.

Pallister competed in every freestyle event from 100m to 1,500m, winning gold in all but the 100m, where she finished second.

That ensured that she would be the headline act for the Dolphins squad named for the Beijing world championships from December 1-6.

The squad includes six debutants: Amelie Smith, Mark Nikolaev, Marcus Da Silva, Emily Jones, Cameron Bladen and Alex Quach.

Lani Pallister (left) and Jenna Forrester both had excellent championships. (Supplied: Swimming Australia/Delly Carr)

Head Dolphins coach Rohan Taylor noted Pallister's performance as a stand-out in Sydney, with Sam Short's clean sweep of the 400m, 800m and 1,500m freestyle and Jenna Forrester's four silvers and a gold also worthy of mention.

"Those three without a doubt have been stand-outs here," Taylor said.

"But also it's been great to see the likes of Amelie Smith and Marcus Da Silva come through the ranks and shift the dial.

"Also credit to Mark Nikolaev; it's a credit to his consistency and perseverance that he has earned his Dolphin number tonight.

"The international exposure in Beijing is an opportunity to come together and build towards LA 2028 and the meet presents a great opportunity for our younger swimmers to learn from established Dolphins."

Lani Pallister won the 200, 400, 800 and 1,500m freestyle events at the Australian short course championships. (Supplied: Swimming Australia/Delly Carr)

Speaking of experienced Dolphins, Cam McEvoy is also set to join the Aussie team in Beijing, despite not competing at the national championships this week.

World Aquatics is offering wildcard spots for the world championships to any to any swimmer who finishes on the podium of an individual final during the the World Cup series.

The 32-year-old long course world record holder duly set a new national short course record of 20.22 for the 50m freestyle to win gold on the opening night of the 2026 World Cup series in Baku, Azerbaijan, on Friday.

Pallister will now head for an altitude training camp in Flagstaff, USA, before the world championships, which represents her ninth Australian Dolphins selection.

"Off to altitude in a couple of weeks' time, and then just pretty much getting back into full training, knuckling down and targeting world champs," Pallister said during the short course titles.

"I didn't really anticipate fast swimming this week. I was actually pretty shocked with the 200 being plus 0.2, so [I'm] pretty happy."

Dolphins World Championships squad

Iona Anderson, Ben Armbruster, Cameron Bladen*, Brittany Castelluzzo, Josh Collett, Isaac Cooper, Marcus Da Silva*, Jenna Forrester, Max Giuliani, Emily Jones*, Tara Kinder, Mark Nikolaev*, Lani Pallister, Alexandria Perkins, William Petric, Alex Quach*, David Schlicht, Sam Short, Amelie Smith*, Flynn Southam, Stuart Swinburn, Matt Temple, Olivia Wunsch, Josh Yong.

*debut Dolphins squad

World.title: Highway potholes puncture tyres after Victoria's latest bout of rain
World.content:
A woman has stood in the rain along a busy Victorian highway to warn more than 50 drivers of a large pothole that took out her tyre, and damaged at least five other cars in Gippsland this morning.

Large sharp-edged potholes have opened up along Victorian roads and highways after heavy rain across the state since Thursday night.

At Rosedale, Karen Ester was on her way to Leongatha on the Princes Highway, when she heard a loud bang after hitting a pothole filled with water.

"I couldn't avoid it without trying to cause a crash into somebody else," she said.

Ms Ester said potholes had been a problem on regional roads for too long.

"It's like they're only doing a lot of patch-up jobs, and as soon as you get a big downpour of rain, it's washed out anyway," she said.

" We are expected to have our cars roadworthy, but the roads aren't roadworthy. "

Karen Ester's flat tyre after she struck a pothole on the Princes Highway between Rosedale and Sale. (ABC News: Lily Kristanto)

Rebecca Billing's family were driving back from a holiday at Golden Beach in the state's east when they hit two potholes in their brand new car.

The family from Geelong had to get their car towed to a nearby town.

Ms Billing said the state of the roads had discouraged her from wanting to travel in the state.

"When you're driving at these sort of speeds, plus you've got to deal with the weather, plus kangaroos … it's really sort of turned us off wanting to travel in Victoria because it's just dangerous.

"It's not worth it."

Andy Gaudion's family were left waiting in the rain when their car hit a pothole and blew two tyres.

Andy Gaudion's family struck a pothole and got a flat tyre on the Princes Highway in Gippsland. (ABC News: Lily Kristanto)

"It was a giant bang … it scared all of us," the 12-year-old said.

"We pulled over, got out, we were all annoyed, stunned.

" We've hit potholes before but not this bad; this one has been the worst one we've hit. "

Pothole anger likely at polling booths

There has been growing community anger over the state of Victorian roads with the issue likely to be front of mind for voters when they head to the polls in November.

Large potholes, including this one on the Princes Highway near Rosedale, have opened up after rain. (ABC News: Lily Kristanto)

Last month, motorcyclist Peter "Tiki" Mason, 71, died after hitting a pothole on the Western Highway near Trawalla.

In August, dozens of cars were forced off the road after hitting large potholes that opened up along the Princes Freeway at Bunyip in Victoria's east.

The Victorian Coalition has promised to invest $5 billion to rebuild the state's roads, if elected in November, by establishing Better Roads Victoria as a standalone division within the Department of Transport and Planning.

Victorian Premier Ben Carroll has attempted to quell the anger over potholes by promising to double the number of potholes the government fixes on the state's roads this year from 250,000 to 500,000 at a cost of $352 million.

But former VicRoads staff told the ABC the privatisation of the state's road-building had led to the decline as had a reliance on flexible pavement comprising crushed rock compacted and then sealed.

A recent auditor-general's report found almost half of Victoria's state-managed roads were in very poor condition.

In a statement, the Minister for Roads and Road Safety, Paul Hamer, said if Labor is re-elected it will develop a plan to put the government back in charge of state road maintenance, from third party contractors.

In the statement, Mr Hamer said the government would give the five road maintenance regions, Barwon South West, Loddon Mallee Hume, Gippsland, Inner Metro and Greater Metro more power to prioritise local repairs.

World.title: What we know about the crash into the Newcastle Knights crowd
World.content:
Updated PoliticsNSWTraffic incident What we know about the crash into the Newcastle Knights crowd Lia Timson Updated October 3, 2026 — 6:52pm ,first published 1:00pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Follow our live coverage here

Read our full report here Multiple people were injured when a car crashed into a crowd of football fans who had come out to farewell the Newcastle Knights rugby league team bus in Wallsend on Saturday morning. Here is everything we know about the incident. Thousands of fans were lining the bus route for the farewell. Sitthixay Ditthavong What happened in Wallsend? Newcastle Knights fans lined the streets of Wallsend, near Newcastle, on Saturday morning to send off their team before their trip south to Sydney for Sunday’s grand final against the Sydney Roosters.



People of all ages were gathered on Newcastle Link Road at the Transfield Drive roundabout in Wallsend about 9.30am when a BMW struck the crowd. Emergency services were called. NSW Police said a large emergency services response involved officers from the Newcastle City Police District, Traffic and Highway Patrol Command officers and NSW Ambulance paramedics. The driver of the BMW was arrested at the scene. Police do not believe the incident was targeted, and are investigating if the driver lost control of his vehicle in the moments before the collision. How many people were injured?



Three young girls were among 10 people injured after they were struck by the car. One of the victims, a five-year-old girl, was still in a critical condition in Newcastle’s John Hunter Hospital on Saturday evening. Another patient was in a serious but stable condition, while five others were in a stable condition. A further three had been discharged from hospital. Paramedics prepare to transport the injured by helicopter. Sitthixay Ditthavong What did the police say?



Police do not believe the incident was targeted or terror related, and are investigating if the driver, an 18-year-old P-plater, lost control of his vehicle in the moments before the collision. The teenager was arrested at the scene of the crash and taken to hospital for mandatory drug and alcohol testing. Police say he was driving “erratically” and is expected to be charged over the crash this weekend.

NSW Police Assistant Commissioner David Waddell told reporters that two other people were in the car at the time of the crash and had to be removed from the scene after witnesses became hostile.

“We had to get the three of them out of there because the crowd did turn on them,” Waddell said Newcastle Mayor Gavin Morris said the driver was believed to be a fan of the Newcastle Knights, who allegedly lost control of the vehicle. “I’ve spoken to the authorities, a number of which, and look, first of all, it is under investigation, and the young driver is now with police, so it appears that he was revving the car in some form. He was excited. He was a supporter. He was, you know, a fan,” Morris told ABC television this morning. The driver was arrested at the scene.



Police at the scene. Sitthixay Ditthavong Have the Newcastle Knights responded? Newcastle Knights captain Kalyn Ponga led tributes to those injured in the crash. “Our hearts are with everyone affected in Wallsend this morning,” Ponga said on social media. “We’re thinking of you, your families and everyone in our Newcastle community. Sending our love and support x.” Chief executive Peter Parr expressed his deep concern and support for those impacted, while thanking fans, police and medical staff.



“We want to thank our incredible fans for the passion and support they showed our team this morning. The scenes across Newcastle demonstrated once again what this football club means to our community,” he said. Parr thanked the response of first responders, police and the doctors and nurses caring for patients at John Hunter Hospital. The club said their thoughts were with everyone impacted by the incident, including those at the scene and their families. “Respectfully, now this is a matter for New South Wales Police, so at this stage, the club can make no further comment,” as spokesman for the club said as the team arrived in Sydney on Saturday. Loading Australian Rugby League Commission executive chairman Peter V’landys said he was deeply saddened by the incident and his thoughts were with the injured. Asked if the incident would impact on the plans for the grand final in Sydney on Sunday night, V’landys said: “We’re just concerned about the victims at the moment, that’s all we’re focusing on.”



What has been the wider reaction? Prime Minister Anthony Albanese thanked emergency services and police for responding so quickly. “My thoughts are with everyone injured or involved in the horrible incident this morning in Newcastle. Rugby league brings people together, and this should have been a weekend of excitement and pride for Newcastle fans,” Albanese said. Morris, the mayor who said it was really upsetting, also said: “What began as a morning of pride and celebration for Novocastrians to support our Newcastle Knights has now been marked by a very serious incident, and as a community, we’re heartbroken ... This terrible incident is hard, and it’s okay to feel it. In the days and weeks ahead, we as the Newcastle and Hunter community need to come together with heart, soul and empathy. We are a strong community and we will support each other.” NSW Premier Chris Minns said it was “heartbreaking to see fans who were sending off their grand final team involved in such a terrible incident. We’ve seen how this grand final has brought the Newcastle together, and I hope the whole community remains united as we continue to respond.”



With Julie Power, Megan Gorrey, Riley Walter, Emily Kowal and Tom Decent. Our Breaking News Alert will notify you of significant breaking news when it happens. Get it here.

World.title: ‘Do you want the filtered version?’ Trainer’s head in a spin after Melham’s close call
World.content:
SportRacingVictorian racing ‘Do you want the filtered version?’ Trainer’s head in a spin after Melham’s close call Danny Russell October 3, 2026 — 6:49pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Experienced group 1 jockey Ben Melham almost caused the sensation of the spring by losing an unlosable race on a day that trainer Andrea Leek emerged from a tough six weeks involving her husband’s three-year ban to experience her greatest high. Melham sent an audible gasp across the rain-soaked Flemington lawn on Saturday when he eased up 25 metres from the finishing post on favourite Skybird with the group 2 Gilgai Stakes seemingly in his grasp. Skybird and Ben Melham took out the Gilgai Stakes at Flemington on Saturday – just. Getty Images But as Skybird throttled down, the six-year-old mare was almost nabbed on the line and beaten by the fast-finishing Smooth Chino, causing winning trainer Mitchell Freedman an unwelcome fright. “I said to guys just before, ‘Do you want the honest opinion or the filtered version?’,” Freedman said after the close call.



“She’s got a big handbrake on her. When you stop, she stops. I think we were pretty lucky that the visiting rider [on Smooth Chino] mistimed the winning post a little bit there, otherwise he might have got over the top of us. Related Article Victorian racing Trainer pleads to move back home after lying about having a ‘leak’ and copping a three-year ban “Anyway, we’ll take the win. We’re relieved, and we’re happy to get the win. I think she deserved it.” Melham pleaded guilty to a stewards charge of failing to ride his mount out to the end of the race and was fined $2000. In an interesting twist, the rider of the runner-up, Western Australian jockey Austin Galati, was also fined $1000 by stewards for failing to ride his mount out to the end of the race.



There were no such heart-in-mouth moments for Leek as she took out the feature race of the day, the group 1 Turnbull Stakes, with Perth gelding Cosmic Crusader. The comfortable victory on a heavy track provided a welcome respite six weeks after her husband, John Leek jnr, was disqualified from the sport for three years for attempting to stomach tube a horse. View post on X The victory also vindicated a decision by big-time Perth owner Bob Peters to send Cosmic Crusader across the Nullarbor to be prepared by Leek at her Nar Nar Goon North base for a shot at the spring riches. “I think I’ve been lucky to have this focus,” Leek said on Saturday after her first group 1 win.



“It’s been tough on the family and I have just focused on my horses and that is what has got me through.” While Leek waits for Racing Victoria to hear an application for her husband to be allowed to move back to their family home – currently disallowed under the rules of racing because she is a trainer – Cosmic Crusader is sure to provide some welcome distractions. Jockey Willie Pike and trainer Andrea Leek were congratulated by owner Bob Peters (right) after Cosmic Crusader’s win. Getty Images After comfortably beating rivals Light Infantry Man (second), Aeliana (third) and pre-race favourite Sir Delius (fourth), the six-year-old gelding has emerged as a key chance in the Cox Plate, to be raced at Flemington in three weeks’ time. “He’s a tricky horse, but I sent a message to Bob this morning, ‘There’s no excuses today, he’s spot on’, and thank God I was right,” Leek said.



“I galloped him one morning at Pakenham, and it was about a heavy 15. The tracks were closed, and they were good enough to let us work him because he was going into one of his previous races. “He went across the top of it like it was a good track. I was pretty confident he would handle the wet.” View post on X The win was also vindication for Perth jockey Willie Pike, who copped criticism from several form experts last month for his ride on the horse – finishing third in the group 1 Memsie Stakes at Caulfield. At the time, Pike did not like what he heard, firing back at his detractors and telling them to mind their own business. He was more considerate after winning the Turnbull Stakes.



“First of all, thank you to Mr Peters and his family,” Pike said. “They were backing me from the get-go even when I put in a bit of an iffy one a couple of starts ago. Jamie Melham aboard Half Yours at Flemington. Getty Images “It is really nice to get the job done. He was putting in those good runs without getting the job done, so I really like to get it done for him.” While last year’s Cups hero Half Yours finished solidly in fifth, jockey Jamie Melham was suspended for 10 race meetings for careless riding and will miss next week’s Caulfield Guineas meeting. She will return in time to defend her Caulfield Cup crown on Half Yours. It was another bountiful day for the Ciaron Maher mega stable, which took out feature staying races in Sydney and Melbourne – Mr Monaco won the 2500m The Bart Cummings at Flemington, while Juja Kibo won the 2400m Metropolitan at Randwick.



The victory means Mr Monaco wins a golden ticket into the Melbourne Cup, and Maher was full of praise for young Tasmanian jockey Jabez Johnstone. “It’s exciting to get another one into the Cup, but Jabez, he’s a little ripper,” Maher said. “I get on with him quite well. He’s usually a man of few words and I don’t mind that either. It was a good positive ride, and he’s strong.” News, results and expert analysis from the weekend of sport sent every Monday.

World.title: Tempted destroys Premiere rivals to issue warning to world’s best
World.content:
SportRacingHorse racing Tempted destroys Premiere rivals to issue warning to world’s best Craig Kerry October 3, 2026 — 6:31pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Tempted ensured she will be wearing Godolphin’s colours again in the $20 million Everest with another stunning win on Saturday and her team believe there is more to come when she steps up against Ka Ying Rising again. A $1.60 favourite after an easy win in the Concorde Stakes (1000m), the four-year-old mare was even more impressive in the Premiere Stakes (1200m) on Saturday, storming to a three-length victory over the top of Savvy Hallie in the final Everest lead-in. Tempted toys with her rivals in the Premiere Stakes. Getty Images Tempted was runner-up last year to Ka Ying Rising and looms as the main challenger again to the Hong Kong superstar on October 17. Godolphin Australia racing and bloodstock manager Jason Walsh said she would be racing in the powerhouse operation’s slot again.



“They are easy to watch like that,” Walsh said. “She’s a special mare, there’s no doubt about that. It was lovely to see her do it that way. “She’ll carry our colours and, as she did last year, when she carried them so well, and it’s pretty clear she’s in even better form, so we look forward to contesting the title again. “She did last year, and she’s furnished mentally and physically this time. She’s getting close to the finished article and she’ll definitely make her presence felt in a couple of weeks.” Trainer Ciaron Maher’s NSW assistant, Johann Gerard-Dubord, said Ka Ying Rising will need to be at his best to hold out Tempted.



“It’s a very good field, and she made them look like they’re nothing special, but it’s a genuine group one field,” Gerard-Dubord said. “The way she quickens, which is her best asset, she is one of a kind. Everything she does is very special. “She’ll have to be very special in two weeks, but we’ll be spot on for that. Ka Ying at his best, he’s very hard to beat, but he’ll have to be at his best. “Every horse is beatable on a day, and there’s more there. She quickens very well, but every time she gets to the front, she still waits for them, so if she’s got something to chase for a bit longer, I think there’s a bit more there.” Earlier, Inglis announced Stradbroke Handicap winner Spicy Martini as its Everest runner about the same time it emerged Golden Slipper winner Guest House was out for the spring.



Guest House was in line to fill the Everest slot of Coolmore, which paid about $30 million for the Home Affairs colt, but trainers Mick Price and Michael Kent jnr revealed the three-year-old had sustained a soft tissue injury to its near hind leg at trackwork on Saturday morning and would be spelled. Related Article Horse racing Sargent sticks solid with Gibbons for drought-breaking group 1 Inglis had already locked in Spicy Martini and announced the news at 1pm. An $8000 Inglis Digital buy for trainer Toby Edmonds and his partner Holly Penfold in March 2023 as a yearling, the five-year-old mare has won six times in just 13 starts and earned more than $2.7 million. She was beaten three-quarters of a length last start when fourth first-up in The Shorts (1100m) at Randwick two weeks ago. Regular jockey Taylor Marshall will keep ride, rounding off the all-Queensland team. Spicy Martini was $51 for the Everest before the announcement. “We have had an eye on her for some time and believe she is capable of posting a career-best effort in The Everest,” Inglis Bloodstock CEO Sebastian Hutch said. “She has run a new peak figure each start this year – including a group 1 victory in the Stradbroke - which tells us she is headed on an upward trajectory.”
