World.title: Ten people injured, P-plater arrested after car crashes into Newcastle Knights fans
World.content:
A five-year-old girl was left fighting for her life and nine others were injured when a teenage P-plate driver allegedly lost control of his car and careered into jubilant crowds lining a Newcastle street to wave the Knights off to the NRL grand final. One of the injured, Chris Clancy, said the car appeared to speed up as it went through a roundabout, and then lost control on the wet road. “No-one had time to move,” he said. “I thought I was going to die, it happened so fast.” Fans at the crash site rushed to provide first aid as emergency crews rushed to the scene and word of the collision spread through the tens of thousands of excited fans waiting for a glimpse of their team. The team’s bus, which had not yet departed when the crash occurred, was rerouted, and players were informed. Loading “They were shocked, it was a very sombre bus ride,” said one of those aboard. “Our fans mean everything to us. For that to happen; horrible.”



The five-year-old girl was in a critical condition in John Hunter Hospital on Saturday evening. One patient was in a serious but stable condition, and five were stable. Three had been discharged. Police arrested the 18-year-old driver at the crash site and took him for mandatory drug and alcohol testing. They said the incident was not believed to be targeted or terror-related. The teen was known to them. NSW Police Assistant Commissioner David Waddell said officers were investigating reports the P-plater had been “driving erratically” before he lost control of the vehicle. Footage posted to social media depicted the BMW careering around the roundabout moments before the crash, as shocked onlookers were heard screaming. The driver is expected to be charged, but no charges had been laid at the time of publication. The crash scene. TNV



Scenes at Wallsend, Newcastle, after a car crashed into a crowd of Knights supporters. Onlookers expressed anger towards the occupants of the car after the crash, police said. “We had to get the three of them out of there because the crowd did turn on them,” Waddell said. Witness Dean Liddell said he could hear the vehicle coming towards the crowd and then “all hell broke loose”. “I watched the little girl get dragged underneath the car. Seeing the whole scene unfold, it took me 10 minutes until I could say anything to anyone,” Liddell said. He said the crowd grabbed the driver from the wreck and a scuffle began before police intervened.



“If the copper wasn’t there the driver would have had massive injuries as well,” he said. The accident came after a joyous week in Newcastle, where the city threw its support behind a team that has not won a premiership for 25 years. The Knights had been expected to be inspired by the joy of their supporters during the grand final, but will now also feel the weight of the tragedy when they take the field. Newcastle Knights captain Kalyn Ponga said on social media that players “hearts are with everyone affected” by the crash. “We’re thinking of you, your families and everyone in our Newcastle community.” Longtime league watchers say no other grand final has been played under such a shadow. “It’s heartbreaking for the whole rugby league community, not just in Newcastle,” said Brad Fittler, a former Roosters captain and a member of the league hall of fame. “We’ve never seen anything like this ahead of a grand final and it puts everything in perspective.”



Australian Rugby League Commission executive chairman Peter V’Landys said he was deeply saddened by the crash. When asked whether it would affect plans for Sunday night’s game, he said “we’re just concerned about the victims at the moment.” Paramedics prepare to transport the injured by helicopter. Sitthixay Ditthavong The Premier Chris Minns said it was heartbreaking to see fans who were sending off their grand final team involved in such a terrible incident. “My thoughts are with the families and friends of loved ones who have been involved or injured in the crash. I also want to thank emergency services including police and ambulance who are responding to this tragedy”, the premier said. “We’ve seen how this grand final has brought the Newcastle together, and I hope the whole community remains united as we continue to respond.”



Newcastle Lord Mayor Gavin Morris said that, before Saturday’s crash, the lead-up to the grand final had been one of the “most incredibly joyous weeks in our city”. “It’s a tragedy. It’s something that we can’t take back,” Morris said. Morris said that passing vehicles were “revving up the crowd” as they drove past thousands of Knights fans lining the roadside before the crash. “That just should not have been occurring, but it has,” he said.



Asked whether bollards or fencing should have been installed at the roadside to protect fans, Morris said securing the 20-kilometre stretch of road between the Knight’s home ground and the crash site was “almost an impossible task”. The injured Clancy said a police vehicle was stationed near the crash site, and responded quickly. He said the car came at the group of supporters too fast for them to jump out of the way. He was hit by the front of the vehicle. Knights fan Jed Partridge, 29, who arrived at 8.20am to join thousands of others in waving off the team bus, was among fans who watched the celebration turn to shock. “We were on the side of the road, just waiting. Everyone was happy and then there was a real flurry of cop cars, ambos and rescue cars shooting past.” He said word soon filtered out that there had been a serious crash. “It was eerie … such a positive thing could quickly turn to this. It’s hard to wrap your head around.” Fans urged the Knights to press forward and do their best on Sunday night. “It will be tough for them, but do what they’ve always done and do it for the town,” said Clancy. “I believe they can win. Regardless of whether they win or lose, they’ve done the town proud.”

He was excited. He was a supporter. He was, you know, a fan,” Morris told ABC television this morning. The driver was arrested at the scene.



Police at the scene. Sitthixay Ditthavong Have the Newcastle Knights responded? Newcastle Knights captain Kalyn Ponga led tributes to those injured in the crash. “Our hearts are with everyone affected in Wallsend this morning,” Ponga said on social media. “We’re thinking of you, your families and everyone in our Newcastle community. Sending our love and support x.” Chief executive Peter Parr expressed his deep concern and support for those impacted, while thanking fans, police and medical staff.



“We want to thank our incredible fans for the passion and support they showed our team this morning. The scenes across Newcastle demonstrated once again what this football club means to our community,” he said. Parr thanked the response of first responders, police and the doctors and nurses caring for patients at John Hunter Hospital. The club said their thoughts were with everyone impacted by the incident, including those at the scene and their families. “Respectfully, now this is a matter for New South Wales Police, so at this stage, the club can make no further comment,” as spokesman for the club said as the team arrived in Sydney on Saturday. Loading Australian Rugby League Commission executive chairman Peter V’landys said he was deeply saddened by the incident and his thoughts were with the injured. Asked if the incident would impact on the plans for the grand final in Sydney on Sunday night, V’landys said: “We’re just concerned about the victims at the moment, that’s all we’re focusing on.”



What has been the wider reaction? Prime Minister Anthony Albanese thanked emergency services and police for responding so quickly. “My thoughts are with everyone injured or involved in the horrible incident this morning in Newcastle. Rugby league brings people together, and this should have been a weekend of excitement and pride for Newcastle fans,” Albanese said. Morris, the mayor who said it was really upsetting, also said: “What began as a morning of pride and celebration for Novocastrians to support our Newcastle Knights has now been marked by a very serious incident, and as a community, we’re heartbroken ... This terrible incident is hard, and it’s okay to feel it. In the days and weeks ahead, we as the Newcastle and Hunter community need to come together with heart, soul and empathy. We are a strong community and we will support each other.” NSW Premier Chris Minns said it was “heartbreaking to see fans who were sending off their grand final team involved in such a terrible incident. We’ve seen how this grand final has brought the Newcastle together, and I hope the whole community remains united as we continue to respond.”



With Julie Power, Megan Gorrey, Riley Walter, Emily Kowal and Tom Decent. Our Breaking News Alert will notify you of significant breaking news when it happens. Get it here.

World.title: ‘Do you want the filtered version?’ Trainer’s head in a spin after Melham’s close call
World.content:
SportRacingVictorian racing ‘Do you want the filtered version?’ Trainer’s head in a spin after Melham’s close call Danny Russell October 3, 2026 — 6:49pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Experienced group 1 jockey Ben Melham almost caused the sensation of the spring by losing an unlosable race on a day that trainer Andrea Leek emerged from a tough six weeks involving her husband’s three-year ban to experience her greatest high. Melham sent an audible gasp across the rain-soaked Flemington lawn on Saturday when he eased up 25 metres from the finishing post on favourite Skybird with the group 2 Gilgai Stakes seemingly in his grasp. Skybird and Ben Melham took out the Gilgai Stakes at Flemington on Saturday – just. Getty Images But as Skybird throttled down, the six-year-old mare was almost nabbed on the line and beaten by the fast-finishing Smooth Chino, causing winning trainer Mitchell Freedman an unwelcome fright. “I said to guys just before, ‘Do you want the honest opinion or the filtered version?’,” Freedman said after the close call.



“She’s got a big handbrake on her. When you stop, she stops. I think we were pretty lucky that the visiting rider [on Smooth Chino] mistimed the winning post a little bit there, otherwise he might have got over the top of us. Related Article Victorian racing Trainer pleads to move back home after lying about having a ‘leak’ and copping a three-year ban “Anyway, we’ll take the win. We’re relieved, and we’re happy to get the win. I think she deserved it.” Melham pleaded guilty to a stewards charge of failing to ride his mount out to the end of the race and was fined $2000. In an interesting twist, the rider of the runner-up, Western Australian jockey Austin Galati, was also fined $1000 by stewards for failing to ride his mount out to the end of the race.



There were no such heart-in-mouth moments for Leek as she took out the feature race of the day, the group 1 Turnbull Stakes, with Perth gelding Cosmic Crusader. The comfortable victory on a heavy track provided a welcome respite six weeks after her husband, John Leek jnr, was disqualified from the sport for three years for attempting to stomach tube a horse. View post on X The victory also vindicated a decision by big-time Perth owner Bob Peters to send Cosmic Crusader across the Nullarbor to be prepared by Leek at her Nar Nar Goon North base for a shot at the spring riches. “I think I’ve been lucky to have this focus,” Leek said on Saturday after her first group 1 win.



“It’s been tough on the family and I have just focused on my horses and that is what has got me through.” While Leek waits for Racing Victoria to hear an application for her husband to be allowed to move back to their family home – currently disallowed under the rules of racing because she is a trainer – Cosmic Crusader is sure to provide some welcome distractions. Jockey Willie Pike and trainer Andrea Leek were congratulated by owner Bob Peters (right) after Cosmic Crusader’s win. Getty Images After comfortably beating rivals Light Infantry Man (second), Aeliana (third) and pre-race favourite Sir Delius (fourth), the six-year-old gelding has emerged as a key chance in the Cox Plate, to be raced at Flemington in three weeks’ time. “He’s a tricky horse, but I sent a message to Bob this morning, ‘There’s no excuses today, he’s spot on’, and thank God I was right,” Leek said.



“I galloped him one morning at Pakenham, and it was about a heavy 15. The tracks were closed, and they were good enough to let us work him because he was going into one of his previous races. “He went across the top of it like it was a good track. I was pretty confident he would handle the wet.” View post on X The win was also vindication for Perth jockey Willie Pike, who copped criticism from several form experts last month for his ride on the horse – finishing third in the group 1 Memsie Stakes at Caulfield. At the time, Pike did not like what he heard, firing back at his detractors and telling them to mind their own business. He was more considerate after winning the Turnbull Stakes.



“First of all, thank you to Mr Peters and his family,” Pike said. “They were backing me from the get-go even when I put in a bit of an iffy one a couple of starts ago. Jamie Melham aboard Half Yours at Flemington. Getty Images “It is really nice to get the job done. He was putting in those good runs without getting the job done, so I really like to get it done for him.” While last year’s Cups hero Half Yours finished solidly in fifth, jockey Jamie Melham was suspended for 10 race meetings for careless riding and will miss next week’s Caulfield Guineas meeting. She will return in time to defend her Caulfield Cup crown on Half Yours. It was another bountiful day for the Ciaron Maher mega stable, which took out feature staying races in Sydney and Melbourne – Mr Monaco won the 2500m The Bart Cummings at Flemington, while Juja Kibo won the 2400m Metropolitan at Randwick.



The victory means Mr Monaco wins a golden ticket into the Melbourne Cup, and Maher was full of praise for young Tasmanian jockey Jabez Johnstone. “It’s exciting to get another one into the Cup, but Jabez, he’s a little ripper,” Maher said. “I get on with him quite well. He’s usually a man of few words and I don’t mind that either. It was a good positive ride, and he’s strong.” News, results and expert analysis from the weekend of sport sent every Monday.

World.title: Tempted destroys Premiere rivals to issue warning to world’s best
World.content:
SportRacingHorse racing Tempted destroys Premiere rivals to issue warning to world’s best Craig Kerry October 3, 2026 — 6:31pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Tempted ensured she will be wearing Godolphin’s colours again in the $20 million Everest with another stunning win on Saturday and her team believe there is more to come when she steps up against Ka Ying Rising again. A $1.60 favourite after an easy win in the Concorde Stakes (1000m), the four-year-old mare was even more impressive in the Premiere Stakes (1200m) on Saturday, storming to a three-length victory over the top of Savvy Hallie in the final Everest lead-in. Tempted toys with her rivals in the Premiere Stakes. Getty Images Tempted was runner-up last year to Ka Ying Rising and looms as the main challenger again to the Hong Kong superstar on October 17. Godolphin Australia racing and bloodstock manager Jason Walsh said she would be racing in the powerhouse operation’s slot again.



“They are easy to watch like that,” Walsh said. “She’s a special mare, there’s no doubt about that. It was lovely to see her do it that way. “She’ll carry our colours and, as she did last year, when she carried them so well, and it’s pretty clear she’s in even better form, so we look forward to contesting the title again. “She did last year, and she’s furnished mentally and physically this time. She’s getting close to the finished article and she’ll definitely make her presence felt in a couple of weeks.” Trainer Ciaron Maher’s NSW assistant, Johann Gerard-Dubord, said Ka Ying Rising will need to be at his best to hold out Tempted.



“It’s a very good field, and she made them look like they’re nothing special, but it’s a genuine group one field,” Gerard-Dubord said. “The way she quickens, which is her best asset, she is one of a kind. Everything she does is very special. “She’ll have to be very special in two weeks, but we’ll be spot on for that. Ka Ying at his best, he’s very hard to beat, but he’ll have to be at his best. “Every horse is beatable on a day, and there’s more there. She quickens very well, but every time she gets to the front, she still waits for them, so if she’s got something to chase for a bit longer, I think there’s a bit more there.” Earlier, Inglis announced Stradbroke Handicap winner Spicy Martini as its Everest runner about the same time it emerged Golden Slipper winner Guest House was out for the spring.



Guest House was in line to fill the Everest slot of Coolmore, which paid about $30 million for the Home Affairs colt, but trainers Mick Price and Michael Kent jnr revealed the three-year-old had sustained a soft tissue injury to its near hind leg at trackwork on Saturday morning and would be spelled. Related Article Horse racing Sargent sticks solid with Gibbons for drought-breaking group 1 Inglis had already locked in Spicy Martini and announced the news at 1pm. An $8000 Inglis Digital buy for trainer Toby Edmonds and his partner Holly Penfold in March 2023 as a yearling, the five-year-old mare has won six times in just 13 starts and earned more than $2.7 million. She was beaten three-quarters of a length last start when fourth first-up in The Shorts (1100m) at Randwick two weeks ago. Regular jockey Taylor Marshall will keep ride, rounding off the all-Queensland team. Spicy Martini was $51 for the Everest before the announcement. “We have had an eye on her for some time and believe she is capable of posting a career-best effort in The Everest,” Inglis Bloodstock CEO Sebastian Hutch said. “She has run a new peak figure each start this year – including a group 1 victory in the Stradbroke - which tells us she is headed on an upward trajectory.”

World.title: Ten people injured, P-plater arrested after car crashes into Newcastle Knights fans
World.content:
A five-year-old girl was left fighting for her life and nine others were injured when a teenage P-plate driver allegedly lost control of his car and careered into jubilant crowds lining a Newcastle street to wave the Knights off to the NRL grand final. One of the injured, Chris Clancy, said the car appeared to speed up as it went through a roundabout, and then lost control on the wet road. “No-one had time to move,” he said. “I thought I was going to die, it happened so fast.” Fans at the crash site rushed to provide first aid as emergency crews rushed to the scene and word of the collision spread through the tens of thousands of excited fans waiting for a glimpse of their team. The team’s bus, which had not yet departed when the crash occurred, was rerouted, and players were informed. Loading “They were shocked, it was a very sombre bus ride,” said one of those aboard. “Our fans mean everything to us. For that to happen; horrible.”



The five-year-old girl was in a critical condition in John Hunter Hospital on Saturday evening. One patient was in a serious but stable condition, and five were stable. Three had been discharged. Police arrested the 18-year-old driver at the crash site and took him for mandatory drug and alcohol testing. They said the incident was not believed to be targeted or terror-related. The teen was known to them. NSW Police Assistant Commissioner David Waddell said officers were investigating reports the P-plater had been “driving erratically” before he lost control of the vehicle. Footage posted to social media depicted the BMW careering around the roundabout moments before the crash, as shocked onlookers were heard screaming. The driver is expected to be charged, but no charges had been laid at the time of publication. The crash scene. TNV



Scenes at Wallsend, Newcastle, after a car crashed into a crowd of Knights supporters. Onlookers expressed anger towards the occupants of the car after the crash, police said. “We had to get the three of them out of there because the crowd did turn on them,” Waddell said. Witness Dean Liddell said he could hear the vehicle coming towards the crowd and then “all hell broke loose”. “I watched the little girl get dragged underneath the car. Seeing the whole scene unfold, it took me 10 minutes until I could say anything to anyone,” Liddell said. He said the crowd grabbed the driver from the wreck and a scuffle began before police intervened.



“If the copper wasn’t there the driver would have had massive injuries as well,” he said. The accident came after a joyous week in Newcastle, where the city threw its support behind a team that has not won a premiership for 25 years. The Knights had been expected to be inspired by the joy of their supporters during the grand final, but will now also feel the weight of the tragedy when they take the field. Newcastle Knights captain Kalyn Ponga said on social media that players “hearts are with everyone affected” by the crash. “We’re thinking of you, your families and everyone in our Newcastle community.” Longtime league watchers say no other grand final has been played under such a shadow. “It’s heartbreaking for the whole rugby league community, not just in Newcastle,” said Brad Fittler, a former Roosters captain and a member of the league hall of fame. “We’ve never seen anything like this ahead of a grand final and it puts everything in perspective.”



Australian Rugby League Commission executive chairman Peter V’Landys said he was deeply saddened by the crash. When asked whether it would affect plans for Sunday night’s game, he said “we’re just concerned about the victims at the moment.” Paramedics prepare to transport the injured by helicopter. Sitthixay Ditthavong The Premier Chris Minns said it was heartbreaking to see fans who were sending off their grand final team involved in such a terrible incident. “My thoughts are with the families and friends of loved ones who have been involved or injured in the crash. I also want to thank emergency services including police and ambulance who are responding to this tragedy”, the premier said. “We’ve seen how this grand final has brought the Newcastle together, and I hope the whole community remains united as we continue to respond.”



Newcastle Lord Mayor Gavin Morris said that, before Saturday’s crash, the lead-up to the grand final had been one of the “most incredibly joyous weeks in our city”. “It’s a tragedy. It’s something that we can’t take back,” Morris said. Morris said that passing vehicles were “revving up the crowd” as they drove past thousands of Knights fans lining the roadside before the crash. “That just should not have been occurring, but it has,” he said.



Asked whether bollards or fencing should have been installed at the roadside to protect fans, Morris said securing the 20-kilometre stretch of road between the Knight’s home ground and the crash site was “almost an impossible task”. The injured Clancy said a police vehicle was stationed near the crash site, and responded quickly. He said the car came at the group of supporters too fast for them to jump out of the way. He was hit by the front of the vehicle. Knights fan Jed Partridge, 29, who arrived at 8.20am to join thousands of others in waving off the team bus, was among fans who watched the celebration turn to shock. “We were on the side of the road, just waiting. Everyone was happy and then there was a real flurry of cop cars, ambos and rescue cars shooting past.” He said word soon filtered out that there had been a serious crash. “It was eerie … such a positive thing could quickly turn to this. It’s hard to wrap your head around.” Fans urged the Knights to press forward and do their best on Sunday night. “It will be tough for them, but do what they’ve always done and do it for the town,” said Clancy. “I believe they can win. Regardless of whether they win or lose, they’ve done the town proud.”

World.title: Cost of fixing storm-damaged Whangārei roads balloons to more than $23m
World.content:
The cost of fixing storm damage inflicted on Whangārei district roads earlier this year has risen to more than $23 million - of which almost $11m has been spent clearing one giant landslide.

The almost week-long January storm cut off coastal settlements at Ōakura and Whangaruru, swept away a bridge approach, damaged dozens of homes and destroyed others, and triggered a huge number of slips on the coastal road between Whangārei and Russell.

One section of road at Helena Bay Hill was only re-opened on Friday, after an eight-month effort to remove almost 100,000 cubic metres of soil, boulders and trees.

Further storms in March and April added more damage.

A report prepared for Whangārei District Council said the initial estimate for repairing storm-damaged roads was $16.5m, but that had now increased to $23.2m.

The report, by transportation manager Greg Monteith, sought councillors' approval for the extra $6.7m.

The NZ Transport Agency was expected to contribute $16m, leaving Whangārei ratepayers to pick up the remaining $7.2m.

The $23.2m total included $10.9m for emergency works at the massive Helena Bay Hill slip on Russell Road, the main connection between Whangārei and coastal communities at Ōakura and Whangaruru.

Almost $11 million has been spent repairing Russell Road, in the Whangārei District, after a massive slip on 21 January. Supplied / Ngātiwai Trust Board

The council previously described the slip repair as one of the biggest and most complex projects it had ever undertaken.

About 93,000 cubic metres of soil, boulders and downed trees had to removed - reduced from the initial estimate of 110,000 cubic metres - and the 35m-high slip face had to be stabilised.

The cost of fixing the slip had previously been put at $7.5m.

The council would fund its share of the extra costs by borrowing, to avoid major delays or cuts to existing roading projects.

The report stated the original cost estimate for the Helena Bay Hill slip was based on a completion date of mid-2026.

Since then, however, persistent wet weather, difficult ground conditions, giant basalt boulders, fill site constraints and further slip movement had delayed work and increased costs.

Some boulders were so big, they could not be broken up, even with a 50-tonne breaker, and instead required blasting or a specialist rock-breaking crew.

The report stated there had also been delays due to health and safety issues, such as near-misses involving trucks and local residents, and unauthorised entry into exclusion areas.

Aerial view of the cleared slip on Russell Road’s Helena Bay Hill. Supplied / Whangārei District Council

Once the slip had settled, which was expected to take about a year, more funding would be needed to repair the road below the slip and along the 2km route to the clean-fill site.

The estimated road rehabilitation cost was $2.3m.

During the road closure, the Whangārei District Council operated a convoy, via steep, narrow and unsealed Kaiikanui Road, to allow continued access from the south.

Piloted convoys left every 35-40 minutes from 6.30am to 6.30pm, seven days a week.

The cost of operating the Kaiikanui Road detour was put at $2.1m.

According to claims recorded by the Insurance Council, the total nationwide cost of the January storm, was $75.9m.

More than 5000 claims were lodged including $54.5m for damage to homes, $13.7m to commercial property and $4.6m for vehicles.

According to the Insurance Council, the most costly event of the past decade in terms of insurance claims was the 2023 Anniversary Weekend storm, which totalled $1.98 billion nationwide.

World.title: Green Party announces plan for passenger rail between major NZ cities
World.content:
The Green Party says it will connect the country with intercity passenger rail services, if elected.

The party has announced plans to introduce an overnight rail service between Auckland and Wellington, passenger rail between Christchurch and Dunedin, and to extend the Te Huia train route to Tauranga.

"Where public transport has been invested in, it's well used, saving people time and money every day. But for a lot of New Zealand, public transport options remain expensive and infrequent, especially when travelling long distances," Green Party co-leader Marama Davidson said.

"We want to connect our cities and our country with alternative ways to travel that will save people money, connect our communities and give New Zealanders real transport choices."

"Aotearoa was once connected by a reliable passenger rail system, with fast, frequent services linking communities across the country. But the privatisation of the rail network led to the sale of our assets for private profit and was returned to the people in disarray.

"Now, our aging rail infrastructure is suffering from a generation of underinvestment, leaving the rail network in a state of decline with cancellations, delays and bus replacements.

"We should restore these systems so we can have an efficient, comfortable and affordable alternative to experience our country."

Green Party co-leaders Marama Davidson and Chlöe Swarbrick Tess Brunton / RNZ

Green Party transport spokesperson Julie Anne Genter said the tracks were already there, so should be used.

"Restoring commuter rail will give smaller regions and towns the benefits of more travellers stopping at their town stations, creating more economic opportunities and connecting them to main centres and other towns."

There were compelling reasons to back the services the party had set out, she said.

"The train journey from Auckland to Wellington is long, which makes it perfect for an overnight service. All that is needed is new, comfortable sleeper trains and operating funding.

"Extending Te Huia to Tauranga would connect one of NZ's fastest-growing regions. All it needs is some station, tunnel and track upgrades to give the region an affordable alternative to driving.

"With KiwiRail already undertaking significant work on the Christchurch to Dunedin track, extending it to passenger rail would only take building stations and some upgrades, making better use of existing rail infrastructure," she added.

Peters: 'Our job is to make sure it's viable'

New Zealand First leader Winston Peters was not opposed to the idea of a sleeper train between Auckland and Wellington.

Peters, who has been the Minister for Rail in the coalition government, said his party did not rule out any idea - it just made sure "we can stand it up practically first".

"There's nothing new about the idea, that's been around for over 100 years," he said.

Regional rail had operated in the past but had ended up shut down, he said.

"That's the point. Our job is to make sure it's viable.

"I'm not saying I'm opposed to supporting anything until I've done the work on it, done the analysis, because the Greens will announce 1000 announcements, but as for the business case, they wouldn't know what the expression means."

Rail was run down when he came back into office in 2023, he said.

"We turned this around for the second time.

"But at least we've got an acceptance in the business community at last that rail is critical for our future."

Luxon says proposal won't work

National leader Christopher Luxon did not want taxpayer funding going into a "white elephant" that was not commercially viable.

"Where it makes sense that's really good but you need a concentration of population to make passenger rail work.

"Of course we're very committed to our 17 roads of national significance and we make no apology for that."

World.title: Sir Sam Neill's legacy lives on in Two Paddocks' next harverst
World.content: "Sam bought it and he kept a whole lot of those botanicals and did a whole lot of planting himself, lots of shelter belts. World.title: Mystery man a 'hero' after saving 89-year-old from burning home
World.content:
A mystery man has been hailed as a "hero", after he entered a burning building to save an 89-year-old from a housefire in Gisborne.

The fire on Aberdeen Road was reported to emergency services about 1am Saturday.

Detective Senior Sergeant John Love said police understood the man was driving past the burning home, saw the fire and pulled over.

"He then entered the burning building and pulled the occupant to safety through a window.

"However, he left the scene, before emergency services were able to speak with him."

Love said police were now looking for the man to thank him for "his quick thinking and courageous actions".

The occupant of the burning home was taken to hospital for further assessment and observation.

Love encouraged anyone with information that could help identify the man to contact Police on 105, quoting file number P067820889.

World.title: Tragic deaths mourned by Auckland councillors
World.content:
Auckland councillors are lamenting after several tragic deaths this week.

A 33-year-old man has been charged with murder after a man died on a residential street in Glen Innes on Thursday afternoon.

Three family members were also found dead at a Papatoetoe home on Thursday evening.

Manukau Ward Councillor Lotu Fuli said one of the victims, a man found on the front porch of the home, had young children.

"It's a man who is well-known in the community and helps out in the community.

"What I've heard from our community and people who live nearby is that it has come as a complete surprise to their neighbours and everybody who knew the family. The family is a quiet family. Everyone is quite shocked because of that."

RNZ / Felix Walton

Fuli believed the victims' extended family were being supported.

She said there was no threat to the wider community and people should still feel safe.

"I know there's a bit of uncertainty out there, but as far as we're aware, there's no ongoing threat and no wider issue for our Papatoetoe community and neighbourhood.

"Hopefully people are feeling okay, and for those neighbours who did see what happened and are experiencing grief and loss, I hope they are able to get some help, some counselling, to help them through it as well. I know it will be a very difficult time for everybody involved."

RNZ / Felix Walton

Fellow Manukau Councillor Alf Filipaina said he planned to pay his respects when possible.

"I've heard that they [the victims] are community people and well liked in the community."

The former police officer said his thoughts were with the families, first responders, and communities affected by both tragedies this week.

"I know what impact it has when you see something of that nature. Please seek professional advice to get you through. I've found that if you take that offer and take it early, it helps you process what you've seen.

"My plea to the community is to stay strong and stand together."

'Huge effects' on the workforce

Police Association President Steve Watt said police around the country dealt with four suspected homicides in one week - with investigations also underway in

Buller and Christchurch.

Video player removed for printing https://players.brightcove.net/6093072280001/default_default/index.html?videoId=6406082423112

He said that would put the workforce under pressure.

"Homicides are extremely intensive and resource driven operations and there's no doubt that having multiple homicides at the same time will draw on a number of police investigations in order to deal with it."

Watt said the investigations had "huge effects" on the workforce, who were driven to get a result and deliver justice for family members and friends.
